News.title: Moment teen yells ‘help’ as he’s dragged along on roof of car after driver tried to escape hit-and-run crash
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a flailing teenager yells “help” as he is dragged across a car roof while the driver flees a hit-and-run.

Dashcam footage shows a VW Passat speeding around a corner with a young man hanging on from the rooftop as he begs to be rescued.



The reckless driver left a man with life-changing injuries before dragging the teenager after a road rage row, cops have said.

Greater Manchester Police were called to Salford at around 5.40pm yesterday afternoon after receiving reports of a hit-and-run following a collision.



Two men reportedly got out of the car to confront the other driver after the crash.

But the driver then sped away, hitting a man in his 50s who was rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries.



An 18-year-old was dragged across the roof of the car as the driver tried to make a getaway.

The teen was taken to hospital with non-life threatening injuries.

The vehicle eventually stopped on Camp Street and the driver, in his 50s, was arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm with intent.

He remained in police custody this morning for questioning.



An onlooker, who captured the shocking incident, said: “I was on my way home, and it was gridlock traffic – I thought, what was going on?

“This car zoomed round the corner with a man on his roof.

“I was very shocked. It was like something out of a movie.

“The guy was shouting for help, but nobody was able to help him as the car was moving at speed.”

A spokesperson for the police said: “Investigations are ongoing at this stage.



“Officers are appealing for anyone who may have witnessed the incident or has any CCTV, dashcam or mobile phone footage from the area to please come forward.”

It follows another hit-and-run near Edinburgh Airport on August 7.

Tributes flooded in for Linda Patterson, 58, who was tragically killed in a catastrophic crash on the A8 in Newbridge.

News.title: Horrifying moment girl, 2, playing with sister is crushed to death by car as mum chatted to pal nearby
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a toddler is crushed to death by a car as the young girl played with her sister just feet away from their mum.

Heartbreaking footage shows two-year-old Adrija crouching by the road as her mum chatted away to a friend when a car turns the corner and veers towards the girl.



The car sharply turned around the bend as Adrija disappeared beneath the vehicle.

The mother immediately rushed over but the toddler was unresponsive.



Adrija was rushed to hospital but was pronounced dead as she arrived.

The tragedy occurred outside the family’s home in Gurugram, northern India, near Delhi, at around 9pm on September 7.

According to Adrija’s father, Virendra Tiwari, the driver had passed the exact same spot just five minutes before the fatal collision, narrowly missing the girls when his wife pulled them to safety.

He said: “He knew there were children at the turning, but even then he was speeding when he crossed the spot for the second time.”



Following the collision, the driver stopped and tried to help, according to Virendra.

He was later arrested and the car was seized by police.

Gurugram Police spokesman Sandeep Turan said the unnamed 30-year-old suspect works for a private company.

Officers registered a case against him for causing death by negligence and rash driving at Sector 5 police station on September 8.

Police said the driver told investigators that he had not seen the children in the road because it was dark.



The family are originally from Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh and had been living in Gurugram for several years.

Police have launched an investigation into the tragic incident.

It comes as two children from the same family were killed on their way to school in a horror car crash near Melbourne, Australia.

Sarah El Hawli, seven, died at the scene as Ossama El Hawli, 11, was rushed hospital but later tragically died.

A 34-year-old female driver and the seven children were inside the car when it flipped and “inexplicably rolled” near Bacchus Marsh on Tuesday.

Five others were injured in the crash.

Major Collision Investigation Unit detectives are investigating the circumstances behind the fatal crash.

News.title: At least 24 children feared dead after fire ripped through school sparking stampede as 300 buildings destroyed by flames
News.content:
AT LEAST 24 children are feared to be dead after a huge fire ripped through two schools and triggered a deadly stampede.

More than 300 buildings have been destroyed as terrified teachers and pupils fled the inferno in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.



Two primary schools were engulfed in flames at around 8am in the densely populated Kadutu commune.

Dramatic photos show furious fires spewing thick plumes of choking smoke as hundreds of homes are transformed into a scorched wasteland.



The horror blaze sparked a “violent stampede” according to local leader Patrice Buduge.

He added the deadly rush “forced students to trample over one another or look for a dangerous way out; many of them fainted and others lost consciousness”.

Local authorities confirmed that “some of the students died in a stampede while trying to flee the flames”.

Survivors with burns and smoke inhalation have been rushed to nearby hospitals – with some in critical condition.



At least 14 children – all under the age of ten – have been killed, according to Christophe Zigashane, a nurse at a local clinic.

He said: “We received around 50 students, including several teachers, in a critical state of asphyxia.

“Among them, 10 were dead and four others died at the scene. That makes a total of 14 deaths, all under 10 years old.”



The fire reportedly started at a neighbouring building before rapidly spreading onto the schools and setting them alight, reported AA.

Emergency services raced to Ujamaa and Furaha primary schools – with firefighters battling to extinguish the flames.

Authorities warn that the death toll is set to rise as rescue teams search through the scorched wreckage.

Police have launched a probe into the monster blaze.

Congo’s government said on X: “The Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship expressed deep sorrow over the deadly fire.”



It added that the death toll remained “provisional” while vowing to conduct checks of the burnt down schools.

It follows just days after a deadly fire ripped through a wedding banquet in the Congo’s capital, killing 22.

The horror blaze sparked a stampede – with many guests struggling to flee through the venue’s narrow corridors.

Harrowing photos show the blackened insides of the venue littered with the metal frames of burnt out chairs and scorched wedding decor.

News.title: Remembering Charlie Kirk’s haunting last words about gun violence seconds before his assassination at 31
News.content:
MOMENTS before a bullet pierced Charlie Kirk in the neck in a harrowing scene, the conservative political activist was fielding questions from a student about gun violence in the United States.

Kirk, 31, was revered for touring college campuses across the nation, hosting in-person debates with students and challenging them about the current state of affairs impacting American society.



On September 10, 2025, Kirk was on stage at Utah Valley University in Orem, about 40 minutes south of Salt Lake City, as part of his organization Turning Point USA’s The American Comeback Tour.

About 20 minutes into the start of the event, Kirk was asked a question about the number of mass shooters there have been in America over the last decade.



Kirk responded, “Counting or not counting gang violence?”

Seconds later, a single shot rang out, striking Kirk in the neck as he uttered his last word.



Thousands were in attendance to witness the harrowing shooting as blood was seen gushing from Kirk’s neck as he fell off his chair.

Video captured bystanders screaming, “Get down! Get down!”

Kirk was rushed to the hospital in critical condition and was pronounced dead hours later.

Prosecutors have accused Tyler Robinson, 23, of shooting Kirk from the roof of a nearby campus building.



The large-scale manhunt in Utah ended less than 33 hours after Kirk’s shooting when Robinson voluntarily surrendered at the Washington County Sheriff’s Office.

Robinson’s relatives told police that sometime before he allegedly carried out the shooting, he spoke about his dislike for Kirk during a family dinner, Utah Governor Spencer Cox said.

He allegedly criticized Kirk for his hateful views.

The family members also said Robinson had become more political in the years leading up to Kirk’s shooting.

Robinson will stand trial for Kirk’s shooting following a five-day evidentiary hearing to determine whether the prosecution had gathered enough evidence to try the suspect.



He has pleaded not guilty on all counts, including aggravated murder, felony discharge of a firearm causing serious bodily injury, obstruction of justice, tampering with a witness, and violent offense committed in the presence of a child.

Prosecutors said they plan to seek the death penalty, if Robinson is convicted.

During the hearing, David Hull, a former State Bureau of Investigation agent, laid out Robinson’s alleged movements in the moments leading up to the shooting.



Hull testified that Robinson arrived at the campus hours before Kirk was scheduled to take the stage.

He allegedly purchased a meal from a campus Chick-fil-A restaurant, and made contact with representatives at Turning Point USA.

Robinson then changed outfits and posted up on the rooftop overlooking the amphitheater where Kirk was speaking.

Surveillance footage showed in court allegedly showed Robinson crouching on the rooftop, then, after the shot rang out and hit Kirk, the suspect was seen sprinting across the roof.

Robinson then dropped to the ground level and fled the scene on foot, Hull added.

He is due back in court on October 23 for a status hearing.

Watch The U.S. Sun‘s interview with Fox host Will Cain about the moment he announced Kirk’s death live on the air.

News.title: Moment driver pulled over by cops after being caught ‘buttering bagel while driving with his knees’ in heavy traffic
News.content:
THIS is the wild moment a man is busted by cops after allegedly buttering a bagel while driving with his knees.

The snacking suspect, 29, had reportedly been readying to tuck into the bread roll while in heavy traffic through Toowoomba, Australia.



Police said they stopped the man, from Queensland, after spotting him around 3.50pm on Monday steering his car – with his knees.

Dramatic body-worn footage shows an officer confronting the silver Honda driver along Tor Street in Newtown.



The baffled cop asked: “Can you explain for me why, in four lines of traffic, that are quite busy at this time of day, that you thought steering a motor vehicle on your P’s, with your knees, while you buttered a bagel, would be a great idea?”

The man, who was on a provisional licence, immediately confessed to the bagel blunder.

He said: “I know that was stupid, but I was hungry.”

“[I] Have been working since this morning“, he added.

But buttering his bagel was not the only driving mishap allegedly being committed by the 29-year-old.

The police officer pointed out that he had also been driving an unregistered car.



“I can’t understand how you thought that would be a great idea in all that traffic”, the officer said.

Body-worn footage from the cop also revealed that the man had been driving on a provisional licence.

He has now been slapped with a £585 (AUS$ 1,104) fine and three demerit points on his licence.



Darling Downs District Officer Acting Superintendent Kelly Hanlen said: “Taking your hands and focus away from the task of driving, even for something as seemingly harmless like preparing food, can have serious consequences.

“There is no meal, message or other distraction worth risking your safety or the safety of other road users.

“If you’re driving, keep your attention on the road and your hands where they belong: on the wheel.”

Elsewhere in Australia shocking footage shows the moment a car mechanic clings to a moving Mercedes in a row over “unpaid work”.

The chaos unfolded after the Mercedes driver allegedly refused to cough up the thousands of pounds due for costly repairs to the car.

Dramatic footage shows the mechanic shouting “stop idiot!” as the suspected swindler tries to reverse and speed away.

Another woman join the fray, banging on the car window and shouting: “Stop the f***ing car, who’s car is this?”.

News.title: Dad of A66 Middlesbrough crash victim charged with assaulting mourner & obstructing police at own son’s funeral
News.content:
THE dad of one of the A66 yobs who crashed into a police car killing two officers has been charged with attacking a mourner at his son’s funeral.

The ceremony for Cole Worthy, 17, was reduced to chaos when his father Gye, 39, allegedly took exception to comments made during the service.



He is accused of assaulting a mourner and of obstructing police who were called to deal with the disturbance.

A source close to the family said that Worthy’s mother Natalie McConnell was left “devastated and shocked” by the disruption at her son’s funeral at Teesside Crematorium on Wednesday.



The couple separated a number of years ago and both have new partners.

A spokesman for Cleveland Police said Gye Worthy will face court next month.



The force said: “The 39-year-old man arrested yesterday at Teesside Crematorium, following a disturbance during a service, has now been charged with common assault, public order and obstructing police.

“He is due to appear before Teesside Magistrates’ Court on 2nd October.”



Sarah Moloney, a friend of Ms McConnell, thanked mourners for their attendance on her behalf.

In a social media post she said: “To everyone who came today for our Coley, thank you from the very bottom of our hearts.

“Seeing so many faces who loved him cared for him and held him close means more than we can ever put into words, your presence your hugs your kind words and every beautiful memory you shared.

“Cole was so loved and today showed us just how far that love reached.

Thank you for walking this hard day with us, thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being here for us

“He will live on in all our hearts forever. Rest peacefully our beautiful Coley, we love you more than anything.”



Gye Worthy, of Acklam, Middlesbrough, works as an offshore deck foreman and is the boss of his own specialist lifting company which operates on offshore platforms.

His semi-detached £200,000 home was rammed on August 22 shortly before his son was killed four pals and two police officers, PC Matthew Blades, 37 and PC Tom Clough, 38.

Police said the five all had links to organised crime and had been trying to flee police when they drove the wrong way up the A66 into the police vehicle.



The incident was blamed on a tit for tat gangland turf war over the supply of drugs on Teesside.

The family announcement for Mr Worthy’s memorial read: “In loving memory of Cole, our beautiful boy taken from us on 22nd August 2022.

“An adored son, brother, grandson, nephew, cousin. A loving boyfriend to Ruby and a cherished friend to many. Fly high Cole, forever 17.”

The funeral was on the same day as that of PC Blades which took place in Hartlepool.

Hundreds of cops lined the streets in an emotional farewell to the “superhero”.



Heartbroken colleagues wiped tears from their eyes as his coffin – draped in the Union flag – was carried into a packed church.

His colleague PC Clough was honoured in a separate service on Thursday.

Before he joined Cleveland police he served in Iraq and Afghanistan in a bomb disposal unit and then joined British Transport Police and the Civil Nuclear Police.

Colleagues revealed that PC Clough used to joke that no-one would turn up to his funeral but hundreds proved him wrong today.

Schools closed early for the previous funerals of some of the other young men who died, sparking a political row, but they remained open during the ceremony for Mr Worthy.



The five young men in the Passat were Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jakub Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

On Monday, teens were seen hanging from car windows as they gathered for the funeral of Theo Rae, a close friend of Mr Worthy.

An extra 200 specialist officers, including armed cops, were deployed to Middlesbrough from six other northern forces as the police tried to keep a lid on the escalating violence.

News.title: Wild moment car mechanic clings to Mercedes boot as driver reverses in row over ‘unpaid work worth thousands’
News.content:
THIS is the wild moment a car mechanic clings to a moving car after an argument over “unpaid work” in Melbourne.

Dramatic footage captures a tense showdown between a driver, a mechanic, and bystanders after a Mercedes C63 owner allegedly refused to pay for repairs.



A mechanic can be seen blocking the car, shouting “stop idiot” as the driver attempts to reverse and speed away.

As the vehicle continues to reverse into the man, a woman sees the crazy moment and tries to intervene.



She bangs on the window, yanks on the handle and shouts “stop the f**king car, who’s car is this?”

Another man also attempts to help but their efforts are useless.

The Mercedes reverses backwards with a roaring engine as the mechanic clings to the boot screaming “he took my money…I’m gonna kill you man, stop the car”.

The terrifying ordeal escalated further when the car speeds towards the parking lot exit with the mechanic still clutching on to the back.

Horrified onlookers shout “call the police” fearing the situation might take a dark turn.

Shockingly the driver continues reversing wildly into oncoming traffic with the mechanic still holding on.



The mechanic finally lets go and the driver bombs it down the wrong side of the road, escaping the furious workers.

A worker claimed on Facebook that the ordeal started because the Mercedes allegedly drove off without paying, and with a car scanner tool, according to Nine News.

The mechanic clinging to the boot, believed to be the owner of Noble Park mechanics, claimed the driver had been trying to flee without paying for thousands of dollars worth of work.



His workers claim that the two men had been disputing the unpaid fees which led to the events of the video.

Victoria Police officers were called to the car park on Cheltenham Road around 5.30pm on Wednesday.

They said: “During the dispute, it is alleged a 48-year-old Keysborough man clung onto the boot of a moving Mercedes-Benz for a short distance,

“The man was not injured and the vehicle fled prior to police arrival.”

The mechanic’s brother said that they were a small business and the whole situation was “ridiculous”.



He said: “Especially on an AMG, his car is worth I think around $80,000, he should have $1000 to pay for it.”

Another fight allegedly occurred on Thursday morning when the driver’s parents tried to settle the dispute.

A worker said: “There was an argument, we’re not paying for this, we’ll just pay for that, and that’s when the trouble started.”

Police confirmed they had responded to reports of an unlawful assault at a Noble Park business.

“It is alleged a 48-year-old Keysborough man was assaulted at the premises on Tower Park Drive about 11.30am. He sustained minor injuries,” police said.



Another 48-year-old man, from Epping, was interviewed and released pending summons, police said.

The alleged driver of the Mercedes-Benz, a 20-year-old man from Campbellfield, presented himself to a police station the following day.

Police said: “He was interviewed and is expected to be charged on summons with traffic offences including reckless conduct endangering life, reckless conduct endangering serious injury and drive in a manner dangerous.”



Police are still investigating.

The viral video, which was initially posted by Aus Street Rides, has shocked viewers and stirred up an online debate.

“This is crazy. I just want to know how much he was supposed to pay … he was reversing to Timbuktu,” one comment said.

“Mad respect for the bloke in the ute,” another person added.

A third said: “Sad people do this but not worth risking your life for.”

News.title: Why Iran’s new missile is a bluff – but ‘invincible’ nuclear Pickaxe Mountain is Trump’s ultimate target to end regime
News.content:
IRAN’S new electro-optical missiles are a bluff – but the regime’s doomsday Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site is the number one target in Donald Trump’s crosshairs.

Chilling satellite pictures revealed an unprecedented building “surge” at the facility where Tehran is feared to be creating an impenetrable atomic plant under 300ft of solid granite.



Trump has fired off a warning – threatening to strike the base if Iran continues to fast-track its nuclear bomb aims there.

Experts from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) said satellites had revealed more activity at Pickaxe Mountain in 2026 “than at any point in the site’s history”.



Their analysis showed how construction speed shot up over the last year and that Tehran had thrown up a new ring of steel around the fortress.

Brit ex-Army commander Hamish de Bretton-Gordon said Pickaxe Mountain “has always been really the focus and the centre of a lot of the Iranians’ nuclear program”.

He told The Sun: “There is a lot of activity and work going on at Pickaxe Mountain… that seems to be the basis for his war with Iran.

“If he [Trump] thinks that they are continuing to develop their nuclear program at Pickaxe Mountain… then it would seem logical from what Trump has done so far for the US to attack Pickaxe Mountain again.”



The US president – who has vowed Iran must never have nukes – is now believed to be mulling the biggest bunker buster strikes ever launched to wipe out the huge threat.

Trump – whose war with the regime is escalating again – told the midterm Republican convention: “We notice there’s a little activity at ‌Pickaxe.

“I would advise Iran not to get cute because we will have to hit them very hard.”



The recent construction boom is an attempt to transform the site into a safe space for Iran’s elusive nuclear program, CSIS believes.

Trump also threatened to blitz Pickaxe Mountain “very soon” last week and has hinted at attacking the facility numerous times over recent months.

He said on Friday: “We may hit Pickaxe Mountain very soon… if there is anything going on with Pickaxe.”

Israel believes Iran has moved thousands of uranium-enrichment centrifuges into tunnels deep inside Pickaxe Mountain.

It is a heavily fortified site that hosts two deeply buried tunnel complexes.



Known in Farsi as Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La, the facility is situated just 2km south of the Natanz uranium enrichment plant.

The regime is believed to have made the transfer after the 12-day war in June 2025, when US and Israeli strikes pummelled Iran’s three main nuclear sites.

Different satellite images previously revealed tunnels feeding into the mountain leading to a deep-buried operation.

Experts say it could be more secure than any of the facilities struck by the US and Israel before.

Pickaxe Mountain could prove difficult to strike because of how deep the facility is buried as well as the tough granite surrounding it.



De Bretton-Gordon added: “We know that the laboratories where they intend to enrich uranium, where they intend to build their bombs are very, very deep underground.

“If you have these sort of factories that are hewn into rock hundreds of feet below the surface, even the most powerful bunker buster bomb is probably not capable of getting down there.”

Trump has previously left the site untouched while bombing Iran’s other major nuclear bunkers.

But the US is said to be developing a successor to the GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator – used in Operation Midnight Hammer last year – to hit even deeper targets.

The GBU-57 can penetrate up to 200ft underground before exploding – just out of reach of Pickaxe Mountain’s base.



CSIS analysis revealed that despite the explosion in construction efforts, the site is still “not yet capable of enrichment”.

Tehran also continued work at Pickaxe Mountain during the temporary ceasefire this summer, according to the think tank.

This was against the terms of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).

They said: “CSIS imagery analysis confirms that construction activity continued at a high rate during the period covered by the MoU.”

It comes as tit-for-tat strikes escalated in recent days as Washington and Tehran blitzed several targets in the region.



The regime reportedly used electro-optical missiles for the first time in the war.

Iran said it used them to strike two US warships and eight oil tankers on Wednesday, as well as a military base in Jordan, according to The Telegraph.

The air assaults came in response to Washington blitzing five Iranian oil tankers, according to Tehran.

But de Bretton-Gordon said the electro-optical missiles were nothing to write home about.

He said: “There’s nothing terribly new about electro-optical sort of guidance… it’s almost sort of yesterday’s game.”



“Iran is sort of trumpeting it as the latest thing sort of since sliced bread, which it’s not really.”

Trump also said on Wednesday the war would come to a close after midterm elections in November, a prospect de Bretton-Gordon agreed was likely.

But the military expert warned the conflict could blow out of proportion unexpectedly because of the two unpredictable sides.

He said: “When you have the Supreme Leader of Iran and President Trump as the two antagonists, it’s very, very difficult to predict the future.

“It would seem that Iran has no desire to end this war in a hurry because they’re an autonomous regime, autocratic regime who don’t really care what’s happening to their people.”

News.title: Bromley London stabbing live: Seven arrested after four men stabbed with one critical
News.content:
Seven arrested after four stabbed in Bromley High Street

Seven men have been arrested after four men were stabbed in an altercation on Bromley High Street, with one victim in a critical condition.

Bromley London stabbing live: Seven arrested after four men stabbed with one critical

Seven men have been arrested after four men were stabbed during an altercation on Bromley High Street.

Police were called at around 2.15pm today, September 10, and attended alongside London Ambulance Service and London’s Air Ambulance.

Officers found four men with stab wounds. Three were taken to hospital with injuries described as non-life-threatening, while one man is in a critical condition.

All seven arrested men remain in custody as police enquiries continue. Officers said there is not believed to be any wider threat to the public.

A spokesperson for the London Ambulance Service said: "We were called at 2:19pm today (10 September) to reports of a stabbing on Bromley High Street, BR1.

“We sent ambulance crews, a paramedic in a fast response car, an incident response officer and an advanced paramedic. We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.

“We treated four patients at the scene and took them all to hospital”.

News.title: Jack Whitehall lifts lid on 'rogue' relative banned from his £250k wedding
News.content:
Tying the knot with model and actress Roxy Horner at Wiltshire’s 17th century Euridge Manor estate in April, at a cost of £250,000, the cheeky Brit Awards host admits his humour made guests blush. Wearing a bespoke Tom Ford suit, while Roxy, 35, had two couture Galia Lahav gowns at £16,000 each for her big day, Jack referenced having daughter Elsie, two, “out of wedlock.” He says: “The joke stinks out the entire marquee.”

Claiming his wife, who is from Essex, was in the driving seat for the wedding planning, Jack - whose estimated worth is £11 million - continues: "We had a ridiculous wedding and it was so over the top. Roxy wanted invitations hand-drawn by a calligrapher and delivered by a peacock.

"I was like ‘what's wrong with a WhatsApp group?’ We had a nine tier wedding cake. I just wanted Colin the Caterpillar but she shot that down."

Speaking to fans at a Milton Keynes gig ahead of his 26-date Bad Influence UK tour, starting in January, Jack, 38, says he also banned a “rogue uncle” from his wedding. The funnyman, whose family home is in West London’s Notting Hill, says: "He is bat shit. He got banned from Ramsgate Wetherspoons.”

‌



View 5 Images Jack Whitehall and Roxy Horner's honeymoon as they kiss in Venice (Image: Instagram)

Despite poking fun at his humanist wedding, Jack says his life feels complete since marrying Roxy, who he met in 2020 during a trip to Australia.

Previously linked to actresses Gemma Chan and Kate Beckinsale, he adds: "Seeing Roxy become a mum and flourish, I have never been so sure that this is the person that I want to do life with. With my insecurities, being with Roxy and my daughter feels like breathing out."

Back in jokey mode, he adds: "I am a dad now. It is wild. My baby came early, really early... by about five years. The birth of my child has to be the most stressful and one of the most physically demanding things I have ever had to do. I had to sleep in a chair. It is amazing the resilience of the male body."

‌



But he admits: "It was obviously harder for my wife.” Joking aside, Elsie’s arrival had a massive impact. Jack says: “As soon as I saw my daughter it was undignified. I was crying like Rylan at judges’ houses on X Factor.”

View 5 Images Jack is a proud dad to daughter Elsie (Image: Instagram/jackwhitehall)

And he says fatherhood has made him a changed man. He says: "Having a baby has changed me. I thought it would be easy as I had my dad to go by, but he set the bar drastically low. It is a lot to get your head around.

"It is a big shift in your life. The biggest change is that there is another person in your world, another human being in your house. But having my daughter is the best thing that has happened to me in my entire life. I don't know what I would do without my nanny though."

‌



Jack’s 2027 arena tour, taking in cities including Newcastle, Manchester, Liverpool, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Cardiff and a giant gig at the O2 in London, will mean time apart from his family. And he admits that, as he approaches 40, he finds it harder to travel light. He says: "I am nearly 40. I am really struggling.

"It does not work for me being middle aged. I am the impish Peter Pan figure. I play students on television. I can't be middle aged. My body is trying to reverse the ageing process. It is much harder to age if you are a beta male. My wash bag these days is like a magician's trunk. It is full of potions, lotions, peptides, serums and beard mascara. I have a whole pharmacy in there now. I have a pill for everything."

View 5 Images Jack Whitehall and Michael Whitehall attend a photocall for 'Jack Whitehall: Travels with My Father' (Image: Getty Images Europe)

Obstinate when it comes to exercise, he adds: "I do cardio, but nobody cares that you run a 10K or a 5k. I don't want to join your running club or watch anyone run online. I hate these people who say they have just run a cheeky 5K. There are only two things that should be cheeky... pints and Nandos."

‌



For the past few years, Jack has spent time in LA, trying to crack the US, with roles in Hollywood movies such as Clifford the Big Red Dog and Jungle Cruise, alongside Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson in 2021.

Of trying to make it in the US he says: “I don't even know why I am still trying to do that. I don't want to live in America. They don't find me funny. My sense of humour bombs in America. I have also been quite insecure about my physique. I had body dysmorphia and bulimia in my 20s. In Los Angeles, I have a whole load of body expectations.

"In LA, every man is ‘Love Island good looking’. You have body expectations to get in shape. I had to take my shirt off in a film next to The Rock. That does wonders for your self esteem.”

View 5 Images Dwayne Johnson as Frank Wolff, Emily Blunt as Lily Houghton and Jack Whitehall as MacGregor Houghton in Disney’s Jungle Cruise (Image: Disney)

‌



And when he did work out for a part, Jack says no one watching him in films believed his body was real. He says: "I tried to rig up for a role for a film which had a sex scene in it. I did the training and was on a strict diet and not drinking. I got into the best shape that I have ever been in, but the problem was that the body I had was still attached to this head. So nobody thought it was real. Everyone thought it was AI."

But for now, Jack says he is just enjoying every minute of newly married life, even though he says he and Roxy argue and make up like any other couple. He adds: "Roxy had a really difficult pregnancy. She struggled with breast feeding. You watch this person you love crumble in front of you. so you cling on to any life raft that you can. What I find helpful is free therapy - seeing other couples argue in public. I say ‘look Roxy, they are more miserable than us’".

News.title: Police officer killed in A66 crash who 'proudly fought to make world better' laid to rest with guard of honour
News.content:
Police officer killed in A66 crash who 'proudly fought to make world better' laid to rest with guard of honour

The cortege carrying PC Tom Clough's coffin, topped with his police helmet and draped with the Union flag, was honoured by officers from every police force in the country today.

Funeral of A66 victim PC Tom Clough

There was a guard of honour as far as the eye could see today for the fallen A66 police officer who 'dedicated his short life to serving others'.

‌



The cortege carrying PC Tom Clough's coffin, topped with his police helmet and draped with the Union flag, passed representatives from every police force in the country.

‌



It made its way down the tree-lined approach to Kirkleatham Walled Garden near Redcar in North Yorkshire as a lone Scottish piper played the Skye Boat Song.

‌



Officers embraced and hugged as they waited for the cortege to arrive.

Four horses led the procession as standards from all 43 police forces in England and Wales were lowered alongside those from Northern Ireland, and the Royal British Legion.

His former colleagues from the nearby Cleveland Police HQ wiped away tears as they stood side by side with army personnel.

‌



View 6 Images The funeral service for PC Tom Clough today (Image: Cleveland Police)

His family told how he "proudly fought for his country to make the world a better place and was always on public duty throughout his short life."

PC Clough, 38, spent six years serving his country in Afghanistan and Iraq, latterly as a lance corporal with the 11th Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Search Regiment (Royal Logistic Corps).

‌



Hundreds of mourners heard of his lifetime of service to others which ended when he made the ultimate sacrifice alongside his friend and colleague, PC Matthew Blades, whose service was also held with full police honours in Hartlepool, Co Durham, yesterday.

View 6 Images The scene inside the marquee holding the funeral service, with hundreds of mourners (Image: Cleveland Police)

‌



They were both much-loved members of the Matrix team of responders.

They tragically lost their lives when a VW Passat containing five youths struck their armed response vehicle head-on at high speed in the early hours of August 22, on the A66 near Middlesbrough. Many of their colleagues wore a special identity badges for the funerals displaying ''PC Blades 2443 PC Clough 3234'.

PC Clough's family proudly told how he would give "everyone his everything," serving in the Civil Nuclear Constabulary and British Transport Police as well as the army before he joined the Cleveland force as an armed response officer. He was a 'partner, brother and son,' and loved his sausage dog, Frank.

‌



View 6 Images A police officer wears a badge embroidered with the names of two colleagues who were killed - Pc Blades and Pc Clough (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Lauren Somerville, chair of the Cleveland Police Federation, said his family wanted to thank the public for the 'outpouring of love' which has 'kept them going over the past few weeks'. She added: "They wanted people to know that he was not just a police officer, he was a partner, a brother and a son. He was so full of fun and most importantly, he deeply loved his sausage dog, Frank.

"Tommy used to say to his partner that there would not be anyone at his funeral. They now wish he could see the support for him. He was described as giving everyone his everything."

‌



There was total silence save for the distant sound of traffic as military and police pall bearers carried the coffin into the beautiful walled garden at Kirkleatham for a humanist ceremony. In a statement, PC Clough's family said: "He was our hero with a fantastic sense of humour who jumped into action whenever needed, and was willing to help anyone for any reason.

"He proudly fought for his country to make the world a better place and was always on public duty throughout his short life. We as a family and Tom's partner would like to express our sincere gratitude for the overwhelming support and condolences from friends, colleagues and the wider community".

View 6 Images Officers line the street for PC Tom Clough funeral today (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Hundreds of mourners, many in police uniform, filed into the garden for the funeral service after the coffin was carried in, as members of the public watched in respectful silence. Software consultant Paul Duce, 57, of Kirkleatham, said: "You can sum up why I am here in one word. Respect.

" I have so much respect for the two officers who lost their lives. PC Clough served his country and then served his community. We should never forget the job that these officers do."

Vicki Smith, 72, a retired pharmacy assistant also from Kirkleatham, added: "I think all the police officers present can be proud. That was a beautiful tribute to him." Anita Tinsley, 55, of Redcar, said: “I come from a police family, my dad was an inspector, so I know the worry that every officer’s loved ones feel when they go to work.

‌



“Sadly, these two young men paid the ultimate price for their service and it’s only right that they are remembered in the right way. I wanted to come along to pay my own respects and to show that the police are valued. The turnout today shows that the vast majority of people feel the same.”

View 6 Images The funeral of PC Tom Clough was held with full police honours (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Brian Dunn, 89, and wife Iris, 87, took a train, bus and then walked from their home in Stockton to pay their respects. Mr Dunn, who said he was proud to have done national service, said: “It is heart-warming to see so many people here.”

Mrs Dunn said: “We both felt it was important to be here. The police work so hard, they do their best, and it is never appreciated, we all know that.”

A woman from Redcar, who declined to be named, added: “I came to pay my respects because it was terrible what happened. “I came to show that the right part of society is behind them, most definitely.”

‌



The service was attended by Policing Minister Sarah Jones, fellow Home Office Minister and Redcar MP Anna Turley, Tees Valley Mayor Ben Houchen and the Cleveland Chief Constable Victoria Fuller, who paid tribute at the service. Chief Superintendent Richard Clark, Tom’s commanding officer at Sellafield Operational Policing Unit, described him as the 'epitome of professionalism'

View 6 Images Police officers hug each other before the funeral of Pc Tom Clough at Kirkleatham Walled Gardens near Redcar (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



He said PC Clough brought "dedication, skill and commitment to every task, whether serving within our Dynamic Search and Interdiction Team, or in his role as a Police Medic". He added: “What made Tom truly special was his personality. Alongside his professional excellence, he possessed a fun-loving, cheeky nature and a wit that could lift spirits even during the most demanding shifts.

"He had an extraordinary ability to light up any room he entered and to bring people together through his warmth, humour and authenticity. Tom was a hugely popular CNC officer, respected by colleagues and leaders alike, and it is no surprise that many of those who served alongside him remained close friends long after he left the organisation.

"While his life was far too short, it was undoubtedly lived to the full. Tom will be remembered with immense affection, gratitude and respect, and he will be hugely missed by all who had the privilege of serving alongside him.”

Article continues below

Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Michael Cahill, 23, Cole Worthy, 17, and Theo Rae, 17, were also killed in the A66 crash. Michael Cahill's funeral took place in County Durham today. He was buried alongside his father, and he was the last of the five to be laid to rest.

News.title: 'We have let down terminally ill people for far too long - all they ask for is choice'
News.content:
'We have let down terminally ill people for far too long - all they ask for is choice'

EXCLUSIVE: Labour MP Kim Leadbeater, who spearheaded the last attempt to legalise assisted dying, writes for The Mirror about why she believes MPs should vote in favour of assisted dying legislation ahead of a vote in the Commons on Friday

View 2 Images Labour MP Kim Leadbeater spearheaded the last attempt to legalise assisted dying (Image: PA)

When MPs voted to back my Bill to give choice to dying people in their last days and weeks we were offering them hope and the dignity they were asking for. They thank me for it every day. So too do so many people who don’t want to see their own loved ones suffer unnecessarily.

‌



That hope was dashed when a small minority of unelected members of the House of Lords stopped it becoming law. That was undemocratic and wrong. People in this country support assisted dying by a big majority. On Friday we can put that right and we must.

‌



My thoughts will be with those terminally ill people who have sadly died since I first brought in my Bill two years ago. They believed Parliament was going to change the unjust and often cruel way the law works now but passed away before we could do it.

‌



Six in 10 people support return of assisting dying bill to Parliament ahead of MPs' vote READ MORE :

View 2 Images 'That hope was dashed when a small minority of unelected members of the House of Lords stopped it becoming law' (Image: PRU/AFP via Getty Images)

We have let down terminally ill people and their loved ones for far too long. All they are asking for is choice. That choice has to be offered with strict safeguards to make sure no vulnerable person is pushed into a decision that isn’t what they genuinely want.

Article continues below

I worked tirelessly to make sure those protections were in place and MPs decided to support the Bill not once but twice. It is the safest in the world.

Now my colleague Lauren Edwards MP has brought the Bill back so the hope we offered is not extinguished.

The House of Commons has the chance to say that what terminally ill people deserve and what our constituents want can be delivered. That will help restore trust in our politics but most important of all it will give hope back to those who fear a painful and undignified death that even the very best end of life care cannot prevent.

News.title: Dr Amir Khan has alarming advice for anyone who uses phone for hours a day
News.content:
Dr Amir Khan has alarming advice for anyone who uses phone for hours a day

"Phones are amazing. We depend on them for lots of different things, and for many people they're a lifeline. But constant scrolling can do more to your body than you think."

View Image Dr Amir Khan has explained five ways using your phone too much could be damaging your health (file image) (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

Long gone are the days when all we used our phones for was to keep in touch with friends and family. Today the little devices we take everywhere with us can be used for almost anything you can think of, from playing music and watching videos, to paying for things and keeping on top of your banking.

‌



But could it be too much of a good thing? TV's Doctor Amir Khan, a familiar face on ITV's Good Morning Britain and Lorraine, has explained five reasons why using your phone too much can actually damage your health.

‌



Speaking in a video on TikTok, he said: "Phones are amazing. We depend on them for lots of different things, and, for many people, they're a lifeline. But constant scrolling can do more to your body than you think. Here are five science backed effects of too much phone use."

‌



1: Eye strain

Explaining this can also be called "computer vision syndrome", Dr Khan said: "When you stare at screens, your blink rate can drop by up to 60 per cent. That dries out the surface of your eye, causing blurred vision, headaches and eye fatigue.

"Try to take a break every 20 minutes from your phone screen. And the best thing to do is to go outside in nature, because things are at different depths and your eyes will have to focus on things near and far and that will help."

2: Neck problems

Describing this as "tech neck", Dr Khan said: "Tilting your head forward by 60 degrees to look at your phone increases the load on your neck to around 27kg. That's like carrying a seven-year-old on your neck all day.

‌



"Over time, it can cause muscle strain and even change the spinal curvature. Remember to take regular breaks and do some neck exercises."

3: Sleep disruption

"Blue light from screens suppresses melatonin, the hormone that signals it's time to sleep," Dr Khan said. "Even 30 minutes of phone use before bed can delay sleep onset and reduce deep restorative sleep.

"Try not to use your phone 30 minutes or more before bed. And if you can, keep your phone out of the bedroom."

‌



4: Mental health impact

Dr Khan explained: "Multiple studies link high screen time with increased rates of anxiety, depression, and reduced life satisfaction, especially in teenagers and young adults. Constant notifications keep the brain in a state of alert, which isn't restful.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"Real life connections are really important, so try meeting your friends for coffee or a walk rather than on the phone."

Article continues below

5: Reduced physical activity

"The more time we spend on screens, the less we tend to move," he said. "Sedentary behaviour is linked to a higher risk of heart disease, obesity, and type 2 diabetes, even if you exercise later in the day.

"My advice is get up and move regularly. They say sitting is the new smoking, and you don't want to be involved in that."

Concluding, Dr Khan said: "So next time you're scrolling, give your eyes, neck, and mind a break. Your future self will thank you."

News.title: Health expert's message to anyone on statins for a long time for cholesterol
News.content:
Health expert's message to anyone on statins for a long time for cholesterol

Taking the medication for a long time could increase the risk for some people

View 2 Images People taking the common medication may want to be aware of the potential risk (stock image) (Image: Getty)

A health expert has issued a message to anyone who has been taking prescribed statins for a long time to help manage their high cholesterol. Statins are one of the most commonly prescribed groups of medicines in the UK.

‌



According to the British Heart Foundation, an estimated seven to eight million people in the UK take statins daily to lower cholesterol and reduce the risk of heart attacks and strokes. The most frequently prescribed statins in the UK include Atorvastatin and Simvastatin.

‌



Most people need to take statins for a long time, and for some, the rest of their lives. According to experts, cholesterol levels typically begin to decline within four weeks of starting the medication. It usually takes about one to three months to see the full cholesterol-lowering effect.

‌



Old mice made to feel young again, a little stress is good for your cells, why you feel sleepy at 3pm, 'bad' cholesterol halved in one fell swoop - all this and more in our science newsletter

For those who have been prescribed statins and have been taking them for a long time, a health expert has issued a message. Dr Eric Berg DC, has taken to YouTube to upload a new video titled "What happens to your body after years of taking statins". In the video, the health specialist discusses the effects the medication can have on your body beyond lowering cholesterol.

Dr Eric Berg is a popular online health educator, author, and former chiropractor. He specialises in the "Healthy Keto" diet and intermittent fasting. He currently has 15 million subscribers on YouTube and is a Doctor of Chiropractic (DC).

‌



Dr Eric Berg warns that while statins block cholesterol production, they also inhibit the production of a co-enzyme called Q10, which he says is vital for heart and muscle energy. He highlights several potential side effects associated with this that may impact some people who take statins, including:

Increased risk of tendon rupture

Exercise intolerance and fatigue

Muscle pain and weakness

‌



He said: "When you take a statin, you are blocking the production of cholesterol, but you're also at the same time blocking the production of something your heart and your muscles depend on. And that is called co-enzyme Q10. Co-enzyme Q10 is a compound that the mitochondria need to produce energy, especially in your heart and your muscles."

Listing the potential associated risks, he added: "Increased risk of tendons rupturing, especially if you're exercising. You get exercise intolerance, and you're so tired you just don't feel like exercising... muscle pain, weakness, fatigue."

View 2 Images The issue may affect a small percentage of people while they're taking statins (stock image)

‌



What is CoQ10 and why is it important?

The British Heart Foundation (BHF) says that CoQ10, which is also called Co-enzyme Q10 or ubiquinone, is a substance similar to vitamins that exists in every cell of your body. It is especially abundant in the heart and brain.

CoQ10 plays a crucial role in helping your cells generate energy. It might also act as an antioxidant, helping reduce inflammation and support the health of your blood vessels.

Some researchers believe lower CoQ10 levels contribute to the muscle pain or fatigue that a small percentage of people feel while taking statins. Although researchers are still looking for a clear connection, many believe that low levels of CoQ10 are a major reason why some people experience muscle problems related to statin use, like weakness, pain, or cramps. Statins are very important for preventing heart attacks and strokes. It's essential to talk to your doctor before stopping them.

‌



Can I just take CoQ10 supplements?

Health organisations, such as the BHF, usually don't recommend CoQ10 supplements for muscle pain caused by statins because the research findings are mixed. If you're experiencing muscle pain or have worries about your medication, talk to your GP before you start any new supplements or stop taking your prescribed Atorvastatin or any other statin.

BHF says: " Statins reduce the amount of cholesterol your liver makes. They do this by blocking a chain of chemical reactions in your body’s cells which is needed to make cholesterol. This same chain of reactions is also used to produce CoQ10. So, taking statins may lead to lower levels of CoQ10.

Article continues below

"One theory is that lower levels of CoQ10 in the body might be linked to the muscle cramps and aches that some people experience when taking statins. However, studies looking at the effect of taking CoQ10 supplements on muscle pain are mixed and inconclusive. Muscle pain and cramps are difficult to diagnose and may be affected by the dose and type of statin, as well as a person’s age, gender, genetics and overall health."

News.title: Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%
News.content:
Labour's regional mayors in England have pledged to cap a new fee on visitors' overnight stays at 5%, after hospitality bosses warned it could put jobs at risk.

Local leaders are set to gain new powers to charge an uncapped levy, dubbed a "tourist tax", as a percentage of the cost of hotels, bed and breakfasts and other types of accommodation.

But the Labour mayors in 10 city regions said they would voluntarily limit the charge if they do apply it, adding that they had listened to concerns over costs.

Reform UK's two regional mayors and the two Conservative ones are likely to oppose any levy given criticism from their national parties of the policy.

In a letter to Chancellor John Healey and Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner, the Labour metro mayors said 5% represented a "reasonable ceiling" on the tax.

"It provides a balance of ensuring that local levies are not excessive, or vary significantly between regions, while also leaving room for local variation as appropriate," they added.

They added this would still allow for "meaningful investment" in local areas, whilst stressing any future levies in their areas would be "subject to local consultation".

The letter was signed by Labour mayors in London, Greater Manchester, Liverpool City Region, West Midlands, North East, West of England, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, East Midlands and York and North Yorkshire.

The government had earlier pledged to protect budget holidays "by making sure low-cost accommodation always pays lowest levy" and said the extra cash could be invested in high streets and local transport.

While Labour mayors have backed the new levy, others have expressed caution or signalled they will not bring it in.

Local leaders, including heads of Foundation Strategic Authorities where there is no mayor, will need to clarify by early 2028 how the revenue raised should be reinvested.

They will also be allowed to offer exemptions, such as for campsites.

However, mayors will not be allowed to exempt whole localities within their regions from the tax, to avoid creating confusion for visitors and businesses.

The government said it would introduce a bill to Parliament "in due course" to bring in the levy, which would apply to both Britons and people visiting from abroad.

News.title: Oil, gas and borrowing costs surge as fears over Middle East escalate
News.content:
The price of oil has jumped to $105 a barrel amid signs the conflict in the Middle East will not be resolved quickly, fuelling fears that inflation could accelerate.

With the conflict between the US and Iran in the Gulf intensifying in recent days, the cost of both crude oil and gas has been rising sharply. Brent crude went back above $100 a barrel on Wednesday and has continued to climb.

The war has led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, preventing supplies of oil and gas from the Gulf from reaching global markets.

US and UK long-term borrowing costs also surged to their highest level in decades.

Speaking at a Republican Party convention in Texas on Wednesday, President Trump said he did not think the fighting would end until after the US mid-term elections in November.

Analysts said the combination of rising energy costs and higher borrowing costs was adding pressure on financial markets.

Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at trading platform IG, said investors were becoming increasingly concerned about the economic impact of higher oil prices.

"It feels like investors worldwide are now waking up to the crisis in oil markets," Beauchamp said. He warned that the surge in energy prices could weigh heavily on the global economy if it continues.

Concerns have also grown after Iran-aligned Houthi forces were reported to have seized Yemen's port of Mokha, a key Red Sea port.

The move could elevate fears of further shipping disruptions.

The price of natural gas has also been soaring on wholesale markets. In the UK, it rose above 200p a therm for the first time since the end of 2022.

Storage levels in Europe are much lower than normal for the time of year, and the need to fill reserves ahead of the winter has helped to push up prices.

News.title: Use all powers necessary on anti-migrant protests, home secretary tells police
News.content:
"These scenes have caused disruption for people and, given that people are dressed in black wearing balaclavas, there is a fear factor and obvious malign intent being communicated to our residents," the Home Secretary said.

"This makes it different from other protests, so we need to make sure we are learning lessons."

The BBC understands that police chiefs are now actively considering using recently-granted powers to completely ban face coverings in specific areas, in light of that demonstration.

Saturday's protest was followed 24 hours later with another in which men blocked the only road out of Langstone Harbour, near Portsmouth, after the RNLI had brought ashore 120 migrants.

It's unclear at this stage whether further such protests will go ahead - but in some areas of England local groups that have associated themselves with the Patriot Platform umbrella group have called for more demonstrations.

The meeting discussed the emergence of Patriot Platform with ministers believing the group aims to intimidate communities.

Mahmood is said to have told police chiefs to make better use of intelligence to make sure they had better plans in place ahead of this weekend.

That call came after Kent Police had earlier admitted it had been made aware of a potential demonstration in Dover but had not "fully assessed" the warning before the town's nationally critical port road was brought to a standstill.

During the meeting, Mahmood is said to have made clear the government expected police to make full use of powers and to deal robustly with any criminal offences.

Speaking after the meeting, Deputy Chief Constable Andy Mariner, the National Police Chiefs Council lead for public order, said forces were "continually assessing and preparing for protests and any potential impact on public safety".

This includes working closely with "local forces, specialist teams, communities and partners" to ensure support is available when needed.

He added: "Our priority is to keep people safe, maintain public order and support the right to peaceful and lawful protest. While people are entitled to express their views, anyone committing criminal offences can and should expect police action."

Major changes to protest law in the last three years mean officers can now intervene more quickly to end demonstrations that block critical national infrastructure, such as roads to ports.

They can also designate an entire area a face mask-free zone for the duration of a protest.

It's that second power that police chiefs are now considering using.

Police chiefs also say they have initiated an "enhanced and co-ordinated" approach to gathering as much intelligence as possible in the days ahead.

News.title: Bayeux Tapestry unveiled to UK public for first time at British Museum
News.content:
Cecilia and Fabio Zanini were completely wowed by the scale of the Bayeux Tapestry.

"I was amazed by the vibrancy of the colours. The detail of the characters," Cecilia said. "It gave both of us goosebumps."

Fabio said he was constantly looking left and right to see all the action and he was surprised by the scale of the tapestry, particularly the number of Norman boats and cavalry.

"It feels like you're in the battlefield," he added, praising the "real sense of movement" in the embroidery.

"It really allowed you to go back to 1066."

But others told the BBC the event was "out of reach" because of its cost and London location.

Angie in Leeds said the "historic event" was "out of reach for many, many families in the north" when you factor in the cost of train tickets and food costs on top of the museum tickets themselves.

"London-only cultural events alienate many families north of Watford," she added.

Another man spoke of the "extreme queuing" required to view the exhibit. Hadyn Blakeston said he felt like he was on a "conveyor belt" while moving along the tapestry.

"It's one long queue," he said. "I know we're supposed to love queuing, but it was extreme queuing."

News.title: Four hurt and seven arrested in London stabbing
News.content:
Seven people have been arrested after four men were stabbed in south-east London, the Metropolitan Police has said.

One of the men remains in a critical condition in hospital, while the other three are being treated for injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening.

Paramedics and the London Air Ambulance were called at about 14:20 BST to Bromley High Street, where one eyewitness reported seeing a man wielding a machete.

A fight is believed to have taken place near a KFC restaurant. KFC has told the BBC the attack did not happen within the premises, and would not comment on eyewitness accounts that a situation began there and spilled into the street.

News.title: Drone display recreates the Twin Towers over New York City
News.content: According to organisers, 2,977 drones recreated the Twin Towers at full scale with each light representing a victim of the 9/11 attacks. The artwork, titled "2,977 Lights Over New York Harbor", is a commemorative public art installation in collaboration with artists, producers, and members of the 9/11 community, including victims' families, survivors, and first responders.

News.title: Esther Rantzen says she is too fragile to travel to Switzerland to end life
News.content:
Dame Esther Rantzen has said she is now "too physically fragile" to travel to Switzerland to end her life at an assisted suicide clinic.

The veteran broadcaster, 86, said she would have to fly to the country, where the practice is legal, alone, which she could only have done before her life became "unbearable" and before she was ready to end her life.

The Childline founder, who is terminally ill with cancer, first revealed in December 2023 that she had joined the Dignitas clinic.

Dame Esther used her statement on Thursday to reiterate a plea for MPs to vote in favour of legalising assisted suicide in England and Wales when proposed legislation is revisited by Parliament on Friday.

She announced she had joined Dignitas about a year after being diagnosed with stage four lung cancer.

"Unfortunately, when I was strong enough to make the flight and go to Dignitas, my life was not unbearably painful, indeed I was able to relax in my beloved cottage in the New Forest," she said.

"And by the time life did become unbearable, I was too physically fragile to make the journey and go through the Dignitas process.

"So even though I had spent the money and made the plans, I was not ready to end my life back then, and did not realise that would be my last chance."

Dame Esther added that "everything I didn't want to happen I'm having to go through now", with loved ones either unable to visit her or "see me suffering pain or indignity" when they do.

The prominent assisted suicide campaigner said the law - which she described as "messy and cruel" - must "change and change quickly".

Helping someone end their life is currently considered a criminal offence across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Jersey legalised assisted dying for terminally ill adults earlier this year.

MPs are considering a draft law that, if passed, would make it legal in England and Wales under specific circumstances for people who are terminally ill with less than six months to live.

While Dame Esther, who is best known for presenting the BBC programme That's Life! for 21 years, is among several leading figures in favour of the bill, there are also campaigners against it, including Paralympian Baroness Grey-Thompson

They fear that a change in the law could mean that disabled and other vulnerable people could be pressured to end their lives, while also criticising the wording of the proposed legislation as not providing strong enough safeguards.

The bill has been through several drafts and has been scrutinised by several Parliamentary committees and the House of Lords, which submitted 1,200 amendments.

The bill was previously introduced in 2024, but the last session of Parliament ran out of time before it was passed.

It was reintroduced in this Parliament and a second vote will be held on Friday afternoon. If it passes the House of Commons, rarely invoked powers could be used, meaning it would not need the assent of the Lords to become law this time.

Proponents of the bill have indicated they would try to bring legislation again as soon as possible were it to be voted down on Friday.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he would not be voting on the issue and has suggested that palliative and social care should be better funded before legalising assisted suicide is considered.

Assisted suicide is legal in a number of countries - including Canada, Australia and Belgium - as well as in Switzerland, though the circumstances under which it is legal differ between those nations.

News.title: Police and army attend funeral for officer killed in wrong-way A66 crash
News.content:
Police officers and army veterans gathered for the funeral of the second officer killed in a head-on crash.

PC Tom Clough, 38, died on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 22 August with his colleague PC Matthew Blades when a Volkswagen Passat hit their marked police car. Five young men in the Passat also died.

Members of the public also gathered for the funeral at Kirkleatham Walled Gardens, in Redcar, along with family, friends and former colleagues from British Transport Police and the Civil Nuclear Constabulary in Sellafield, Cumbria.

Cleveland Police Federation chair Lauren Somerville said PC Clough's partner said public support "brought them so much strength".

The ceremonial procession made its way along Plantation Road towards the Walled Gardens, accompanied by the music of a lone piper.

The road was lined on both sides with standard bearers who had lowered their flags before the cortege went past.

At its head was a mounted police unit of four horses.

Immediately behind them came the hearse carrying PC Clough's coffin, draped with the Union Flag and topped with his custodian helmet.

The hearse was flanked by officers in ceremonial dress escorting the coffin to the service.

News.title: Catherine joins William as he says sport can save lives from suicide
News.content:
It was important that sports stars admitted their own vulnerability, said Olympic cyclist Dame Laura Kenny.

She spoke movingly of how a family member had tried to take their life and how she felt "almost ashamed to admit that this could happen in my family because it's not a subject that is easily spoken about".

The cyclist also described the darkness of her feelings after the loss of two babies, through a miscarriage and an ectopic pregnancy, "which ultimately ended up in an emergency situation".

On Your Side aims to use the reach of sport to raise awareness about suicide and to show people the help available in a crisis, with the Football Association, Premier League and Team GB providing support.

The level of suicide is disproportionately higher among men than women - it is the biggest cause of death for men under the age of 50 in the UK - and sport is seen as an effective way of communicating that help is available.

"My hope is that every sporting organisation in the country will look at what is being launched today and ask a question: 'What more can we do?' Because the opportunity before us is enormous," Prince William said.

The royal couple saw a bench at the ground dedicated in memory of Gary Speed, a footballer who once played at the club, and who died by suicide in 2011.

The bench, unveiled last year, is intended to give people a space to speak openly about their anxieties and the royal couple met Speed's mother there.

Shearer was a friend of Speed and is backing the call for people to try to support people they have worries about.

"You don't have to be an expert. You don't have to have all the answers," said Shearer. "But we can all be better at asking, listening, and helping someone find the right support."

News.title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat
News.content:
People will be able to go to their local chemist in England this autumn and get on-the-spot treatment for 12 common conditions without going to their GP first.

Pharmacists can already prescribe medication for seven conditions - sore throat, earache, sinusitis, shingles, impetigo, infected bites and urinary tract infections.

Five more - migraines, acne, scabies, ear infections and badly blocked noses - are now also being added to that list.

NHS England said the move was to ease pressure on busy GPs and A&E departments while making sure people could get treatment quickly and conveniently.

After a very hot summer and three of the busiest months on record in A&Es in England, the NHS says it wants to make it as easy as possible for people to get help when they need it for everyday conditions.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said people were "fed up with the scramble for routine appointments" and wanted help close to home, with no more taking time off work or waiting to get seen.

"For five more common conditions, you'll be able to walk into your local pharmacy and get treated on the spot," he said.

Mr Burnham said families would feel the change, and the plan would give people back "precious time".

The five conditions which can now also be treated via pharmacies are:

low frequency migraines in adults

hay fever or allergic rhinitis in children

ear infections in adults

mild to moderate acne in young people and adults

mild skin infections and scabies

That's in addition to these seven:

sore throat

sinusitis

earache

insect bites

impetigo

shingles

uncomplicated UTIs

Initially, a few hundred chemists will offer treatments for the five new conditions, NHS England says.

There will be a gradual rollout and the service will eventually be available at thousands of community NHS pharmacies across England.

Community pharmacies also offer support with healthy eating, exercise, stopping smoking, monitoring your blood pressure, contraception, flu and Covid vaccinations.

News.title: Ex-Tory campaign chief pleads guilty over election bet
News.content:
The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have pleaded guilty to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.

Anthony Lee stood to win approximately Â£15,000 after placing more than 60 successful bets totalling Â£1,549, the Gambling Commission said.

He passed confidential information to his wife about when former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak was planning to call the general election.

Laura Lee, who was a parliamentary candidate at the time, placed eight successful bets on the election date totalling Â£535 and would have profited by around Â£5,000.

On Thursday at Southwark Crown Court, Anthony Lee pleaded guilty to two offences and Laura Lee pleaded guilty to one offence.

They will be sentenced in October.

The trials of 10 other defendants will take place in September 2027 and January 2028.

Former MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.

In Williams' case, the prosecution said he bet Â£250, Â£100, and Â£22.50 on the date of the 2024 election, telling the court he "used highly sensitive and confidential information".

When details of the scandal first emerged in June 2024, Williams admitted making a "huge error of judgment".

Sunak's decision to call the poll was a surprise to many, including many Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.

The Conservative Party has been approached for comment.

News.title: Michael Sheen says he was snubbed by first minister over toxic pollution claims
News.content:
Michael Sheen says an offer to meet Wales' first minister over claims people have been poisoned by decades of exposure to toxic waste dumps "was not taken up".

The Welsh actor contacted Rhun ap Iorwerth ahead of a BBC documentary which looked into claims of widespread chemical contamination in Wales.

In Parliament on Thursday, Sheen urged MPs to back a national testing programme for historic toxic dumps to make sure sites were safe, after high levels of cancer-causing chemicals - known as PCBs - were found in soil samples and in the blood of people living near sites linked to chemical giant Monsanto.

Eastman Chemical Company, which is responsible for its legacy production, was asked to comment.

The Welsh government said addressing the issue of contaminated land was "a key priority".

One MP at the UK Parliament committee hearing later suggested to the BBC that there was confusion about whether it was the Welsh or UK government that would be responsible for any testing.

News.title: Council told to disclose 24,000 pages of Sara Sharif files
News.content:
A coroner leading the inquest into the death of Sara Sharif has ordered Surrey County Council to disclose more than 24,000 pages of documents.

Sara, 10, was found dead at her family home in Woking, with her father Urfan Sharif and stepmother Beinash Batool jailed for life in 2024 for murder.

A pre-inquest review heard that the inquest, originally scheduled for April, will be pushed back by a further six months to October 2027.

The eight-week inquest will examine what state agencies knew, or ought to have known, about Sara's safety before she was murdered.

At the hearing in Woking on Thursday, senior coroner Richard Travers told the county council that he wants "all of the pages" to be disclosed to him by 2 October.

He said he would call the local authority's chief executive Terence Herbert to appear before the court if he did not have them.

Alethea Redfern, representing the authority, argued against the full disclosure of the documents, saying that many were "irrelevant" to the inquest.

But Travers said he does not understand what the council's "issue" was with him obtaining the files.

News.title: Two arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service
News.content:
Two people have been arrested in London on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service, the Metropolitan Police has said.

A 60-year-old man and 42-year-old woman were arrested at properties in London on Wednesday as part of an investigation into suspected National Security Act (NSA) offences.

The suspects, who were both held on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service, have been released on bail under strict conditions until late October, the Met said.

Police said the arrests were not "connected to any of the incidents or attacks" linked to Jewish and Iranian communities across London earlier this year.

The arrests took place following two searches carried out at properties in north and north-west London in June, the Met added.

Commander Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said she knows "news of these arrests will come as a concern to some members of the public" but stressed she does "not believe there to be any imminent threat to the wider public".

She added: "We've seen a marked increase in the tempo of our work linked to national security and state threats over the past year and this investigation is a continuation of that.

"As we've shown here, if we suspect any activity could threaten the safety of the UK or the public, then we will not hesitate to take action."

She added the UK's terror threat level was severe and called for people to be vigilant.

News.title: Teacher sexually abused pupils at multiple schools
News.content:
A teacher has been found guilty of sexually abusing a 16-year-old boy after previously admitting offences against two teenage girls.

Former PE teacher Bronwen James, 30, of Chippenham, Wiltshire, admitted nine sexual offences against two teenage girls - one a pupil at Bitterne Park School in Southampton and the other at Hardenhuish School in Chippenham.

She was convicted earlier at Winchester Crown Court of three counts of sexual activity with a 16-year-old boy who also attended Bitterne Park School.

During the trial the prosecution said James "craved" attention and "abused the trust put in her" as a teacher.

The jury found James guilty of the three counts of sexual activity with a child by a person in a position of trust by a majority of 11 to one and acquitted her of a fourth charge.

Due to legal restrictions covering the trial, media had been unable to report James' guilty pleas against two girls - which she made in January - and the jury were not told about them until after they had passed their verdict.

News.title: Library books overdue by 116 years returned in 'excellent condition'
News.content:
A man has returned his late grandfather's library books which were overdue by 116 years.

Peter O'Sullivan's grandfather, Walter Griffith Owen, took out Milton's Paradise Lost and Shakespeare's King Lear in 1910.

A note inside showed they came from former Llanrwst Reading Room & Library in Conwy county, and were originally "lent for one week".

The note continued that should a book "be required for a second week, application should be made to the caretaker. Fee, one penny per week".

Peter said he was initially concerned about a possible fine, as they had been on loan for in excess of 6,000 weeks.

There were 12 pennies in a shilling and 20 shillings in a pound before decimalisation in 1971.

News.title: ‘Dangerous’ teenager who murdered grandfather while on police bail jailed for life
News.content:
