Read our Privacy notice

A violent teenager who was released on police bail twice – leaving him free to murder a beloved grandfather in a “shocking and cowardly” attack – has been jailed for life.

Rasheed Rahman, then aged 19, plunged a five-inch kitchen knife that he had signed out from his supported living accommodation into the back of Mark Carroll, 55, as he walked in a small London park with a friend on 10 April 2024.

Rahman, who was not known to Mr Carroll, then fled the scene, still armed with the murder weapon, sparking an hour-long manhunt. He threatened two other people with the blade before he was eventually caught.

The Independent revealed in June how, in the days leading up to the murder, Rahman – a Sudanese national who told immigration enforcement that he had come to the UK illegally via a lorry as a child – had been arrested on two separate occasions and released on police bail, leaving him free to kill.

open image in gallery Rasheed Rahman checked out a knife from his supported accommodation, before going on to kill Mark Carroll in a random unprovoked attack ( Metropolitan Police )

And in the two months before the killing, Rahman had stabbed Iulian Cavaliuc in a separate attack in east London but was not tracked down by police due to delays in gathering CCTV.

The Metropolitan Police has since launched an investigation into contact police had with Rahman in the days leading up to Mr Carroll’s murder in St Martin’s Gardens, Camden – and whether anything could have been done to stop the killing.

Jailing him for a minimum term of 24 years and 59 days, Judge Dodd told Wood Green Crown Court on Thursday that “it was a shocking and cowardly attack”.

Judge Dodd said the act “left Mark Carroll’s family broken and grieving”, adding: “This was a random unprovoked attack by you on a wholly innocent unsuspecting member of the public. You are clearly a very dangerous young man.”

Mr Carroll’s daughter, Danielle Morley, told the court she was 19 weeks pregnant with her son when she heard her father had been killed in the shocking attack.

She said: “My dad was a loving, caring, and humble person and an amazing grandad to my two girls. He would never hurt anybody, on the day of the attack, all he was doing was spending time with his friends, in one of his favourite places, enjoying the sunshine, something he would do every day.”

open image in gallery Mark Carroll was remembered as a loving and caring father ( Metropolitan Police )

She added: “Having to identify his body while heavily pregnant traumatised me in ways I cannot explain... Nobody deserves what happened to our dad, he was excited to meet his grandson, we had so many plans together,” she said.

Mr Carroll’s other daughter, Ayisha Carroll, told the court that she has been diagnosed with PTSD since her father’s murder and continues to experience flashbacks and often relives the moment she heard he had died.

“It feels as though the world has become a much more dangerous place, and I worry constantly about losing about other people I love,” Ms Carroll said. “The crime did not only take my father’s life - it took my sense of safety, my peace of mind, and the future I thought I would have with him in it.”

Ms Carroll said her mother, who remained close to Mr Carroll, lives with schizophrenia, which has become worse since his death. “She sometimes hears him as a voice and speaks about him as though he is still alive.”

In the lead up to murdering Mr Carroll, Rahman had been arrested after he lashed out at members of the public on a canal towpath in Camden Town, north London. He had tried to punch and kick people, threw a cafe sign into the canal, and brandished a metal pole before he was pushed into the water by a “public-spirited member of the public”, Judge Dodd said.

open image in gallery Rasheed Rahman talking to Iulian Cavaliuc before he stabbed him in the back ( CPS/ Met police )

He had also allegedly used a brick to smash a window to break into an office in a church.

Even before the February attack on Mr Cavaliuc, Rahman was known to police. Seven months earlier, in June 2023, Rahman pleaded guilty to possession of a Class B drug and possession of a sharp pointed article – a broken pub dart – in a public place. Rahman was sentenced to a community order for that offence.

A few months earlier, in March 2023, he had been granted temporary leave to remain in the UK following a successful asylum application. He had been living undocumented in the UK before being picked up by immigration officers while working at a restaurant in Essex in 2021.

John Femi-Ola KC, acting for the defence, told the court Rahman had no medical defence to murder but had “a complex post-traumatic stress disorder”.

He said Rahman had been born in Sudan “and it’s quite clear that he suffered terrible experiences.” Mr Femi-Ola told the judge: “His village was raided by the terrorist militia group Boko Haram, who murdered his sister before his very eyes. He was then able to escape, leaving his family behind.”

Mr Femi-Ola said Rahman had been enslaved in Libya and tortured and raped. “He clearly has significant disruption and trauma from the age of 9. We submit that the trauma that he experienced in Libya, and Sudan, rendered him emotionally vulnerable and psychologically immature, at the time of these offences.”

open image in gallery St Martin’s Gardens in Camden where Mark Carroll was killed ( Metropolitan Police )

Mr Femi-Ola also argued Rahman’s age was a “significant mitigating factor”.

Judge Dodd said it was clear from doctor’s notes that Rahman “is not suffering currently from a severe and enduring psychotic illness”. The court heard Rahman’s symptoms could worsen under stress or “in the context of the disinhibiting effects of illicit drugs”.

Rahman has a previous conviction for the possession of cannabis, and was found with the drug when he was arrested for Mr Carroll’s death.

Judge Dodd questioned whether there was independent evidence that established Rahman’s history of trauma or his age, but was told independent material was not available to support information about Rahman’s background.

Judge Dodd said: “There is in reality no mitigation of substance here, save for recognising your age at the time 19, and the absence as I find it of an intention to kill. But I do not consider that your mental health issues reduced the seriousness of your offending.”

The judge told the court that Rahman had previously been admitted to hospital for mental health issues, with cannabis use considered to be a factor in that admission.

A new documentary about the ongoing conflict in Gaza earned a 24.5-minute ovation at its Venice Film Festival premiere on Thursday, making it the longest-ever standing ovation at the event.

Naza directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, also known for the Oscar-winning documentary film No Other Land, grew teary-eyed during the applause while audience members held up Palestinian flags.

The film gives insight into Israeli airstrikes in the region, featuring testimonies from 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers about the attitude towards civilian casualties.

Naza, the title of the film, is an acronym used by Israeli intelligence to refer to civilian collateral damage, which means the number of civilians killed or expected to be killed in an airstrike.

open image in gallery ‘Naza’ filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor wiped away tears as they received Venice Film Festival’s longest standing ovation ( Reuters )

The subjects in the film detail the surveillance systems and remote bombing involved in the Israeli military's operation.

“We just told these officers and soldiers, please describe to us what you did,” Abraham said in a news conference Thursday. “Of course there were other questions that arose but the principal question was a question of detail — sketch it for us, we want to know how it worked. And sometimes just asking the question, you get answers.”

The film builds on reporting between 2023 and 2025 published by the Israeli-Palestinian +972 Magazine, the Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and The Guardian.

“We felt that there is still some sort of importance to take those testimonies and put it in a film,” Szor said. “It’s different to hear, actually, the people who designed and operated those systems talk about it in front of a camera, and sketch it, show it.”

open image in gallery The subjects in ‘Naza’ detail the surveillance systems and remote bombing involved in the Israeli military's operation. ( Getty )

The film is produced by The Guardian and James Wilson (JW Films) and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer. Wilson and Glazer are the Oscar-winning team behind the film The Zone of Interest.

At last year’s festival, The Voice of Hind Rajab, about the death of a six-year-old Palestinian girl called Hind Rajab, who was killed by an Israeli strike in Gaza while she was waiting for aid, earned a 22-minute standing ovation. It held the record for the longest standing ovation before Naza.

News.title: What happens now after man accused of locking 16 kids in a squalid room found unfit to stand trial
News.content:
The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A southern Ohio grandfather whose 16 grandchildren were found living in squalid conditions was declared mentally incompetent to stand trial on Wednesday – but the case is still set to continue against other members of his family.

Gary Siders Sr., 73, appeared in a Vinton County courtroom in a wheelchair and a gray T-shirt, facing 16 counts of child endangerment. The charges stem from a June 30 raid on a rural property in Hamden, Ohio, where authorities discovered 16 children ranging in age from 18 months to 18 years living in a small, 12-by-12-foot room amid severe squalor and human waste.

When police breached the home, Vinton County Sheriff Ryan Cain described it as a “disgusting scene.” Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson later stated that the isolated youths looked “almost like feral animals” and that several “couldn’t even speak.”

Vinton County Prosecutor William Archer raised no objections to the competency findings.

Discussing the ruling, defense attorney Dorian Baum told reporters that his client had experienced a prolonged cognitive decline.

open image in gallery Gary Siders Sr, a 73-year-old southern Ohio grandfather whose 16 grandchildren were found living in squalid conditions, was declared mentally incompetent to stand trial on Wednesday ( Southeastern Ohio Regional Jail )

“It’s not really a surprise to any of us that he’s not been found competent at this point,” Baum said. “He doesn’t fully understand or appreciate what’s going on.”

Baum added that because the evaluation deemed Siders’ condition “not restorable,” the criminal prosecution against the grandfather would likely conclude without moving to trial.

Legal proceedings against the three other co-defendants remain active. Siders’ wife Christina Siders, 68, his son Gary Siders Jr., 36, and his daughter-in-law Elizabeth Siders, 33 — who court records show is the mother of all 16 children — have each pleaded not guilty to 19 counts of child endangerment.

open image in gallery Authorities arrested Gary Siders Jr (top left), Elizabeth Siders (top right), Christina Siders (bottom left) and Gary Siders Sr (bottom right) on June 30 ( Vinton County Sheriff )

Before the competency ruling, Baum defended the patriarch by claiming the house was fully functional with working utilities and food, telling reporters that critics should “step back” from what he argued was a state agency “criminalizing poverty.”

Court documents indicate that Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders married in West Virginia in March 2008, when he was 18 and she was 15, with her parents’ consent. Their eldest child was born two months later in May 2008, and filings show Elizabeth Siders was pregnant during most of the years that followed. of scho

Records show that the discovery came despite child protective services investigating the family years earlier. Gallia County Children’s Services opened an inquiry in March 2020 after online educators raised alarms over severe educational neglect, noting that an 11-year-old child could not write the alphabet or pronounce letter sounds and could only count to 12, while a 13-year-old sibling had dropped out of school.

open image in gallery The house in Hamden, Ohio, where police found 16 children living in a single, waste-filled room ( AP )

By December 2020, a physician warned officials of severe developmental delays linked to potential lead poisoning, and a later home visit by a caseworker found roaches, gnats and flies swarming the residence along with two children showing insect bites and bruising. Despite this, the agency permitted the parents to retain physical custody under protective supervision before closing the file five months later.

The initial search warrant that led deputies to discover the captive children was executed as part of a separate sex crimes investigation. Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders also face separate counts of sexual battery and unlawful sexual conduct with a minor involving individuals outside their immediate family.

All 16 rescued children were initially hospitalized for medical evaluation before being transitioned into state protective custody.

Officials previously noted that the victims lacked formal schooling, medical histories or government documentation as the family moved through various Ohio counties over two decades, with surrounding neighbors reporting that they had never once seen the kids outdoors.

A coalition of civil rights groups and voting rights advocates are suing to block Donald Trump’s administration from deploying immigration enforcement agents to polling places on Election Day.

The administration has not explicitly outlined plans to send armed Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers to the polls, but top officials have repeatedly suggested that federal agents could show up to respond to “threats” or make an immigration arrest.

But that’s illegal, according to Thursday’s lawsuit, which was joined by the city of Denver. Under federal law, the only reason federal agents or the U.S. military can show up to polling places is to “repel armed enemies of the United States,” the lawsuit states.

“The specter of armed officers at polling places threatens the freedom of this upcoming election,” according to the complaint.

That threat “places voters in fear that they will be confronted by armed federal immigration enforcement officers if they choose to cast a ballot” and “makes it more difficult for state and local election officials and law enforcement to do their jobs by making polling places spaces of confrontation,” the groups wrote.

open image in gallery Voting rights groups are suing to block the Trump administration from deploying ICE agents to polling places after officials have repeatedly suggested that they have authority to do so ( Reuters )

The lawsuit follows a series of public statements from top administration officials clarifying the role, if any, that ICE could play in upcoming midterm elections, with the balance of power in Congress — and fate of Trump’s remaining years in office — at stake.

The president, meanwhile, has not dismissed the idea of declaring a national emergency to implement sweeping plans to overhaul election systems on a debunked conspiracy theory that millions of noncitizen voters are illegally casting ballots and manipulating the outcomes.

In a statement to The Independent, a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security said that “ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations.”

“ICE conducts intelligence-driven targeted enforcement, and if an active public safety threat endangered a polling location, they may be arrested as a result of that targeted enforcement action,” the person said.

In February, after Trump pushed Republicans to “nationalize the voting,” former Trump adviser Steve Bannon called on ICE to “surround the polls.” Asked whether Trump is planning to send ICE agents to the polls, then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said she “can’t guarantee that an ICE agent won’t be around a polling location in November.”

During the Conservative Political Action Conference in March, now-Attorney General Todd Blanche questioned why there would be any “objection” to sending ICE officers to polling places.

In May, after several secretaries of state asked officials to clarify whether that was actually happening, then-Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons said “there is no reason for ICE personnel to be deployed to polling places” but said that the agency “plays an important role in investigating voter fraud and will continue to perform this vital mission.”

That same month, armed ICE agents made an arrest in the parking lot outside a polling place in San Antonio, Texas. And in June, agents showed up to polling places in California and New York.

open image in gallery Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says ICE agents are allowed to respond to ‘threats’ and serve warrants at polling places ( Reuters )

Agents questioned an election worker in Syracuse, New York, about her social media posts about an ICE agent who fatally shot Renee Good in Minneapolis, but the election worker was in the middle of her shift at the polling place while they confronted her.

“I don't understand what the concern is about enforcement of immigration at polling places anyways because honestly if you're not a citizen you shouldn't be voting anyways so technically there shouldn't be illegals at the polling spot,” Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said during his Senate confirmation hearing.

“The only reason why my officers would be there is if there was a specific threat for them to be there, not for intimidation,” he added.

Earlier this month, Mullin did not dispel the idea of ICE agents at polling places with Election Day just weeks away.

He told reporters that “the only reason why we would be at polling places is if there is a threat to that polling place or we’re serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down.”

“ICE’s job is immigration, customs enforcement,” he said. “If we’re serving a warrant we will be where we need to be.”

open image in gallery Voting rights groups have accused the Trump administration of illegally trying to suppress voter turnout by raising the specter of noncitizen voting to undermine election results when Republicans lose ( Getty )

“The right to vote, and to do so without fear of intimidation, is fundamental to our democracy and to being an American,” Denver Mayor Mike Johnston said in a Thursday statement.

“Stationing ICE agents near polling places is only meant to scare people and suppress votes,” he added. “We’ll fight tooth and nail to prevent it.”

Stationing armed agents at polling places “is a tactic used by dictators,” said Virginia Kase Solomón, president of voting rights group Common Cause.

“No American should ever have to walk past armed federal law enforcement just to cast a ballot, yet this administration has adopted a policy that allows exactly that,” she said.

Janet Murguía, president of Latino rights group UnidosUS, called the policy “voter suppression, plain and simple.”

“All Americans — including Latino voters — have a constitutional right to cast their ballot without fear of interrogation, detention, or family separation,” she said.

Changing jobs has become a lucrative move - and Gen Z have got the memo.

Pay rises for job switchers have reached a three-year high, according to July data from a Bank of America study published Wednesday.

Job switchers saw a 15 percent pay increase - compared to a 4 percent increase for those who stayed put.

“Gen Z continue to benefit the most from changing jobs, while workers paid by the hour are also making particularly large gains from switching,” the study said.

Adults, aged 18 to 30, who changed jobs saw their pay go up nearly 20 percent in July. Boomers (aged 62 to 80) saw the smallest pay increase from switching jobs, according to the study.

open image in gallery Younger Gen Z workers typically enter the workforce earning lower wages than workers later in their careers. Pay rises from job switching tend to have a bigger impact on their income ( Getty )

President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act may be fueling the raises, the study found. The legislation removed overtime tax, a change that could be fueling lower-income wage growth.

Gen Z is seeing the biggest impact because they’re early in their careers and pay is relatively low, “creating substantial percentage increases when they switch jobs,” the study said.

Getting a pay rise couldn’t come at a better time for a lot of Americans. The past six months have been a patchwork of trade-offs and cutbacks for consumers due to increased cost of living. Inflation remains above 3 percent and gas prices persist above $4 a gallon, linked to the Trump administration’s war with Iran.

open image in gallery Blue-collar hourly employees like construction workers might be benefiting from President Donald Trump ending taxes on overtime pay, a Bank of America study found ( Reuters )

Even a $200 or $300 monthly wage increase from a job switch can provide much-needed breathing room.

Some 39 percent of consumers have less than $50 left at the end of the month, and another 35 percent have nothing left over, according to a June study from financial services firm Self found.

Seat belts and a flight attendant call button from the doomed United Airlines Flight 93. A purse filled with keys and a wallet recovered from the World Trade Center site. The telephone that sat on U.S. Solicitor General Ted Olson's desk when his wife, Barbara, called from a hijacked airplane.

The Smithsonian's National Museum of American History is honoring the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks this week with displays of dozens of rarely seen objects that tell the story of that day in often searingly personal terms.

The exhibit, which runs through Saturday, comes as the museum is under growing scrutiny by President Donald Trump and Republicans in Congress over the manner in which it tells American history.

The Smithsonian began collecting items just months after the attacks and regularly displays some of them throughout the sprawling museum along the National Mall. But this week's exhibit is unique as the items are displayed on tables, rather than seen through glass. The museum's director, Anthea Hartig, said some of the items being shown this week are “so fragile they'll probably never go on display.”

The goal, she said, is to help visitors “both never forget, but also kind of reconnect" as a new generation emerges that didn't experience the attacks.

“This has truly slipped into history rather than being part of our memory landscape,” she said.

Some of the items, including a beeper belonging to an employee who worked on the 97th floor of the South Tower, harken back to office life at the turn of the century. A candy dispenser from the Pentagon includes melted chocolate.

The museum has faced conservative criticism since the White House released a report on Independence Day branding the museum's leadership as radical activists. Hartig faced two days of congressional hearings in July, where Republicans argued the museum should present a more unifying version of American history, prompting concern from historians that lawmakers and the White House were more interested in revisionism than accurate history.

Trump later ordered his administration to install signs in front of the museum telling visitors that some of the exhibits are inaccurate. More than a month later, such signs have not been installed.

In an interview, Hartig said the scrutiny didn't influence how the Sept. 11 exhibit came together.

“This museum exists as a repository, as a place of memory,” she said. “And so the current political moment is like many other political moments that we document. There’s different opinions and contestation over how we do our work.”

More change could be ahead after Lonnie Bunch announced his plans to step down as the leader of the Smithsonian Institution. The Smithsonian operates outside the executive branch and Bunch's successor will be chosen by a Board of Regents that includes Vice President JD Vance, Supreme Court Chief Justice John Roberts, a bipartisan group of lawmakers and so-called citizen regents.

Hartig acknowledged that “leadership transitions are always complicated.”

But, she said, “I wake up every day confident in Americans' ability to embrace the complexities of their past.”

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stands in the lead up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

News.title: West Nile virus hits Europe as temperatures climb
News.content:
“The future looks rosy for West Nile virus and other mosquito-borne viruses that follow it to the New World,” wrote the science writer Carl Zimmer in his 2011 book ‘Planet of Viruses’.

“That’s because the future is going to be warm and wet.”

More than a decade on, and after a record-setting hot summer, Mr Zimmer’s prediction has come to pass: the mosquito-borne disease, once confined mostly to the warmest parts of Africa, has become firmly entrenched in Europe, experts have warned.

At least 1,086 locally acquired cases of West Nile virus have been recorded across the continent over the last three months, as mosquitoes continue their slow march northwards.

The insects – which are cold-blooded – need warm weather to accelerate their life cycles and survive long enough to spread disease.

Across July and August, countries including Italy, Spain and France recorded West Nile cases in previously unaffected regions and cities, while others, including the Netherlands, recorded their first deaths from the virus this summer.

“I don’t think there are any more ‘tropical viruses’... the geographic barrier of these viruses no longer exists because of climate change,” said Dr Krishanthi Subramaniam, a microbiology lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

News.title: Britain pioneers new dried blood products for the modern battlefield
News.content:
A powdered blood product that can be mixed with water and used in minutes could help solve the challenges of treating severely wounded soldiers on hard-to-reach battlefields.

Britain is rethinking how to get blood to soldiers on the frontline, in the latest sign that the war in Ukraine has forced Western militaries to reconsider assumptions about modern combat medicine that had held since Iraq and Afghanistan.

The product, known as “spray-dried plasma”, is made by turning liquid plasma – the clotting-rich component of blood – into a stable powder that can be stored at room temperature for years before being rehydrated with water when needed.

“Plasma is vital for saving soldiers in war zones,” said Dr Ian Nesbitt, a former military anaesthetist and Faculty Lead for Anaesthesia at the David Nott Foundation, which trains doctors working in conflict zones.

“It helps blood clot when someone is injured. But in war zones, getting plasma to soldiers is incredibly complicated. It’s actually the logistics of it that are a real problem in maintaining a reliable supply of fresh frozen plasma for acutely injured patients.”

The NHS and the UK Ministry of Defence signed a strategic partnership this summer to jointly develop new blood products for frontline soldiers, focusing on dried plasma.

The agreement formalises work under way with a biotechnology company called Velico Medical. If successful, it will be used in future battlefields like the one in Ukraine.

“The war in Ukraine has woken up all countries, not just the UK,” Professor Renata Gomes, Chief Scientific Officer at NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT), told The Telegraph.

News.title: Mosquitoes are evolving to evade bed nets – but there may be a solution
News.content:
In Papua’s low-lying mangrove swamps and dense tropical rainforests, mosquitoes have always got to work early.

Here, the disease-ridden insects begin feeding in the early evening as people socialise and children play. It’s a characteristic that’s hampered malaria control efforts, because it has rendered bed nets less effective. People are bitten before they climb under the netting to sleep.

It’s also part of the reason that Indonesian Papua remains one of Asia’s most persistent malaria hotspots. Last year, cases across the country jumped by 30 per cent, to 706,000 new infections. The vast majority, roughly 90 per cent, were reported in Papua’s six provinces.

The same pattern is now emerging in parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where mosquitoes used to bite mostly at night and where the rollout of insecticide-treated bed nets is estimated to have averted 450 million malaria cases between 2000 and 2015, according to modelling in Nature journal.

A number of studies suggest mosquitoes in Africa are evolving in response to the mass rollout of bed nets, biting earlier in the evening, or later in the morning. In some cases, species which already did this have become more dominant, while others are adapting their habits.

“We’re battling evolution. And right now, we’re losing,” said Prof Neil Lobo, a research professor in the Eck Institute for Global Health at the University of Notre Dame.

“Mosquitoes are adapting. They’re biting outdoors, they’re biting earlier in the evening when people aren’t under their nets, and they’re becoming resistant to the insecticides we use. So we’re reaching the limits of what bed nets alone can do,” he told The Telegraph.

But there may be a solution.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

News.title: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal
News.content:
In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

News.title: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner
News.content:
Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Sports.title: Diletta Leotta puts on busty display in elegant black dress as she returns to screens for Champions League
Sports.content:
DILETTA LEOTTA has stunned fans with a busty display for her Champions League return.

The TV presenter and wife of former Liverpool star Loris Karius regularly wows her followers.



Diletta, 35, lives a glamorous lifestyle as a presenter for Dazn in Italy and as a model.

She has built up an enormous fanbase on Instagram with 9.4million followers.





Diletta’s recent post was no different ahead of her return to screens for the Champions League.

She treated fans to a glamorous look as she wore an elegant black button-up dress.

She shared the snaps on her Instagram account for her adoring followers.

She captioned the post: “Back to school.”



The post also included a glimpse of Diletta at work as she could be seen reading a script in the studio.

Fans loved the pictures as they flooded the comment section with praise for the presenter.



One commented: “Beautiful in black, tanned, the red lipstick suits you perfectly.”

A second posted: “Stunning beauty.”

A third wrote: “Mamma mia.”

A fourth said: “Gorgeous dress.”



Another added: “Best part of the Champions League right here.”

Diletta joined Dazn’s Serie A broadcast team in 2018, after previously working as a meteorologist for Sky Meteo24.

She married the now-Schalke goalkeeper Karius, 33, on the island of Sicily in June 2024, after two years of dating.

The wedding came less than one year after giving birth to their first child, before welcoming their second in May 2026.

Sports.title: Man Utd icon and BBC star opens up on living with Jason Statham at 17 before they became famous
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED icon Dion Dublin has opened up on living with Jason Statham as a teenager.

The unlikely duo lived together in Norfolk while Dublin, now 57, was coming through the Norwich academy.



He has explained that Statham, 59, was close friends with his brother, Ash, who worked as a DJ in Great Yarmouth, even playing in the same band together.

Dublin said to FourFourTwo: “I was a 17-year-old boy who would go and watch their band then I’d go watch my brother’s DJ sets with Jason, then me and J would go out after. It was good fun. Very chilled out.”



Former forward Dublin left Norwich for Cambridge United in 1988, making 156 appearances for the club, before a switch to Manchester United four years later.

He then established himself with moves to Coventry City and Aston Villa, eventually ending his career back where it started, as Dublin signed for Norwich in 2006.



But Statham was also a promising athlete during his time living with the Dublin brothers in Great Yarmouth.

The world famous movie star was a high diver and even competed for England at the 1990 Commonwealth Games in New Zealand.

And Dublin has recalled that the Norfolk coast was the perfect training venue with the former Team GB star frequenting a seafront leisure complex in Great Yarmouth.

The four-cap England international has also explained that Statham’s charisma was clear even as teenagers.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He told The Telegraph: “He didn’t try very hard to be cool, it was just him. You could imagine the reaction when he did his somersault.

“I used to get his flick-ons. Whatever girls Jason didn’t fancy, I’d be all over. They were great times. Amazing.”

Statham’s effortless coolness has resulted in him becoming one of Hollywood’s most marketable stars, with his movies grossing a staggering £6.3billion.

This includes a massive £1.12 billion coming from his role in 2015’s Furious 7.



Meanwhile, Dublin has forged a post-playing career on the small screen, initially working for Sky Sports before a move to the BBC.

Now Dublin has become a household name with his regular appearances on Match of the Day and Homes Under the Hammer.

Sports.title: Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle reveals which star he has fallen in ‘love’ with after hitting Man Utd with transfer blow
Sports.content:
MATTHIAS JAISSLE has fallen in “love” with Lewis Hall.

Manchester United have suffered a hammer blow with the news their top target to replace Luke Shaw has agreed a new five-year contract at Newcastle.



The 22-year-old left-back’s stunning form has been rewarded with the package making him one of the club’s top earners.

Hall missed out on the World Cup following a dip in form after being switched to right-back under previous boss Eddie Howe towards the end of last term.



But he has been one of the key men in new manager Jaissle’s unbeaten start at Newcastle.

The German said: “Without speaking about his contract, I can just say that I’m in love with what I’ve seen so far from him.

“It’s an amazing player with huge potential still, and this makes me so happy to, hopefully, have him here for the next few years and the long term.

“He’s fitting so good to this identity, how we want to play football, and again, he’s doing an excellent job.”

Another player Jaissle hopes to have long-term is Lukas Hornicek. The Czech Republic goalie, 24, arrived in a £25.7m deal from Portuguese club Braga just days before Jaissle took charge.

Hornicek has made 13 saves across his first three Premier League games, the joint-most in the top-flight along with Ipswich’s Kjell Scherpen.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The star is looking for a third clean sheet in Black and White at Leeds on Monday and Jaissle is delighted with what he has seen.

He said: “An amazing job so far. Amazing signing. A young lad as well. It’s not easy coming in the Premier League, performing already on a high level, dealing with the pressure. As a keeper, it’s something else as well.

“We are really pleased, and we hope that he can progress in the same way.



“I like him a lot as he’s so calm, but so mature as well. That gives the whole team this confidence.

“Having someone between the posts with that confidence and showing not even a sign of nervousness, that helps a lot.”

Meanwhile, Jaissle eased fears over fellow summer signing Amar Dedic’s injury. The right-back came off in the Carabao Cup win at Millwall with a hamstring issue but the Mags head coach says “it doesn’t look too serious”.

He added: “I treat these things really confidential, and I hope my staff too, and that nothing comes out. Because first of all, it’s about the player and it’s about his health.

“But what I said already after Millwall, it doesn’t look too serious.”

Sports.title: Europa League team forced to stay in another COUNTRY for Uefa match due to clash with major sporting event
Sports.content:
STADE RENNAIS have been forced to stay in Slovenia ahead of their Europa League clash against Austrian side Sturm Graz due to a lack of hotel rooms.

The French outfit travel to Austria next week for the opening match of their European campaign.



The team were due to book accommodation in the Austrian city of Graz just days before the game on September 16.

But according to French outlet L’Equipe, Rennais’ plans have been thrown into chaos after having difficulty finding a hotel nearby.



The situation has been caused by the MotoGP Grand Prix in Spielberg, which is just 75km away from the city.

And club chiefs have now decided to stay in a totally different country.

Rennais will stay in Maribor, Slovenia, which is only an hour’s drive away from Graz.

The team are set to be in Slovenia for three days before travelling just 69km to their European clash.

Rennais are then expected to fly back to Lyon for their next Ligue 1 game on September 19.

It wil be their first time in Slovenia since they beat NS Mura in the UEFA Conference League in 2021.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rennais are one of three French teams competing in the Europa League this season alongside Lyon and Marseille.

This is not the first time a team has had to make drastic changes to their plans in European competition this season.

Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk have been forced to change stadiums entirely for their Champions League campaign this season amid their country’s conflict with Russia.

Donestk are playing all their home games at Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge instead of their usual Donbas Arena.

They have been unable to play at their home ground since Russia’s invasion in 2022.

Sports.title: West Ham star Edson Alvarez issues lengthy statement denying his involvement after sensational claims of kidnap plot
Sports.content:
EDSON ALVAREZ has issued a lengthy statement denying sensational claims that he was involved in a kidnapping plot.

The midfielder has not played for West Ham since the first round of the Carabao Cup in August.



Alvarez, 28, has not featured for the club in the Championship and was expected to leave during the summer transfer window.

However, no move came to fruition for the Mexico international, who played at the World Cup.



Alvarez has now taken to social media to reject sensational allegations that he was connected to a kidnapping.

He has rejected the bombshell claims and insisted that the situation had “nothing” to do with him in a statement on social media.



He wrote: “In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly.

“I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me.

“Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.

“Until now, I had chosen not to respond.



“However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line.

“If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it.

“Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritises sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth.



“I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure.

“Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me.

“I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner’s father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported.

“Throughout nearly ten years of my professional career, I have made every effort to stay away from media scandals and to have my name recognised for my work both on and off the pitch.

“I come from a hardworking and honourable family that taught me that a reputation is built over many years through hard work, discipline, and conduct.



“For that very reason, I will not allow mine to be irresponsibly used to involve me in matters that are entirely unrelated to me.

“My priority is, and will continue to be, where it has always been: my daughters, my family, and my professional career.”

Alvarez joined West Ham in a £35million switch from Dutch giants Ajax in 2023.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He has played 74 times for the East London outfit but spent last season on loan at Fenerbahce.

The midfielder is the captain of the Mexico national team and has earned 103 caps.

Sports.title: Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel scores HAT-TRICK in Uefa Youth League debut in embarrassingly one-sided thrashing
Sports.content:
TEENAGE Manchester United superstar JJ Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut in a dominant 5-0 win against Sabah.

The 15-year-old scored once at the end of the first half and twice late in the match to sign off the win for United and become the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer in the competition.



Amir Ibragimov had put the Red Devils 1-0 up just two minutes into the match after tapping home a free kick from Jim Thwaites.

And Jacob Watson made it two by drilling the ball into the bottom-left corner from 12 yards out.



Man Utd completely dominated the match, with 44 total attempts on goal, 15 of which were on target.

The Red Devils also missed the target 13 times and had 16 shots blocked.

Meanwhile, Sabah failed to manage a single shot in the 90 minutes.

They also didn’t win a corner at Leigh Sports Village.

The result saw United jump straight up to third in the UEFA Youth League standings, only behind Paris Saint-Germain and Stuttgart after the opening match of the competition.

Gabriel is widely considered one of the best talents in the Man Utd academy.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

At just 15 years old, he could potentially make his Premier League debut with the senior squad this season.

Asked about his incredible rise last term, head coach Michael Carrick said: “JJ is a big talent, it’s pretty obvious to know that and he’s had a really good season for the Under-18s.

“We obviously think an awful lot of him, but patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and working with him in development as we do with all the different younger players and picking the right moment to step up.”

Gabriel enjoyed an impressive campaign for United’s U18s last season, scoring 28 goals in 35 appearances.

The forward has moved up to U21s this term and now plays Premier League 2 football.



He has already managed two goals and two assists in his first two outings.

Sports.title: England closing in on emphatic series sweep of Pakistan
Sports.content:
England are closing in on the most emphatic of series sweeps of Pakistan after reducing the visitors to 52-2 - still 268 runs behind - before rain ended play early on day two of the third Test at Edgbaston.

Pakistan's score at stumps actually represented somewhat of a recovery after their prospects looked even gloomier than the darkening skies overhead when reduced to 0-2 in Ollie Robinson's first over.

Robinson (2-10) saw off Saim Ayub first ball - the opener, one of four players flown straight into the team after seven were axed from the touring squad, out for a pair - before Abdullah Shafique also nicked to the slips three deliveries later.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson took two wickets for no runs in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings

It means that Robinson now has 28 wickets across his four Test appearances this summer, taking them at a staggering 7.75 apiece. In this series that improves even further to 6.66.

Joe Root's grab at slip to send back Shafique moved him one clear of Australia's Steve Smith and onto 220 in their personal battle to claim the most catches by an outfielder in Test cricket.

The clatter of wickets didn't follow as it had in Pakistan's first innings, with Azan Awais (29no) and Shan Masood (21no) sharing a fifty stand before the rain arrived - albeit Masood was put down on 13 by Ben Duckett, his third spill of the Test, off the unfortunate Gus Atkinson.

Brook, Lawrence and Smith all miss out with Test tons looming

Earlier, England were bowled out for 452, earning a 320-run lead on first innings as Dan Lawrence (65), Jamie Smith (69) and Robinson (50) added half-centuries to those notched by Emilio Gay (60) and Harry Brook (75) on day one.

Brook added 23 to his overnight total before he was the first wicket to fall on the second morning, just at the point where he and Dan Lawrence - who had stormed through to a 47-ball fifty - had seemingly broken Pakistan's spirits with 73 scored off the opening 10 overs of the day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook spurned his chance of making a century as he ran himself out on 75 while England built a first-innings lead over Pakistan

The breakthrough was a gift, Brook practically running himself out as he called for a risky single to midwicket, where Masood did the honours with a direct hit.

The scoring didn't slow as Smith joined Lawrence at the crease, the pair putting on 64 together before Lawrence was left kicking himself as he chopped one from Mohammad Imran (2-47) back onto his stumps just before lunch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence couldn't hide his fury after knocking the ball onto his own stumps

Smith was the next through to fifty - off 54 balls - but failed to convert as, after Gus Atkinson (19) was bowled by a beauty from Imran, Smith chipped one back to the fired-up Razaullah (4-148).

While he was okay to bat, Smith would later be absent from the field - Jordan Cox subbing in at wicketkeeper - with the regular gloveman nursing an injured finger from the first day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A fiery Razaullah gave a strong celebration after he caught and bowled Jamie Smith

Robinson, hitting a second Test half-century, and Jofra Archer (32no) had some fun lower down the order, finding the boundary - or clearing it - with regularity as England pushed their total above 400 and lead beyond 300 before the innings was finally ended.

Pakistan carried their increasingly timid approach in the field over into the start of their second innings, and a two-day finish briefly looked a possibility after Robinson's double strike in the first over, before Azan and Masood showed some much-needed resilience and the rain intervened.

Nasser: Ayub shouldn't be here

Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain:

"Saim Ayub, in particular, struggled. The truth is he shouldn't be here. He came from the CPL [Caribbean Premier League] and hasn't played first-class cricket in some time.

"I don't know who thinks it's the right thing to fly someone over from foreign conditions, and think they'll be fine in these conditions against a Duke's ball and Ollie Robinson's bowling attack?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain labelled Pakistan’s selection of Saim Ayub as a ‘disrespect for Test Match cricket’ after they flew out the batsman for his first class game in 11 months, just 10 days after playing in the CPL

"The players who are here, their friends and room-mates have been axed. People who have got five-fors have been axed.

"How you treat players is so important. It's a two-way thing when players are presented with a Test cap. You're expected to meet the core values of representing Pakistan, but the team needs to look after the players in return.

"That goes the moment you send seven people home. People start looking after themselves. Why should I bother about a team that doesn't bother about me and has sent my team-mates home between Tests?

"This Pakistan side, not only are they in poor form, they look like a team that says, 'what will be, will be', and just looks after itself."

Sports.title: Verstappen: New Madring circuit 'probably a car killer'
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen says the new Madring F1 circuit is "probably a car killer" with several drivers expecting a disruptive Spanish Grand Prix weekend.

The close proximity of the walls at the high-speed track, which includes a big banked corner in the middle sector, was the big talk of the paddock on Thursday.

It means Friday's practice sessions at 12.30pm and 4pm, live on Sky Sports F1, will be more important than usual so the drivers can get up to speed around the challenging circuit.

"It's a tough track. For me, what I feel while driving, it's a little bit the same kind of sensation that I get sometimes around Jeddah in places," said Verstappen.

"Of course, Jeddah is faster on average with the corners, but the walls are quite similar in how they are positioned.

"It's going to be tough. I think when F3 were testing here there were a lot of shunts, so it's not an easy track, easy to make a mistake also with the layout of the track. The kerbs that are there, we need to run over a few of them, and that's normally not the strong point of our car, but we will try to do the best we can."

Asked if it was a car killer, Verstappen added: "It probably is a car killer from what I've seen so far but you just need to try and stay out of the walls and try to get the best possible feeling in the car. When you're confident in the car on a street circuit it helps a lot."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oracle Red Bull Racing swapped the asphalt for the underground, as the iconic RB8 took to the tracks of the Madrid Metro in a first-of-its-kind stunt

Last month, a two-day Formula 3 test took place at the Madring and there were 19 red flags, mostly for crashes at several areas of the track.

Williams' Carlos Sainz, who has given some input into the circuit design, says the track is "different to what we're used to".

"Realistically speaking, it's going to be now tomorrow in FP1 when we really know what this track is all about. And I'm going to say it looks different," he said.

"It looks that the track has character, that it's charismatic, with a lot of different kinds of corners."

Image: The Madring F1 track layout (Credit: F1)

Most risky circuit on the calendar?

Qualifying is expected to be pivotal due to the difficulty of overtaking as most corners only have one racing line, so the drivers will be keen to push the limits come Saturday afternoon, even if it means taking huge risks.

Last week's shock pole-sitter Pierre Gasly believes it will create "huge adrenaline" for the drivers.

"The track layout is something I've never seen before. You have these crazy corners, blind corners, a huge banking," said the Alpine driver.

"It took me a few laps in the sim to get my head around what's where. It's very challenging because everything is twisty. I'm excited. I expect a really hectic weekend with lots of disruption and mistakes and we will have to make sure we are on the right side of it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The F1 review the new Madring track!

It will be particularly important for the championship contenders to keep out of the barriers so they don't lose big points to their rivals.

After his spectacular Monza win, Kimi Antonelli leads George Russell by 66 points in the Drivers' Championship, Lewis Hamilton by 76 points and Lando Norris by 96 points.

"It's a crazy circuit. I would put it as arguably the most risky circuit of the whole calendar because you have real high-speed corners, sort of Jeddah-esque. The walls are very close, so there's no margin for error," said Russell.

"But then you have other corners that are quite like Baku, where you're coming from a high speed into a slow braking zone, you're braking and turning at the same time, so locking tyres is going to be easy. And if you lock up, you'll be straight in the wall."

Image: Despite its tightness, the Turn 5 chicane is one of the few overtaking spots at the Madring

Hamilton added: "There's probably some similarities with these kerbs compared to somewhere like Montreal where you saw obviously Mercedes was very quick, but there was a lot more straights there as well.

"It's a massively challenging circuit. Of all the new tracks that I've gone to, this one, maybe Saudi, are the two closest in terms of how difficult it was to get on top of the car and find the right lines etc."

Sports.title: Can 'polarising' Hurts win over Eagles critics?
Sports.content:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts enters the 2026 NFL season facing more question marks than ever before, believes Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds.

The Eagles leaned heavily on Vic Fangio's star-studded defense alongside a sputtering Hurts-led attack on the way to winning the NFC East title last season.

It would culminate in a playoff defeat to the San Francisco 49ers and the firing of offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo, while a disgruntled AJ Brown departed in the offseason after an apparent breakdown in his connection with Hurts both on and off the field.

"Only Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have accounted for more offensive touchdowns than Jalen Hurts in the last five years," said Reynolds on Inside the Huddle.

"He's a Super Bowl MVP, but those whispers about how he can impact the offense, how he gets along with his team-mates, all of that's grown about as loud as it's ever been during this offseason, about how he can run an offense, what he can do, what his limitations are."

Hurts was named Super Bowl MVP after a commanding performance to lead the Eagles to victory over the Kansas City Chiefs two years ago, denying Andy Reid's side a historic three-peat.

Still, doubts of his talents would follow amid a laboured 2025 campaign.

"It's hard, I think he can be a polarizing character at times because he's actually just so stoic throughout or almost maintains the same emotions. And people want to see him get happy or mad or anything like that," said Sky Sports NFL's Phoebe Schecter.

"I feel like there's so much of other people applying how they feel he should think or feel. Then you have people looking at his career in terms of criticising the run game, criticising his passing game, criticising who he throws the football to, and Philadelphia is not an easy place to play.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Inside The Huddle podcast Neil Reynolds, Jeff Reinebold and Phoebe Schecter give their predictions on who will make the Super Bowl in 2027

"We know that there's a lot of external pressure from the Eagles fans, whether you're winning or losing, but it feels like a team that has consistently been driven by what the outside noise wants, or maybe the coordinators are allowing that to happen where they think, 'oh, they think we need to pass it to this person, they think we should throw it'.

"It almost just needs all those doors shut, which is probably why Jalen Hurts is very much like that. Even spending time with him this offseason he pretty much is exactly the same. He doesn't really get too excited.

"It will be fascinating now, is it that addition by subtraction when it comes to AJ Brown, what does the offense look like?"

Hurts and the Eagles begin their season against another quarterback facing queries in the light of a disappointing campaign marred by injury.

Jayden Daniels missed 10 games for the Washington Commanders last season, failing to build on his Offensive Rookie of the Year-winning campaign.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Inside the Huddle podcast, Neil Reynolds and Phoebe Schecter examine whether the Broncos are ready to mount a genuine Super Bowl challenge

"He told me in the summer he was going to learn to live to fight another down," said Reynolds. "I will believe it when I see it, once you get in the heat of the battle.

"There's a lot of questions about Jayden Daniels, because if he's healthy, let's not forget two seasons ago, they were in the NFC championship game against these very Eagles."

Schecter added: "Jayden Daniels is so fascinating because he does have such a slim fit frame and we've seen how that can have a negative impact, but we've also seen how his speed and athleticism has really helped the team at times is evasive moves in the pocket, or even just when he's scrambling or running down field.

"And then you've got on top of it, the amount of off-field work that he does from a preparation perspective. The extra meetings that he's doing in the morning to walk through the play script or the virtual reality that he's watching, not every quarterback does that.

"Its just making sure that his offensive line can protect him long enough against an Eagles defense and especially an Eagles defensive line that are just known for their aggression."

Sports.title: Musical Times 6/1 for 1000 Guineas after May Hill romp at Doncaster
Sports.content:
Musical Times burst into the next year's Classic picture with a wide-margin victory in the Betfred May Hill Stakes at Doncaster.

Winner of her first two races at Newmarket and Yarmouth, she had not done anything to suggest she was about to blow a Group Two field wide apart.

Travelling strongly in the hands of William Buick, the Charlie Appleby-trained 7-4 favourite shot clear over a furlong out and the race was over.

The daughter of Lope De Vega pulled a yawning seven-and-a-half lengths clear clear of Scommessa Sicura, who was only a neck behind the winner on her debut, in second.

Appleby said: "Delighted. Coming into the race I wouldn't say I was trying to sit on the fence, but she shows so much natural pace at home, I thought 'I hope she stays'. She should stay on pedigree but everything at home has been very zippy and we saw that through the race today.

"She's handled everything and the race was faultless, wasn't it? There was a nice pace on, she travelled into it, travelled up to leaders well and most importantly she accelerated, which is what you always like to see.

"We'll head to the Fillies' Mile, which was always our pencil plan since Yarmouth really."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Newmarket's Fillies' Mile is the next target for Musical Times after she made light work of the Group Two May Hill Stakes at Doncaster.

Paddy Power initially cut Musical Times to 12-1 from 25s for next year's 1000 Guineas, but that did not last long and neither did 8-1, with the firm eventually forced to make her their 6-1 favourite.

"She's handled that slightly slower ground today but she's a neat filly, so if it came up quick at Newmarket in the autumn or in the spring it wouldn't worry me," the trainer added.

"I don't see why she shouldn't be a Guineas filly. We won this a couple of years ago with Desert Flower, who went on to win the Guineas. Funnily enough I see this filly as more of a Guineas filly than Desert Flower, who was a big and scopey and unfortunately didn't quite win the Oaks."

Sports.title: De Zerbi 'was the key' - Fernandes on his Spurs switch and trophy ambitions
Sports.content:
Spurs may have failed to win any of their first three Premier League games this season, but summer signing Matheus Fernandes is convinced he has joined a squad set to start fighting for trophies.

The £85m midfielder was wanted by a list of clubs after impressing for West Ham last season, with Man Utd keen on a deal but ultimately unable to go head-to-head with Spurs on the fee.

For Fernandes, it was his conversations with head coach Roberto De Zerbi which persuaded him the north London project was for him.

"I spoke with the Mister and he was the key for this decision," Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of the Saturday Night Football clash with Everton.

"You can feel when you speak with him, the energy, the passion about football.

"He spoke with me, he spoke with my dad, he spoke with my mum. So it was not just about me, it was about the people around me. He said to my dad, 'we'll take care' [of] me.

"He's a top manager. You can feel on the pitch, off the pitch as well. And I'm very happy to work with him."

Tottenham Hotspur

Everton Saturday 12th September 5:00pm Kick off 5:30pm

Fernandes made his feelings for De Zerbi clear to the Spurs boss himself when the deal was done.

"The first day of the pre-season, I met him and he was very happy. I was very happy as well for playing for him. I said, 'Look, I chose Tottenham because one of the biggest parts was you'."

It wasn't just De Zerbi's way with words. The Italian's style of football also impressed Fernandes. "For me as a midfielder, I like so much," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Nottingham Forest’s match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

Fernandes believes the quality of the Spurs squad can raise his own level of performance, too.

"I believe that I can be a much better player than I was last season," said the 22-year-old Portuguese, who recorded three goals and four assists in the Premier League for the Hammers.

"If you look at the squad, it's a big team with big players, important players, players with experience, players with a lot of quality. So, when you play with better players, I think you play better. So, I believe that I can be much better."

Spurs' players have been unable to turn that perception into more than one point so far. But, despite substantial criticism in the early weeks of the season, Fernandes is full of belief the team will soon start to prove their doubters wrong - and deliver in a significant way.

"I know what it's like: when you win, you are the best. When you lose, you are the worst," he said.

"We just focus on us. If you believe in the club, if you believe in the manager, you know that you need to take some time to learn the timings, everything tactical, and when you arrive there, it's like ketchup. It starts spilling."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Michael Bridge shares the latest from Tottenham Hotspur's training as both Richarlison and James Maddison return but Mykhailo Mudryk is sidelined for 'six-eight weeks'.

Fernandes' first two seasons in English football have ended in relegation, at Southampton and then West Ham. But he is at Tottenham to win.

"This is one of the reasons that I came here, to play for winning something," he said.

"We want to win the games, we want to fight for the titles and, with this squad, it's normal that we want to fight for the titles.

"Now, we didn't win the last three games, so things need to calm. We need to take time. And then, like I said, it's like ketchup, when you win one game, it's going to be more easy."

Fernandes, his Spurs colleagues and the club's supporters will hope that starts on Saturday.

Sports.title: Manchester United v Sabah: Champions League – live
Sports.content:
We live in a world eager to issue commands about all the things we need – chief among them money, not one we often contest. But it is unarguably the case that the world’s resources are bountiful enough for every person in it to live in comfort and luxury … if only our species was pleasant enough to deem that essential.

The problem is that for some people, it’s not about having, but about having more. Take Manchester United, for example: we’re currently being told that they need to be in the Champions League because the financial disadvantage of being out of it is so extreme that it’s impossible for them to compete with the clubs that are involved.

This is not so because, rather like planet earth – yes, here cometh the segue – Manchester United possesses the means to sustain itself. Rather what Manchester United need is owners who don’t sequester sizeable chunks of what it generates for their own selfish ends.

It does, though, remain the case that for reasons emotional and mythological, well enough known not to require enumerating here, Manchester United need to be in the Champions League. Well, here they are.

And they have the players to do something. They’ve made a spotty start in the league, but despite conceding an injury-time equaliser at Everton last weekend, the game contained more positives than negatives, the team still settling into a style of play intended to be dominant and controlled, in the aftermath of a World Cup summer, with their big midfield signing still injured.

All that will cost them in the league, so too the failure or inability to reinforce the defence. But provided they can stay in this competition into the new year – something that’s often been beyond them in the Post-Fergie Wilderness YearsTM – they ought by then to have a method which suits knockout football, and already no longer have André Onana in net, chucking them in as fast as they can be scored.

In the meantime, though, there’s a league out of which they need to get – created, by amazing coincidence, because for some, it’s not about having but about having more.

Sports.title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support
Sports.content:
The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election.

The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash.

During the World Cup the suspension of the US forward Folarin Balogun was overturned by Fifa after lobbying from Donald Trump. The US president said he called Infantino to recommend that Balogun be allowed to play. Fifa has said the decision taken by its disciplinary committee was “a balanced measure” and “based on an explicit provision of the applicable regulations”.

Diallo outlined the reasons for the loss in confidence: “From July onwards, the conditions which led to us to support his candidacy had been disrupted. Does the withdrawal of the [sell-off] project solve the issue? I don’t think so. His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”

Diallo said of the initial decision to support Infantino: “It would be wrong to say that certain developments in football were not made under his mandate.” But he added: “When you are making changes to the game itself, in a unilateral and opaque fashion to sell our shared asset, that changes our appreciation.

“France is one of the founding members of Fifa, and as such we have a historical legitimacy to intervene when we feel that Fifa and its president are deviating from our vision of how world football should be run. We also have sporting legitimacy, as one of the top three teams in the world rankings over the last 10 years. We wanted to make it clear that we refuse to go in a direction which does not correspond to the general interest of our sport.”

When reports of the sell-off project came to light, the FFF expressed “doubts and deep concerns”. Uefa threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions and several European countries, including Wales and England, withdrew their support for Infantino but the FFF had not until Thursday publicly disavowed him.

Diallo indicated France would play an active part in Uefa’s search for an alternative candidate for the Fifa presidency before the 18 November deadline. The election will take place in March during Fifa’s next congress.

Before then, Diallo said, the FFF would reach out to figures it considers experts in “transparency and good governance” in football and beyond as part of France’s “contribution to the debate”, as it pushes for “far-reaching reform” of Fifa.

He cited Kevin Lamour, the former Fifa chief operating officer who was dismissed after criticising the sell-off plan, as one of the people the FFF would look to consult.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Mauricio Pochettino, Tottenham’s game of thrones and retrospective action
Sports.content:
ER, MEMORY LANE?

State-sanctioned execution of spouses and allies (Henry VIII), the Marian persecutions (Mary I), and enslavement and branding of the unemployed (Edward VI). During the 15th and 16th centuries, assorted monarchs from the House of Tudor were responsible for visiting no end of dread and terror on their subjects but it is the 44-day reign of one of their more contemporary counterparts at Tottenham that local subjects found truly unforgivable. Enthroned last February to secure Spurs’ safety following the dismissal of Thomas Frank, Igor Tudor took just one point from 15 available in his five top-flight games in charge. His subsequent deposition heralded the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi and ultimately last-day Premier League survival, but may also have denied the club’s fans a reunion with Mauricio Pochettino, a comparatively beloved former monarch who was tasked with focusing on other conquests in the Americas at the time.

“The problem was that the timings were never the best,” tooted Poch of the game of thrones played out in the kingdoms of the Seven Sisters and the New World that he claims dashed his hopes of coaching at the Geopolitics World Cup and then returning to a club he had managed for more than five years. “When I was free, I never received a contact. And then when I was working [with USA USA USA], I received a contact but I cannot make the decision to come back. It was a little bit unlucky. Maybe one day the stars will align and it can happen. If I was free, of course, I come. But I wasn’t free.” Having since signed a new four-year deal, he remains with the USA USA USA, while De Zerbi is tied to Spurs until 2031. Or possibly November.

A man who famously keeps a bowl of lemons in the office to help soak up negative energy, Pochettino might have needed several silos of the citrus fruit if things had worked out differently and he’d returned to coach a Spurs side muddying their spats in the Championship. However, it is a role the former manager of Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea insists he would not have considered beneath him. “Tottenham … it’s the only club that always I am open to help in whatever division,” he cooed, when quizzed about his appetite for the grind of midweek trips to Lincoln City, Bolton and Stoke.

In a wide-ranging interview staged in That There Big London to mark the beginning of his second cycle as USA USA USA head coach, Pochettino stated that Chelsea should be stripped of the Premier League title they won in 2016-17, having since been found guilty of multiple and serious financial shenanigans at that time. As luck would have it, in such a scenario the honour would almost certainly be bestowed on a Spurs side that finished second in the league that season and happened to be coached by him. “If that [Chelsea’s chicanery] was true, then we deserve to be champions that year, for sure,” he parped. “They were punished, they admitted it? So that’s it. The title should be for the team that was second.” While Poch might well have an excellent point, Football Daily can’t say we recall him being such a stickler for the fastidious application of the rules when his USA USA USA team’s star striker had a ban controversially shelved by Fifa following the intervention of Donald Trump at the recent GWC.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Daniel Harris from 8pm BST for hot Bigger Cup minute-by-minute coverage of Manchester United 2-0 Mr Loverman Sabah ! Sabah! .

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“At that time it was quite big money. I could have bought a flat in my home town; it was a very difficult period there and they were almost free. But my plan was to go to England and follow my dream to become a coach, and that’s how it started” – Valdas Dambrauskas gets his very entertaining chat on with Nick Ames about his remarkable journey from an appearance on the Lithuanian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? via pub work in north London, to becoming manager of Azerbaijani champions Sabah.

View image in fullscreen Valdas Dambrauskas there. Photograph: Aziz Karimov/Getty Images

double quotation mark Given that Mauricio Pochettino believes the Premier League title shouldn’t go to the club that finished first in the table, he truly is a Spurs manager at heart. And, given he also says that if he were Chelsea manager at the time, he’d admit that ‘we don’t deserve the title because we broke the rules’, it also conclusively proves he was the completely wrong man for Chelsea” – Noble Francis.
