Sports.title: Why Kai Havertz’s dummy was perhaps more pleasing than a Lionel Messi waltz | Max Rushden
Sports.content:
During Covid, when sport was back but behind closed doors, I hosted a number of strange online shows to fill the void of real life. The highlight was chatting to Darren Gough about a lifesize bronze rhinoceros for 45 minutes to 15 small boxes on a Zoom call. I don’t recall who it was for and where the rhinoceros came from – but it might be in his garden.

I ended up doing virtual pre-match corporate Zoom calls for Heineken before Europa League games. It was the wifi version of Club Wembley: a Q&A happening on stage between a generic host and some random ex-pro while you’re trying to chat to your mate and eat an unidentified square of meat with some dauphinoise potatoes.

I’d be in my little square talking to Luis García in his little square about the ghost goal while an assorted group of faces and living rooms or kitchen tables would stare at you, perhaps interested, perhaps not. Did they even want to be there? Were we on mute while someone from marketing was filling a spare box on my laptop watching Death In Paradise on the TV behind me?

Certainly it was hard to create an amazing vibe with Mark van Bommel while his internet connection crashed and a little note on a Google doc appeared telling me to fill for 25 minutes with my favourite memories of the Europa League. Did these disembodied heads in front of me want the deep dive they got on Tony Parks’ heroics in 1984? How many of them knew about Gary Mabbutt playing centre mid and marking Enzo Scifo out of the game?

One of the guests was Dimitar Berbatov. You’d log on half an hour before the show and say hello, try to build some kind of electric rapport with a man in Bulgaria (I think) presumably looking to get in and get out and get back on with whatever social distancing life in Sofia had to offer.

He may have not had Akabusi levels of energy, and his economy of language was not unlike his playing style – why use a hundred words when one will do? But he was into it and did the job perfectly. I absolutely loved Berbatov as a player. Watching him pluck a goalkick out of the sky was more beautiful than watching a lot of other players banging one in from 25 yards. There’s a YouTube video called Dimitar Berbatov – the most underrated first touch ever? It begins with him standing like a lamp-post on the halfway line at Craven Cottage and stopping a crossfield ball stone dead like it’s an anvil.

View image in fullscreen Dimitar Berbatov, pictured scoring for Manchester United against Sunderland in 2009, could make football look easy. Photograph: Carl Recine/Action Images/Reuters

Back to the Zoom call: I welcome Dimitar, he says hello, I explain my admiration for him, and then say to him that he made football look easy. Did he find it easy? “Yes” he replied. Totally matter of fact. Not trying to impress – just explaining that football was easy.

And for someone like Berbatov, it is a different level to “good touch for a big man”. This is the ultimate type of grace on a football pitch. And perhaps it is reserved for tall, skilful players. I’ve probably used the word languid already but I can’t think of any other use of the word – reserved for players who are almost balletic.

Is it insane to say it’s more aesthetically pleasing than seeing a Messi or a Maradona waltz through a defence? It almost feels as if a low centre of gravity gives you an unfair advantage when it comes to technical skill. No flailing arms and legs to get in the way of you being naturally brilliant.

View image in fullscreen Argentina’s Lionel Messi dribbles away from three Dutch players in the 2022 World Cup. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

My biased brain instantly goes to Glenn Hoddle walking through the Oxford United defence with one sway, sitting the keeper down with a movement of the leg. It’s all saying: “This is easier for me than it is for you.”

Which brings us to Kai Havertz – and that dummy against Chelsea. The more and more football becomes that David Mitchell sketch, the more surprised I am that there are still moments in a game that lead to some involuntary noise from deep within.

The ball from Christos Tzolis is definitely for him. Havertz points in front to where he wants the ball. If it’s played there he can probably get a shot away first time. But when it comes, controlling the ball would have been a sensible choice. Back to goal. He could have turned and shot, or just kept the ball. There are lots of good players to pass it to.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard scores Arsenal’s second goal against Chelsea after Kai Havertz’s dummy. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Even the way he lifts his left leg at the last second to let the ball run through to Martin Ødegaard is delightful. It’s easy to forget the pace of the game at this level. And when you’re watching on TV where it’s much easier to see the pass you also forget these guys don’t have that view.

Someone somewhere will have done a report on Havertz’s scanning abilities. He doesn’t appear to look behind to check where Ødegaard is. But awareness is hard to calculate. He just knows. And he does it all in a split second, not even. How wonderful that you can do so much without even touching the ball.

A lot of people do quite well out of repeatedly asking whether Arsenal need a centre-forward, so I don’t want to do them out of work. And Havertz isn’t perfect – he isn’t Robbie Fowler in the box. But he has scored in two Champions League finals. He did win the league last season. A lot of beautiful graceful players tend to be beautiful and graceful without delivering on the biggest occasions. Havertz does both. And when he gets it right, it looks easy to him. Imagine finding it easy.

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister makes his point as Liverpool fight back to defeat Atlético
Sports.content:
It was the time and place for Alexis Mac Allister to do his talking on the pitch and the disgruntled Liverpool midfielder delivered on cue. “Very sad” over Liverpool’s refusal to offer him a new contract, while Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch were getting theirs, Mac Allister made Anfield very happy with a match-winning display against Atlético Madrid.

The Argentina international, one of five World Cup finalists involved in an absorbing, delicately-poised contest, vented his frustrations in the best possible and most professional way – from behind an immaculate 20-yard strike into Jan Oblak’s goal rather than a microphone. Mac Allister believes he is playing for a new deal this season and promised to give “100% to my last day” at the pre-match press conference. He was true to his word to extend Atlético’s winless sequence against English opposition in the Champions League league phase to 11 matches.

For Andoni Iraola, it was the perfect start to life as a Champions League coach after an imperfect start to the game. Diego Simeone’s switch to a 3-5-2 formation caught Liverpool cold and it was only when they regrouped in the aftermath of Marcos Llorente’s latest Anfield goal, and again during the half-time interval, that their performance level improved. Mac Allister’s timely moment, Alexander Isak’s relentless industry, Florian Wirtz’s creativity and another performance of drive and intelligence from Szoboszlai ensured the Liverpool head coach had plenty to savour.

“I have to blame myself a bit for the start of the game,” Iraola said. “Atlético surprised us with the way they approached the game. They haven’t used that system too much this season and it’s difficult if you are not ready for it, but we adjusted and played better. In the second half we were the best team. We came back for the third time [this season] and that showed the players are pushing and they have character.”

It was a night of firsts. Iraola coached a Champions League game for the first time in his career – he did take charge of 12 Europa League matches with AEK Larnaca in 2018-19 – Bradley Barcola made his first Liverpool start following a £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain and Julián Álvarez was in Atlético’s starting lineup for the first time this season since his failed attempt to join Barcelona. All appeared to have been forgiven – for now at least – as his name was cheered by the small pocket of Atlético fans when the teams were announced before kick-off and he repaid them by creating the opening goal.

View image in fullscreen Dominik Szoboszlai scores Liverpool’s equaliser late in the first half. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Llorente was the scourge of Anfield yet again when Álvarez threaded a pass behind the home defence and the right wing-back raced clear on goal. The man who named his dog Anfield after scoring twice to eliminate Jürgen Klopp’s team from the competition in 2020, in the game played while Madrid was in lockdown from the Covid pandemic, lofted a confident finish beyond Alisson. It was Llorente’s fifth goal at Anfield, half of his entire total of Champions League goals. He had been kept onside by Milos Kerkez, who endured a poor night with his positioning and distribution before atoning with a key role in Liverpool’s equaliser.

Álvarez almost doubled the visitors’ lead when granted far too much time and space to take aim from almost 30 yards. Alisson, at full stretch, intervened with a superb finger-tip save. Anfield was growing restless at Liverpool’s carelessness on the ball and Atlético’s comfort on it. But the threat and control from the hosts increased.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wirtz drew a fine save from Oblak at the end of a flowing move involving Barcola and Isak. Liverpool then drew level thanks to tenacity from Kerkez, a lovely touch from Ronald Araújo and Szoboszlai’s instinctive finish. The left-back won possession with a clean, crunching challenge on Lee Kang-in before finding Barcola. The France international was denied a goal on his full debut by Oblak’s low save but Wirtz kept the pressure on and Szoboszlai, having been halted on the edge of the area, got a second bite from Araújo’s clever flick. The midfielder’s first time shot sailed into the far corner.

Barcola should have put Liverpool ahead when played through on goal by Wirtz early in the second half. The winger had time to measure the finish but pulled it wide of Oblak’s right-hand post. He would later depart with cramp. Liverpool were ahead one minute later when the lively Rio Ngumoha beat Llorente and his cross fell to Mac Allister via a deflection off Isak. Mac Allister told Szoboszlai to leave the ball and drilled home an unstoppable left-footed drive from 20 yards. Atlético remained dangerous and the introduction of Ademola Lookman added an extra dimension to the visitors’ attack but Liverpool defended impressively to secure a deserved victory.

Sports.title: Champions League roundup: Raphinha shines as Barcelona thrash Feyenoord
Sports.content:
Raphinha let his goals do the talking after being omitted from the Ballon d’Or shortlist, striking twice as Barcelona eased to a 5-1 win over Feyenoord in the Champions League.

The Brazilian was a surprise omission from this week’s 30-strong list of candidates for the prestigious award but brushed any disappointment aside to continue his early season hot streak at a rain-soaked Camp Nou. The forward finished brilliantly in the third minute and added a second just before the hour mark to down the Eredivisie side and take his tally to eight goals in six outings at the start of the campaign.

The summer signing Karim Adeyemi produced a stunning finish, Lamine Yamal stroked a free-kick through a gap in the Dutch wall and recent arrival Gabriel Jesus opened his account for the club just two minutes after stepping off the bench.

There was little to celebrate for Giovanni van Bronckhorst on his Barça return but Sem Steijn gave the visiting fans something to enjoy when he poked in at far post late on.

“The most important thing is we are playing like a team, like one unit,” the Barcelona head coach, Hansi Flick, said. “We controlled the game, we are dominant and this is fantastic to see. This is our style and how we want to play.”

Ferran Torres scored a hat-trick and Ousmane Dembélé also starred as Paris Saint-Germain began their quest to win a third successive Champions League title by thrashing Slovan Bratislava 6-1 at the Parc des Princes.

View image in fullscreen Paris Saint-Germain’s Ferran Torres celebrates scoring their fifth goal with Ousmane Dembélé. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters

Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembélé had scored twice by the midway point of the first half in the French capital, and then set up Spain’s World Cup final hero Torres to make it 3-0 by the interval.

Torres, a close-season signing from Barcelona, added two more just after the restart to complete his hat-trick before the hour mark, with Suleiman Camara pulling one back for the Slovakian champions and Fabián Ruiz then sealing PSG’s win.

Elsewhere, Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic struck a 12-minute first-half hat-trick to ⁠earn ⁠a ​3-1 victory over Viking Stavanger.

He opened the ​scoring after 20 minutes with a touch at the near post, but Viking, making their first appearance in the league phase of the Champions League, were level two minutes later when Zlatko Tripic finished a ⁠swift counter-attack with his left foot.

Demirovic quickly re-established the lead ​in the ​26th minute and then completed ​the hat-trick with a hooked volley six minutes later. “For me personally it was the perfect start and also for the team as a whole,” Demirovic told Dazn.

Quick Guide Championship: Ten-man West Brom win at Derby to go top Show West Bromwich Albion held on for a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park, after playing for more than an hour with 10 men. Aune Heggebø's early goal proved enough to take the Baggies top of the table, despite Brayann Pereira being dismissed on his debut after collecting two first-half yellow cards. Derby had started the stronger, but West Brom swept downfield to score in the 16th minute, Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipping in a low cross from the left which Heggebø [pictured] finished at the near post. The visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute, as he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor. The hosts went close just before half-time when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in. Derby should have levelled in the 68th minute but Lars-Jørgen Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward’s cross. Late on, Nat Phillips made a great clearance after a late goalmouth scramble, summing up a performance full of grit and resolve. James Morrison's side move above West Ham to top the Championship table with 13 points from six games. Either Charlton or QPR could have joined them on 13 points, but the sides played out a stalemate at the Valley. Derby, meanwhile, slipped into the bottom three with their fourth defeat in six games. Norwich moved up to ninth in the table as they edged past visitors Birmingham 2-1 to make it three wins in four league games. Oscar Schwartau's screamer opened the scoring, the young Dane lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle from 25 yards out. Papa Diallo's first goal for the Canaries doubled their advantage before the break, as the Senegal winger sidefooted home from Andre Brooks' cross. Carlos Vicente pulled a goal back for the visitors, but wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies’ men suffered their first league defeat this season. Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Sporting, quarter-finalists last season for the first time since 1983, fought back to see off Galatasaray 3-1 in Lisbon.

Galatasaray took an early lead through Gonçalo Inacio’s own goal but Geny ​Catamo punished poor defending to equalise in the 27th minute. Luis Suárez converted a 57th-minute penalty to put Sporting ahead and a blistering free kick from Rodrigo Zalazar six minutes later sealed the win.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer powers Chelsea to comeback win over Leeds in nine-goal epic
Sports.content:
Where’s the fun in doing it the easy way? Chelsea remain chaotic at the back but can drag their opponents into horrible places. It helps, mind you, to have some assistance from the referee. Jarred Gillett and Cole Palmer? They made for a killer combination as Chelsea swerved embarrassment and treated Stamford Bridge to one of life’s rarities: a classic in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Gillett, a referee who always seems to be guessing when he makes key calls, was the villain as far as Leeds were concerned. They had just gone 2-0 up when Gillett altered the flow of the tie by pointing to the spot after Pep Chavarría made the most of slight contact from Daniel James. The subsequent conversion from Palmer was inevitable and from there so was the comeback from Chelsea, who rattled through four goals in 12 minutes before eventually reaching the last 16 by winning 6-3.

It made little sense. It could have gone down as Xabi Alonso’s first misjudgment as Chelsea’s manager. The Carabao Cup is important given the Spaniard’s side are not in Europe, but his rotation almost backfired. Chelsea were shambolic after making nine changes – the 16-year-old debutant Reggie Watson was overrun in midfield while Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens struggled in attack – and Alonso was in emergency mode when he made a quadruple change at half-time.

“I take responsibility,” Alonso said. “No player is to blame. It’s the decisions we took. When you don’t have this time to work with them, it’s difficult to compete at this level. I need to take my own blame for the things that happen. I need to be able to help them better. They are not responsible. After you need to react and think what’s better for the team.”

Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Equally Alonso can take credit for responding. His moves were decisive. Reece James offered security after replacing Watson and Pedro Neto scored after coming on for Malo Gusto, who could barely complete a pass during a wretched first half. Leeds, beaten at this stage for the 14th time in 18 years, were overwhelmed once their lead was halved. Morgan Rogers and Palmer were devastating after replacing Estêvão and Gittens. Rogers had a hand in four goals and Palmer, who scored twice, seemed affronted by the notion of Leeds going through.

It finished as another thrilling attacking display from Chelsea, who have scored 16 goals in Alonso’s first five games. There are flaws to fix at the other end, though. Leeds also experimented, Daniel Farke making eight changes, but controlled the first half. They led when the Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, signed from Sassuolo last summer, headed Harry Wilson’s corner past Mike Penders in the 23rd minute.

Chelsea have already conceded 10 goals in all competitions. Leeds could have doubled their lead through Sean Longstaff. Valentín Barco and Watson, son of the former Wigan midfielder Ben Watson, were second best in midfield.

Leeds were on their way when Barco lost possession three minutes into the second half. Ethan Ampadu charged past Rogers and found Lukas Nmecha, who teed up Brenden Aaronson to make it 2-0.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto fires home Chelsea’s third goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Chelsea needed a lift. Chavarría crossed from the left and went to ground. Gillett whistled and Palmer scored with 53 minutes played. “He gave out of nothing a penalty where it wasn’t even a chance for them,” Farke said. “A quality player scores and the body language of the Chelsea players was different.”

Palmer was in his element, equalising in the 55th minute after Rogers laid the ball off for his pal to stroke a casual finish past Michael Zetterer from 20 yards. Chelsea were rampant and led on the hour, Palmer and Rogers combining for Neto to finish well. Leeds looked dizzy. They readied the changes but Danny Welbeck made it 4-2 with a sharp turn and finish in the 65th minute.

Leeds kept fighting. Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on and pulled one back to remind Alonso of Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses. Chelsea responded, Rogers crossing for Barco to score his first goal for the club. The sixth followed, Barco’s mis-hit shot diverted in by Welbeck. “A crazy nuts game,” Farke said. That’s been the way for Chelsea under Alonso.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Miovski hits last-gasp Rangers winner and Celtic keep 100% record
Sports.content:
A dramatic last-gasp strike from substitute Bojan Miovski gave Rangers a 1-0 Premiership win over St Mirren at Ibrox.

Back in the technical area after a two-game touchline suspension, Derek McInnes watched St Mirren’s Australian goalkeeper Jacob Chapman keep the home side at bay in the first half with a string of saves, albeit helped by some poor finishing.

Craig McLeish’s side, who lost 5-1 at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup last month, grew in confidence after the break and Fraser Taylor missed a great chance while the frustrated home support returned to the state of agitation which characterised the start of the season.

However, in the final seconds of normal time, Miovski, on for Djeidi Gassama, pounced in the box to grab the winner to make it four victories in a row.

Summer signing Mika Baur notched his first goal for Celtic as the Scottish champions maintained their perfect start to their title defence with a 1-0 victory away to St Johnstone.

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Mika Baur scored his first Celtic goal at McDiarmid Park. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

The German midfielder struck from close range early in the second half after the debutant Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone had produced a stunning first-half save to deny Saints midfielder Joel Cotterill.

It was a night when the Celtic head coach, Martin O’Neill, was able to demonstrate the depth of his squad before Sunday’s Old Firm meeting away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup, with key players such as Camilo Duran, Benjamin Nygren and Kieran Tierney on the bench and defender Cameron Carter-Vickers given the evening off.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Although far from their convincing best, the Hoops did enough to close out a sixth consecutive league victory this term and their 13th in a row in total stretching back to the closing weeks of last season.

Sports.title: Boxing Day bonanza is back with SEVEN games as Premier League confirm TV dates for festive period - following last season's backlash with just one fixture played
Sports.content:
Boxing Day bonanza is back with SEVEN games as Premier League confirm TV dates for festive period - following last season's backlash with just one fixture played

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Premier League has confirmed that seven games will be staged on Boxing Day after releasing its latest set of fixtures.

Four games will be held at 3pm, with Aston Villa facing Leeds at 12.30pm, Hull taking on Liverpool at 5.30pm, before Newcastle host Manchester City at 8pm.

A triple header follows on Super Sunday on Sky Sports on December 27, with Chelsea facing Coventry at 2pm, Man United hosting Nottingham Forest at 4.30pm and Crystal Palace taking on champions Arsenal at 7pm.

It comes after the league faced widespread backlash after hosting just one game on Boxing Day - one of the most popular dates on the football calendar - last year.

That will kick off a busy schedule over the festive season, with three further rounds of matches to be held over the period up to January 7.

A round of midweek evening fixtures will take place on December 29 and December 30, before Leeds host Everton in the only game on New Year's Day.

Boxing Day football is back in the Premier League with seven fixtures confirmed

Last year, Man United vs Newcastle was the only fixture that was scheduled on Boxing Day

The rest of that gameweek will take place on January 2 and January 3, before the festive schedule concludes with a round of games that will fall from January 5 to January 7.

Every fixture from the December 29 to December 30 round and the one from January 5 to January 7 will be broadcast on Sky Sports

The early announcement comes after the Premier League consulted broadcast partners, the Football Supporters' Association and representatives from club Fan Advisory Boards.

There is a desire to give as much notice as possible for those travelling to games.

As part of the schedule, each club is guaranteed at least a 60-hour break between matches in order to help them deal with the fixture congestion.

The early announcement is likely to be welcomed by fans after the Premier League was heavily criticised for arranging just one game on Boxing Day last season.

Manchester United vs Newcastle was the only match, with the top flight blaming scheduling issues caused by European football and the Carabao Cup.

At the time, they said: 'There are now several challenges to Premier League fixture scheduling rooted in the expansion of European club competitions – which led to a revision of our domestic calendar ahead of last season, including changes to the FA Cup.

'This ultimately left the Premier League as a 33-weekend competition – fewer than previous seasons, despite being a 380-match competition since 1995.

'With fewer weekends to work with, the league is bound by how the calendar falls.

'The league can give an assurance that next season there will be more Premier League matches on Boxing Day – as the date falls on a Saturday.'

Sports.title: Chelsea Confidential: Marco Palestra injury update revealed, scouting blow for Blues, Xabi Alonso's view on the Declan Rice 'foul', club's stance on Mauricio Pochettino title talk and latest on missing Geovany Quenda
Sports.content:
Chelsea Confidential: Marco Palestra injury update revealed, scouting blow for Blues, Xabi Alonso's view on the Declan Rice 'foul', club's stance on Mauricio Pochettino title talk and latest on missing Geovany Quenda

Marco Palestra is getting closer to his Premier League debut after this week taking part in individual training with one of Xabi Alonso’s coaches at Cobham, Confidential can reveal.

That was a precursor to participating in Chelsea’s main sessions which would be the final step before being passed fit for selection. Alonso is keen to have him available, but learned his lesson when rushing back Moises Caicedo, who reinjured himself upon returning two weekends ago.

The manager has been preaching caution with both Palestra and Caicedo since that setback, with the Blues boss insisting he will only use the pair once he believes it does not represent a risk. Before the September international break, Chelsea have Hull at home and Brentford away.

Chelsea signed Palestra for £47million from Atalanta. He was named Serie A Defender of the Year while on loan at Cagliari last season, where he was named the fastest player in the division.

The 21-year-old Italian seems set to play an important role under Alonso after the wing back and full back was a feature throughout pre-season, starting in friendlies against Tottenham, Juventus, AC Milan and Real Sociedad.

However, Palestra was then missing from the first matchday squad that won 3-2 at Fulham and has not been seen since, including in Wednesday night's Carabao Cup clash with Leeds. Alonso said he picked up his problem in training a few days prior to travelling to Craven Cottage.

With sources saying Palestra is now involved in outdoor work, he appears to be nearing availability. Confidential asked Alonso earlier this week whether Caicedo was training, and Chelsea’s manager said he was, so the midfielder is likewise closing in on his own return.

Marco Palestra is getting closer to his Premier League debut with Chelsea after this week taking part in individual training, Confidential can reveal

Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo is likewise closing in on a return

CHELSEA LOSE SCOUT TO ADARABIOYO AGENCY

One of Chelsea’s leading scouts, Stewart Thompson, has left the club and joined the football agency, WNRS, headed up by Gbolahan Adarabioyo, the brother of Tosin. Thompson made the move to Chelsea as a first-team scout in 2023. Prior to that, he had been a UK and European scout for Manchester City since 2010.

WNRS handled Tosin’s switch to Tottenham on deadline day. That was understood to be worth an initial £10m with a further £2m in add-ons for Chelsea.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi was said to play a pivotal role in that signing, along with securing Mykhailo Mudryk on a season-long loan with a £75m option to buy. In a blow to Tottenham, Mudryk has suffered an ankle injury in training and is set to be sidelined for several weeks.

Meanwhile, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, the 16-year-old academy prodigy who impressed on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia, has also joined WNRS. The agency’s tagline is: ‘Football management – built for winners.’

Chelsea's Mykhailo Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Spurs, has suffered an ankle injury in training and is set to be sidelined for several weeks

ALONSO TURNS QUESTIONER

In between asking Alonso about free agents and Caicedo earlier this week at Cobham, Confidential wanted to know the Chelsea manager's thoughts on Morgan Rogers’ reaction when he shoved Declan Rice in their 2-1 loss to Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Whether he liked his player showing such passion. Whether he would have preferred his £117m summer signing to have kept a cool head. Alonso did answer, but only once he had asked Confidential a couple of his own questions first. Here’s how our exchange went:

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘Rogers got a yellow for shoving Rice – do you like that passion or would you rather he did not react?’

ALONSO: ‘Did you see the tackle?’

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘I did.’

ALONSO: ‘And?'

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘And Rice should have been the one booked with a Chelsea free-kick for the trip.’

ALONSO: ‘It was clear. It was pretty clear. It’s the emotion of the game. Sometimes, to be able to manage all of them, it’s difficult. We were trying to find the equaliser. Morgan saw the chance to get into the box. It was a tackle that was very… I don’t know how to say in English…’

CONFIDENTIAL: ‘Cynical?’

ALONSO: ‘Cynical – that’s a good one. He showed his frustration. But it’s part of the game.’

Morgan Rogers shows his frustration with Declan Rice after the Arsenal man's 'cynical' foul

CAS: NO CHELSEA CONTACT

Confidential checked in with the Court of Arbitration for Sport, who say there has been no request from Chelsea concerning how they missed out on signing Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day.

We have not heard of any desire to try to escalate that situation into a legal matter, either.

Chelsea remain disappointed with Monaco for how they pulled the plug on that £47m deal, but the noise coming back from inside Stamford Bridge is that they are moving on from what happened.

POCH: STRIP CHELSEA OF THE TITLE

If there was any doubt left within Chelsea that they should not have hired a head coach whose heart was still with Tottenham, Mauricio Pochettino may have just wiped that away.

In an hour-long interview conducted in London with various newspapers, Pochettino, now in charge of the United States, said Chelsea should be stripped of their 2017 Premier League title and that it should be awarded to Tottenham, who finished second that season.

That follows Chelsea being fined £10m this summer for breaching rules relating to payments to agents between 2009 and 2022. The club escaped sporting and retrospective sanctions.

Other than some raised eyebrows, it does not appear there will be an official response to Pochettino’s comments from Chelsea.

Pochettino, now in charge of the US national team, said Chelsea should be stripped of their 2017 Premier League title

GRAHAM POTTER AND THE PHILOSOPHER’S MOAN

Speaking of former Chelsea managers having a pop…

Graham Potter is currently the head coach of the Swedish national team and has been using his Instagram for some sly digs at his old club. The former Chelsea and West Ham boss was surprisingly frank after he uploaded some snaps of himself trying Pilates.

When one user commented: ‘Hopefully you are better at Pilates than you are a football manager.’

Potter replied: ‘I’ll try not to do Pilates in a dysfunctional place and I will be OK.’

When another user responded: 'Didn’t mind the money though, did you?’

Potter replied: ‘Absolutely not.’

They were West Ham fans to whom he was replying, so maybe he will still be welcomed back at Stamford Bridge should he ever want to survey a Swedish player for his national team.

Graham Potter tries a spot of Pilates - and posts it on his Instagram feed

And he was surprisingly frank in an the exchange with a West Ham fan that followed

GEORGE-OUS SAVING

Everton’s deal to sign Tyrique George was worth £24m – £18m plus £6m in add-ons – while Chelsea will retain a 15 per cent sell-on fee for any future sale.

It is already looking like a bargain from Everton’s perspective. Not only because of the 20-year-old’s goal against Manchester United at the weekend, but he can also help David Moyes with his striker shortage, having been used up front at Chelsea.

CHANCE FOR PAEZ TO GET BACK ON TRACK

There was considerable excitement before Kendry Paez arrived.

Chelsea secured him from Independiente del Valle in Ecuador on a pre-agreement worth £17.3m when he was 16 years old, and he arrived once 18. However, loans with sister side Strasbourg and Argentinian club River Plate did not go to plan amid speculation surrounding his lifestyle.

Chelsea tried to find him an English club to join on loan until the end of the summer but they were unable to do so. Now, he is 19, somewhat stuck, and not in Alonso’s first-team plans.

What it does give Paez is the chance to work with Chelsea staff for a few months at least, and hopefully that can do him some good. In the last two years, this South American teenager has lived in Ecuador, France, Argentina and England.

It has been a chaotic time for him, and hopefully he can use this period to focus on getting his once-promising career back on track.

Kendry Paez, 19, has been here, there and everywhere since joining Chelsea but is now with the club for a spell and can hopefully knuckle down

PANEL TO REVEAL GABRIEL VERDICT

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents panel sit down each week to review the major refereeing decisions from every weekend, delivering a verdict on whether calls were right or wrong.

Previously, the results remained private, used only to tell Howard Webb’s organisation where their officials were in the wrong. As of this season, they are being made public.

That means by this time next week, we should know whether this panel believe Arsenal centre back Gabriel should have been in bother for kicking Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez in the head during that Premier League showdown at the Emirates.

There are certainly some within Chelsea who think Gabriel got away with one. Alonso was asked for his take on the Gabriel-Martinez incident, but he said with a little smile at the end of his answer: ‘I have my opinion but we’ll leave it there.’

Arsenal's Gabriel kicks Chelsea keeper Emi Martinez in the head at the Emirates last weekend - but he escaped punishment

QUENDA ABSENCE – A TECHNICAL DECISION

Geovany Quenda was an unused substitute in the Carabao Cup against Leeds, having only appeared once in all competitions all season, coming on in the 82nd minute at Fulham in Chelsea’s first Premier League match of the campaign.

Sources close to Quenda say he is not carrying any injury, and that he is fully fit.

It appears, therefore, it is simply down to technical decisions that Alonso is not using the 19-year-old winger and wing back who arrived from Sporting CP this summer. Chelsea spent £40m to acquire him on a pre-agreement.

Sports.title: Musical Times storms to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with scintillating display... plus our top tips for Day Two of the St Leger Festival
Sports.content:
Musical Times stormed to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with a scintillating display in the Group 2 Betfred May Hill Stakes at Doncaster.

A smooth winner of her first two starts at Newmarket and Yarmouth, the daughter of Lope De Vega travelled kindly in the hands of rider William Buick before being asked to quicken at the furlong marker.

From that point, the response was instantaneous as the 7/4 favourite shot clear of her toiling rivals to score geared down by an enormous seven-and-a-half length margin from Scommessa Sicura and go one better than her mother, Dubai Fountain, who was runner-up in the Group 2 contest.

Bookmakers William Hill reacted by slashing Godolphin's unbeaten filly to 6/1 favourite (from 25/1) for next May's Betfred 1,000 Guineas, while the Leeds-based firm installed Musical Times as 7/4 market leader for the bet365 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket on October 9.

'We'll head to the Fillies' Mile, which was always our plan since Yarmouth really,' reported a delighted Appleby who was saddling his sixth winner from nine September runners.

'She's handled that slightly slower ground today but she's a neat filly, so if it came up quick at Newmarket in the autumn or in the spring it wouldn't worry me.'

Musical Times streaks to victory in the highlight of day one of the St Leger Festival

SAM'S TOP TIPS FOR DAY TWO 2.25 – Final Objective (ew): The talented Pershaada should relish tackling her own age group after taking on the likes of the trail-blazing Bacio in a warm renewal of the Nunthorpe Stakes at York last time. However, the prospect of easy ground will demand a different skillset from the speedy filly and Final Objective could trouble the likely favourite now he drops to the minimum trip for the first time. The selection posted a clear career best in the Group 2 Gimcrack Stakes at York and a strongly-run five furlongs could see him to good effect. 4.45 – Launch Sequence: The application of the first-time cheekpieces and the return to six furlongs could see Launch Sequence power to a first career success in this competitive nursery. A promising debut over course and distance has been followed by two highly promising efforts in decent company with his creditable effort in the Convivial Maiden at York enhanced when the runner-up was placed in Group company next time out. 5.20 - Something Splendid (e/w): It is quite a while since Peter Chapple-Hyam was enjoying Classic success, but the ardent West Bromwich Albion fan has sent out a couple of winners in recent days and Something Splendid is fancied to defy a 5lb penalty for a recent Yarmouth triumph. No doubt buoyed by his beloved team's start to the new Championship season, the Newmarket handler saw the son of Postponed finish runner-up in a division of this corresponding race last year and, although he was later awarded the race when the winner was thrown out, the selection can win this year's renewal under his own volition today.

The Newmarket handler saddled Desert Flower to win the Fillies' Mile before winning the 1,000 Guineas two years ago, but was at pains to point out she was a different model to Musical Times.

'I don't see why she (Musical Times) shouldn't be a Guineas filly. We won this a couple of years ago with Desert Flower, who went on to win the Guineas.

'Funnily enough I see this filly as more of a Guineas filly than Desert Flower, who was big and scopey and unfortunately didn't quite win the Oaks.'

Waardah was another of the fairer sex to shine on Town Moor, comfortably capturing the Group 2 Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes for trainer Owen Burrows and rider Callum Rodriguez.

'We haven't seen a lot of her as she does appreciate a bit of juice in the ground,' said Burrows.

'It was a good run at Carlisle against David O'Meara's Group 1 filly (Estrange) and she was only beaten a neck at Goodwood on quick ground last time, so I was hopeful today.

'She's in the fillies' race (Prix de Royallieu) in France on Arc weekend so that would be her next target and, depending on how that went, we'd have a look at the Group 1 Fillies & Mares on British Champions Day at Ascot.'

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton reveals he held crunch face-to-face talks with Charles Leclerc after blaming Ferrari team-mate for crash on opening lap of Italian Grand Prix
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has admitted he held 'face-to-face' discussions with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc after they clashed on the opening lap of last weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

The pair met ahead of this weekend's first Formula One race in Madrid to iron out the problems brought about by their coming together in Monza.

Hamilton was squeezed off the track by Leclerc, clearly the Monegasque's error, in the second half of the first chicane in early exchanges of positions last Sunday. 'Charles pushed me off,' the seven-time world champion complained at the time.

Leclerc crashed out moments later at the Parabolica in an unrelated event, again his mistake, and it was a big bang. Hamilton went on to finish sixth – a combination of failure that amounted to a poor result for Ferrari on home turf.

Speaking ahead of the new home of the Spanish Grand Prix, Hamilton said: 'What is great is that there was no shying away from having a discussion. We sat face to face, just him (Charles) and me, and talked about it and we were both honest and open and then we quashed it and moved on.

'That shows maturity from him and it is healthy. It is a relationship we have built over time.

Lewis Hamilton (left) has held clear-the-air talks with Charles Leclerc (right) following their clash at Monza

'Of course, there are going to be frustrations along the way. And there will be more times where we are close because we are approximate in pace and we both want to win as much as each other and do well for the team, but, yes, it is really positive.

'It has been really positive. I spoke to Fred (Vasseur, Ferrari's team principal) on Monday and we had clearing out discussions.

'Naturally we are going to have different opinions, but we come together to find a way forward and that is the positive of where we have got to over the past 15 months, when we can have really great communication internally and same with me and Charles.

'If you look at the history of the sport, this happened before, so it is no biggie.'

Hamilton spoke after the race in Italy about needing rules of engagement. Have they been agreed?

'No,' he said. 'Right now I am trying to focus on having a better weekend. I am sure at some stage we will discuss how we can be better but we have not had a lot of time. You can't change things in two days.'

Hamilton's deficit to Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli stands at 76 points. It is a vertical fight for the Briton. Tough, but the target is not insurmountable.

Chasing a never-achieved eighth title, Hamilton said: 'Mathematically it is not impossible, but it is the biggest gap I have seen in a long, long time, and at this stage of the year, too (with 10 rounds remaining).

'Mercedes are the leaders, out ahead, and doing a fantastic job and we should just focus on doing our best each weekend.

'My job at Ferrari is a long-term process and not something that will change this weekend. There are a huge amount of moving parts, a lot of people, and a culture that has been there for a long time. Moving pieces are not so easy. It doesn't happen overnight. But we will get there.'

Sports.title: Conor Benn hits out at 'spoiled brat' Ryan Garcia ahead of Las Vegas world title showdown - as Brit dismisses concerns over huge weight cut on eve of clash with 'insecure' rival
Sports.content:
Conor Benn hits out at 'spoiled brat' Ryan Garcia ahead of Las Vegas world title showdown - as Brit dismisses concerns over huge weight cut on eve of clash with 'insecure' rival

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Conor Benn knows there is a sizeable question hanging over him before he even gets into the ring with Ryan Garcia this weekend: can he still make 147lb?

Benn has not fought at welterweight for more than four years, having moved up through the divisions before competing at middleweight during his two-fight rivalry with Chris Eubank Jr.

Now, for the biggest fight of his career, taking on Garcia for the World Boxing Council (WBC) title under the bright lights in Las Vegas, he has to come all the way back down.

'I can't wait. It's going to be hard,' Benn told Daily Mail Sport during camp. 'I know it's going to be hard, but I believe I can do it.

'I think a lot of people are banking on the weight being an issue and me not having made 147 for four years. Ultimately, my discipline will prevail, and I'll continue to show why I can do what people say I can't do.'

Whether the weight cut affects Benn's strength and power on Saturday night will be one of the central questions of his WBC world title fight.

Conor Benn works out at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas ahead of his showdown with Garcia

Garcia has suggested Benn's move back down could leave him vulnerable, but Benn is dismissive of that concern.

'You think I've been up at middleweight, mixed it with someone who's competed at super middleweight? You think I'm worried about what a lightweight can do to me?' he said.

'You think I'm concerned in the slightest about this guy? I'm not concerned about one little thing he brings to the table… that silly left hook of his is useless. He can bring whatever he wants. It don't concern me.'

Benn's unusual route to this fight has been shaped by his rivalry with Eubank.

Their first meeting at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in April 2025 was the culmination of years of animosity between the two families, with Benn and Eubank Jr inheriting a rivalry that began with their fathers in 1990.

The fight itself was fought at a catchweight above 160lb, with Benn stepping up significantly from his previous division. Eubank won a close decision, leaving Benn to reflect on a performance in which he felt the occasion and the emotion had affected him.

Benn and father Nigel at the Mandalay Bay in Vegas - this is Benn's second fight since he renewed the family feud with the Eubanks

Seven months later, the pair met again at the same venue. This time Benn won the decision, dropping Eubank twice in the final round in a dramatic conclusion to their second fight. It left them level at one victory apiece and appeared to finally close the door on one of British boxing's most talked-about rivalries.

Benn insisted the atmosphere this week is nothing like those two nights when asked whether his hatred for Garcia compared.

'This is nothing like the Eubank fight,' he said. 'The Eubank fight, there was nothing pleasant or friendly or fake about the Eubank fight. There was a lot more raw emotion in that fight and I let that get the better of me the first time. That won't happen here.'

Garcia has been happy to trade insults with his British opponent, but Benn clearly has little time for his opponent's personality.

'He just carries on like a spoiled brat, like a big child who throws his toys out of the pram,' Benn said. 'I'm not worried about him in the slightest. If anything, I'm gonna have a bit of fun with him. He's a little bit sensitive, highly emotional, and a little bit insecure.'

There is also an uncomfortable shared history between the two men when it comes to drugs testing.

Benn's original 2022 fight with Eubank was cancelled after he returned two adverse findings for clomifene, something he has consistently denied intentionally taking. Garcia subsequently returned an adverse finding for ostarine following his 2024 victory over Devin Haney, which he also denied intentionally taking.

Both men were asked at the fight's press conference whether they had concerns that the other could use performance-enhancing drugs ahead of Saturday's contest.

Neither appeared keen to make it a central issue, with the focus instead returning to the fight itself.

Ryan Garcia, Benn's opponent, has also had controversy in his career over positive drug tests

Garcia has also questioned whether Benn's career has prepared him for this level of opposition, arguing that the Briton is taking a step too far by challenging for the world title.

JEFF POWELL IN LAS VEGAS An advance guard of a couple of hundred UK fight fans arrived here in time to see Conor Benn stage a public work-out three days before he challenges Ryan Garcia for the world welterweight title in the intimidating T-Mobile Arena. They kicked up a din as Benn went through a few minutes of snappy pad work in a temporary ring pitched between a bar waiting to serve them and the MGM Grand Casino’s sports book. While admitting he can’t wait to wolf down fish and chips after all the dieting to make the 147lbs welter limit he assured them: ‘I feel great and I’ll give my all to give you all a night to remember.’ But he refrained from removing his top to give them a glimpse of his body. Both he and Garcia looked sharp and calm in their brief appearances. The Benn faithful will be heavily outnumbered on Saturday night by the Americans and Mexicans rooting for King Ry but they are in good voice.

Benn's response was typically blunt. 'How is this too far? He quit against Tank Davis. He got outclassed by Rolly [Romero], and then got a world title shot with Barrios,' he said.

'Then there is me. Stepping up to fight the contenders up at middleweight, fight of the year up at middleweight, avenging my loss. Two big stadium shows. Just come off beating a two-time former world champion and having to make 147, which again I ain't made in four years in six weeks.

'What's he talking about? Ultimately, who cares what he thinks? I don't listen to quitters anyway.'

For all the talk, though, the immediate challenge is the scales. Benn has to get himself back down to a weight he has not made since 2022, before attempting to deal with one of boxing's fastest and most dangerous punchers.

He accepts it will not be straightforward, but he remains convinced the doubts surrounding him will only add to his motivation.

'If I'd listened to everyone that didn't believe in me, I'd be nowhere,' he said. 'But I continue to believe in me. And that's all that matters… you believing in yourself. I believe in me to get me to where I am right now, to revenge that loss against Eubank, to put on Fight of the Year against Eubank, to then fight for the WBC world title.

'I don't need nobody else to believe in me. Continue to doubt me because doubt fuels the fire.'

Sports.title: Barcelona sporting director Deco reveals why LaLiga giants chose to sign Anthony Gordon after overlooking Marcus Rashford - and explains what the team were missing last season
Sports.content:
Deco has explained why Anthony Gordon was deemed the 'best fit' for Barcelona following his £70million move from Newcastle United this summer.

Gordon, who arrived joined Barcelona just weeks after representing England at the World Cup, has already made a positive start to life in Spain, chalking up five assists from four LaLiga appearances so far.

Barcelona had the option to sign Marcus Rashford for £26m following his loan spell at the Nou Camp last season, but the Catalan giants ultimately opted to sign Gordon instead, forcing the Manchester United star to return to Old Trafford ahead of the 2026-27 campaign.

Opening up on Barcelona's transfer strategy during the summer transfer window, sporting director Deco explained how Gordon was signed to bring 'energy' to Hansi Flick's squad after the club noticed a weakness in the side last season.

'One of the things we saw that was difficult last year was the fact that, when we were without Raphinha, the team's energy seemed to drop,' Deco told Marca on Thursday.

'We looked at many wingers, but signing players in the Premier League is almost impossible, you see the figures involved. He was the profile that best fit. The great advantage is that the players are excited to come to our project.'

Anthony Gordon was viewed as the 'best fit' for Barcelona this summer, according to Deco

Barcelona chief Deco signed Gordon for his 'energy' after spotting what the team was missing

After winning LaLiga last season, Barcelona bolstered Flick's squad handsomely in the summer by attracting a string of high profile stars including Rodri, Bernardo Silva, Gabriel Jesus and Karim Adeyemi to the Nou Camp, as well as Gordon.

The £150m summer spending spree appears to have paid dividends, with Barcelona currently top of LaLiga after winning all four of their matches so far.

The Catalans also triumphed 5-1 over Feyenoord in their first Champions League outing of the campaign on Wednesday.

Despite strengthening Flick’s ranks ahead of the new campaign, Barcelona were also keen to sign Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez, but their pursuit of the Argentine ultimately proved unsuccessful.

When asked for his verdict on the Alvarez transfer saga, Deco added: 'I don't want to talk about it anymore. We did things right. We sent them an offer, but there was no response. There's been more talk in the press than reality.

'(Barcelona president Joan) Laporta has already explained that he spoke with them respectfully and clearly. And that's it. We can't keep going on about the same thing. It's more about social pressure than reality.

'Barca didn't tell him to publicly express his desire to leave Atletico. The president of Porto wouldn't let me go to Barca. He told me to stay for a year and then he'd let me go. I stayed, and my obsession was to play well. Luckily, in my case, I was able to go where I wanted.'

Marcus Rashford returned to Man United after Barcelona opted not to sign him permanently

Meanwhile, Rashford has quickly earned the trust of Manchester United boss Michael Carrick and reclaimed his place in the starting XI at Old Trafford.

Rashford, who left the Red Devils under acrimonious circumstances when he joined Barcelona on loan last year, started both United's 5-2 win over Ipswich and 2-2 draw against Everton after beginning the campaign on the substitutes' bench at Hull City.

Manchester United face off against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday night, while Gordon and Barcelona take on Levante away from home in their next LaLiga test on Sunday.

Sports.title: Inside Gloucester's 'radical' revamp as they eye PREM glory: Out with the infamous eight pint 'milk challenge', in with coaching gurus, a Springbok star, history lessons - and the winners of the pre-season fitness challenge revealed
Sports.content:
Significant change has been afoot at Kingsholm this summer as Gloucester – one of English rugby’s proudest and most historic clubs – look to challenge at the top of PREM Rugby once more.

Out have gone 13 players and in have come two Wales captains and a South African World Cup winner. Out has gone the squad’s infamous pre-season milk challenge, which involved new players drinking eight pints in 20 minutes with the aim of not being sick. If they were, they would have their head shaved.

Instead, in have come presentations and acting performances designed to reconnect the squad’s players with the heritage of their employers and the city in which they play. And a new pre-season fitness challenge which took place in the club’s iconic Shed stand.

‘We haven't won a Premiership and for that to happen, there needs to be radical change around the place,’ Lewis Ludlow, Gloucester’s long-serving flanker, tells Daily Mail Sport.

There are new faces everywhere you look at Gloucester, both on and off the field. Wales leaders Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, Springbok enforcer Jean Kleyn and No 9 Dan Robson are the headline playing arrivals.

Assistant coaches Brett Deacon and Joel Tomkins have also joined this summer. Experienced technical director Chris Boyd and rugby manager Rob Burgess both signed on last season.

‘We haven't won a Premiership and for that to happen, there needs to be radical change around the place,’ say Lewis Ludlow, Gloucester’s long-serving flanker

Jamal Ford-Robinson flexes his muscles during pre-season training at Gloucester's Kingsholm

Gloucester’s investment in their first-team squad has come at significant cost and is designed to take some of the pressure off George Skivington, their head coach.

In the boardroom, chief executive Alex Brown continues to seek the sort of external investment that has boosted their PREM rivals Exeter and Newcastle.

‘I feel I now understand Gloucester,’ says Skivington, who joined in 2020. ‘We’ve got a lot of new players and I’ve told them that ultimately, the club wants to win the PREM.

‘This club has never done it, but it's built on a great foundation. We want to re-embrace that. In pre-season, we’ve asked the boys to do projects on former players, past seasons and the history of Kingsholm.

'They did a great job, bringing class and humour. Everybody left knowing a little bit more about the club. They all did it differently. Some of them acted skits out. Some of them did PowerPoints.

'We had a number of former players back for a barbecue and the current lads presented to the old boys on their careers. Will Trenholm was right in the mix on one of the skits.’

Powerful back-row Trenholm impressed with his acting, but it will soon be time for him and his Gloucester team-mates to do their performing between the white lines. By Skivington’s own admission, last season was a transitional one for Gloucester as they finished eighth, winning only five PREM matches.

‘We're very much looking forward now,’ Skivington says. ‘We recruited Jac and Dewi three or four games into last season. We knew very early on we needed to bulk the squad up and we needed senior leadership in certain positions.

‘I feel I now understand Gloucester,’ says head coach George Skivington. ‘We’ve got a lot of new players and I’ve told them that ultimately, the club wants to win the PREM'

Powerful back-row Will Trenholm impressed with his acting during some of Gloucester's quirkier pre-season prep

'We knew we had to sort the backroom staff out and that process began at the start of last season. It was a tough year we had to ride out, but there was always this subplot in the background that we were recruiting well.

‘There's money coming into clubs everywhere. Everyone is getting stronger. We've clearly spent more on and off the field than we have in a long time. That’s really, really important.’

The loss of Wales and Lions scrum-half Tomos Williams to Saracens has been a significant blow to Gloucester, with Robson his replacement. But on the whole, Skivington’s squad looks stronger than it did 12 months ago.

With that comes expectation. Gloucester’s heritage demands they compete at English club rugby’s top table.

‘I've not done a season yet that hasn't started with a lot of pressure,’ Skivington says. ‘But I think there's a good pressure on us this year because we've got a good team on and off the field and we'll welcome the pressure of trying to deliver with that.’

Ludlow, 31, was replaced as Gloucester’s club captain by Williams last season. He has played his entire career with the Cherry and Whites and is preparing for his 14th and Testimonial season at Kingsholm. His sights are set on surpassing Nick Wood's all-time club record of 277 appearances in the professional era.

‘We're in a unique position in that rugby is the main sport around these parts,’ Ludlow says. ‘It’s at the heart of the city. A lot of the ex-players we met still live here. The oldest was in their 80s. They told us of the honour they had playing for Gloucester.

'You could see how much them being back at the club meant to them. There was a lot of emotion. It was nice to see.’

Gloucester have brought in Joel Tomkins (left) as defence coach and Brett Deacon as forwards coach to help Skivington

One-time England No 9 Dan Robson has joined Gloucester from French club Pau

Two seasons ago, Gloucester just missed out on the top four by playing an all-court, attacking game with the imprint of highly-rated backs coach James Lightfoot Brown all over it. Despite the PREM turning into one of club rugby’s highest scoring divisions, that approach has been tempered somewhat.

‘A trophy is definitely achievable,’ says Ludlow. ‘There's been a serious influx of quality coming into the squad. We have an amazing set of fans and what I’ve said to the new lads is they will get behind you.

'But they’ll also let you know when it's not good enough. There was plenty of that last year, which was fully deserved. But they will still be back to support us again.

‘Hopefully, we go out there and deliver. Our performances at home in particular need to be of a better standard. For our fans, the results are the be-all-and-end-all of their week. That's the sort of pressure you need to feel and embrace.’

Gloucester have lifted silverware just once since 2015, in the Premiership Rugby Cup two years ago. In the league, it will be tough – but not impossible – to challenge the likes of Northampton and Bath.

‘We’ve had some big signings come in,’ says No 10 Charlie Atkinson. ‘I know we finished eighth last year, but we took Bath and Northampton to the wire. They were two games we should have won. This year there's a lot more potential for a higher finish. We’re all aiming for top four. There is a big sense of excitement around the club.’

Skivington wants Gloucester to rediscover a harder edge and make Kingsholm a fortress once again.

The club’s pre-season fitness challenge which involved running up and down and across Kingsholm’s most famous stand carrying a raft of different equipment in pairs was part of that. Robson and James Venter were crowned winners.

Jack Innard puts in the hard work during a tough pre-season with Gloucester

Gloucester - with Junior Denny in full flight - hope to challenge at the top end of the PREM this season

‘If you look at Northampton, they're the benchmark at the moment as they’ve won two of the last three PREM titles,’ Ludlow says. ‘People probably underestimate how good their defence is. Last season, they made the most tackles.

'That’s an area we know we need to change and improve on. Joel coming in has put a big emphasis on our defence. We have to go back to being a proper Gloucester forward pack.’

The hard, abrasive nature of new signings Morgan, Lake and Kleyn should give Gloucester more firepower and grunt up front. A big season awaits for the Cherry and Whites. The feeling is they can have no excuses if they don’t perform.

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Insiders reveal Ronald Araujo's desire to stay at Anfield permanently and why he's already loving life on Merseyside, boost for 'next Gerrard' in Reds' academy and decision time for Virgil van Dijk
Sports.content:
Liverpool Confidential: Insiders reveal Ronald Araujo's desire to stay at Anfield permanently and why he's already loving life on Merseyside, boost for 'next Gerrard' in Reds' academy and decision time for Virgil van Dijk

Ronald Araujo is loving life in England and can already picture himself staying at Liverpool beyond his loan spell.

The Uruguay international has only started two matches since joining the club on a season-long loan from Barcelona but has already become something of a cult hero with two stellar performances, one ending in him being named man of the match against Atletico Madrid.

Fans online and at Anfield have been waxing lyrical about the new defender, who showed his South American skills with a fancy backheel assist for Dominik Szoboszlai against Atletico. It appears the feeling is mutual.

Sources have told Liverpool Confidential that Araujo is loving playing for Liverpool and has been on several walks around the city, where he has got a feel for the place.

He has noticed that everyone on Merseyside lives and breathes football in a way that is different even to Barcelona, and he believes there is a real smell of success around the place. This, above everything else, is something the player loves.

It is far too early to say whether Liverpool and Araujo will make the loan move permanent but it is understood there is a pre-existing agreement in place over the fee worth £47million. There is no obligation and the Reds will have the final say at the end of the season.

Ronald Araujo is loving playing for Liverpool and has already become something of a cult hero for their fans

Boss Andoni Iraola has been impressed with the loanee defender and hopes the club can keep him permanently

Araujo's English, at this stage, is limited. The club have offered him daily lessons which he is enjoying but he has taken the additional step of doing an extra hour at home each afternoon. He is able to have basic conversations already.

‘Liverpool is a big club like Barcelona,’ the 27-year-old told Spanish TV after beating Atletico. ‘I am happy, I’m working hard as you can see on the pitch. I am happy here and hungry for more

‘I’m really happy to be here, because Liverpool are a great club, and I’m really looking forward to continuing to give my all so I can keep contributing to the team.

‘I love playing in this stadium; I think it’s a very special and lovely place, and when we’re also able to show off all our hard work here with a good result, it makes us feel very satisfied.’

Araujo was identified because of his versatility and leadership. The Barcelona captain can play at his preferred position of centre back but, as he has shown in the last few days, is just as adept at right back.

He has naturally fallen in with fellow Spanish speakers in the group but Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk have also helped him settle. Sources say how Araujo can ‘smell’ the drive for success and has noticed how everyone in the building is aligned.

Andoni Iraola also gave a glowing review of Araujo, saying after the Atletico game: ‘He’s been very good. The other day he was (against Ipswich) and I’d say he was even better tonight. He’s defending his side really well, but also sometimes because he’s a centre back, we underrate his offensive side.

‘He gave a great assist to Dominik Szoboszlai. He’s made a couple of very good serves from his position and I’m very happy with him. He’s come with the willingness to show he belongs at this level. I hope we can keep him there because he’s in a lovely place.’

Araujo is versatile and a leader - two qualities that make him invaluable to Iraola

Sources close to Araujo say he can ‘smell’ the drive for success behind the scenes at Liverpool and has noticed how everyone is aligned

The three-time La Liga winner adds to the cohort of winners in the building and it should also be said how much he wanted the move.

When Liverpool made contact with his camp, the answer was clear: he was immediately sold on the switch, something cemented by talks with Iraola. He took a pay cut to make the move happen and the Reds are covering that salary in full.

So far, so good. Whether they pay almost £50m for a player who will then be 28 is a question for another day. For now, Araujo is plugging several gaps, excelling in numerous positions – and the Kop are slowly falling in love with a loan player.

Kop Kids - the Eden project is underway

Liverpool’s Under 19s were frustrated in their UEFA Youth League opener on Wednesday afternoon, squandering a two-goal lead to draw 2-2 with Atletico Madrid.

Mor Talla Ndiaye and Josh Sonni-Lambie, two members of the first-team pre-season party, scored in the first half but Joel Sanchez and Adrian Lis-Zielinski brought the visitors level at Kirkby.

The most notable part of the game, though, was Luca Eden becoming Liverpool's youngest-ever player in the competition, at just 15 years and 182 days old.

Eden takes that mantle from Joshua Abe, the talented 16-year-old who Confidential revealed was set for shoulder surgery a fortnight ago. He has since gone under the knife and is on the road to recovery after correcting a long-standing shoulder problem.

Eden, meanwhile, plays like a certain Steven Gerrard, according to seasoned academy observers. He is just 15 so let’s not put too much pressure on his shoulders but he is clearly one of the best talents in the academy, having joined at age four.

Luca Eden (pictured) has become Liverpool's youngest player ever in the UEFA Youth League and has been compared to Steven Gerrard

Sack the board! Alisson fined for fourth official kit kick

Goalkeeper Alisson Becker has been fined £8,000 for misconduct following the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest a fortnight ago.

The goalkeeper was deemed to have acted in an improper manner around the tunnel area after the final whistle.

Confidential has been told the fine relates to Alisson kicking over and damaging the fourth official’s electronic board in frustration as he walked down the tunnel at full-time.

That anger came after Liverpool had waited for three minutes to make substitutions in the build-up to a penalty Alisson conceded, with Iraola accusing the fourth official of taking too long and saying: ‘A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes.’

Alisson accepted the fine.

Alisson has been fined £8,000 after kicking the fourth official's board in frustration following Liverpool's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest last month

Will Van Dijk get the call?

There were plenty of blasts from the past at Anfield on Wednesday night, from former boss Rafa Benitez to ex-Sky Sports commentator Andy Gray back on the microphone with talkSPORT on his first appearance on UK airwaves since 2014.

Another was former Barcelona midfielder and manager Xavi, who is now the Netherlands head coach. The boss might have been aggrieved to arrive only to learn Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong were substitutes, while Cody Gakpo was injured.

Van Dijk, though, was playing, and Xavi has a decision to make over the national team skipper: will he pick him in his first squad? Van Dijk will turn 37 during the next European Championship in 2028.

The pair have held discussions over this matter and Xavi is to announce his first selection next Friday. There is no serious suggestion Van Dijk will be dropped from the Netherlands’ plans but the two parties wanted to ensure they were aligned.

Lewis loving it

One thing we were promised under Iraola was a trust in youth.

While Arne Slot was sometimes accused of having his favourites and being too stubborn, the new boss is not afraid to promote young players.

It has already been evident with the likes of Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Luke Chambers being asked to stick around rather than leave the club on loan, a decision flagged in this column two weeks before the transfer deadline.

No one has been rewarded more than Koumas, with the Welshman making his Premier League and Champions League debuts already this campaign.

Only a few months ago Lewis Koumas was sitting on the bench at Hull City - now he is being trusted in huge games in the Premier League and Champions League

You can see why Iraola likes him, too. The 20-year-old comes on late and injects energy, pace and carries out the manager’s pressing instructions well.

Koumas seems to be loving life and can act as an inspiration to all those out on loan. His spell at Hull City saw him score some big goals but ended with him spending most of his time on the substitutes' bench.

A few months on, he is trusted by Iraola in huge games in the league and Europe.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
