World.title: Croatia Imports 870,000 Tonnes of Waste Each Year, But Why?
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – The hazardous waste scandal that has taken Lika and Croatia by storm shows no sign of dying down, but few realise Croatia actually imports 870,000 tonnes of waste each year. The question is: Why?

If Croatia has truly become Europe’s dumping ground, the 2024 statistics don’t really show it: about 90,000 more tonnes of waste actually left the country than entered it. However, that isn’t enough proof that there are no problems to speak of. The same system in which a Croatian factory legally imports scrap iron, paper or waste wood as raw material can be abused so that hazardous waste ends up buried in Lika.

Slobodan Mufic reports for Index that according to data from the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition, after Croatia’s entry into the European Union back in July 2013, an increase in waste imports was recorded, but exports also continuously grew. Since 2015, waste imports have only twice exceeded exports on an annual basis, and then by roughly five percent. As such, back in 2024, the last year for which official data exists, Croatia imported 871,255 tonnes of waste, of which about 7,100 tonnes of hazardous waste with prior approval. Five Croatian companies carried out the import of hazardous waste in 2024: C.I.A.K., Holcim, NEXE, Premifab and Spectra-Media. The largest part of the imported non-hazardous waste, more than half, consists of metal, paper, cardboard and wood that domestic companies process and use as secondary raw material in production.

During the same year, 961,442 tonnes of waste were exported from Croatia, of which hazardous waste accounted for 26,851 tonnes, or 2.8 percent of the total quantity. All exported hazardous waste ended up in other European Union member states, mostly in Austria, Germany, Poland and Hungary.

it isn’t possible for croatia to entirely ban waste imports

It should be emphasised that Croatia cannot simply ban the import of all types of waste from other EU member states, nor would that be good for Croatian industry. Cross-border waste shipments within the EU are regulated by European rules. Waste is considered goods and no EU Member State can prevent (by way of a general ban) what European Union regulations currently allow. As of the 21st of May 2026, the new EU Regulation 2024/1157 on waste shipments applies, which introduces different cross-border regimes depending on the type of waste and whether the waste is destined for disposal or recovery (reuse of waste as raw material or energy source). For waste intended for disposal, shipments are in principle prohibited, unless the competent authorities give consent. For waste going for recovery there is a prior consent procedure, depending on the degree of toxicity.

Recovery means that the waste is directed to some useful purpose such as recycling, composting or incineration and thereby replaces material or energy that would otherwise have to be obtained from other sources. Disposal means finally removing the waste at a landfill, storage facility or incinerator without energy recovery. Croatia, however, does not have to accept every waste that someone wants to send it. The law already prohibits some categories, for example the delivery of hazardous waste and mixed municipal waste for disposal, and gives the minister the possibility to additionally restrict certain flows if they endanger the domestic waste management system or public health.

why does croatia even need imported waste?

A ban on waste imports would also be harmful to Croatian industry. Existing energy recovery facilities alone have permitted capacities of almost 400,000 tonnes per year, and the largest consumers are cement plants. Našice’s NEXE energy-recovered 58,000 tonnes of waste in 2023 alone, Holcim in Koromačno today consumes tens of thousands of tonnes and plans to reach around 60,000 tonnes per year, while CEMEX in Kaštel Sućurac and Solin already obtains more than a third of the energy for cement from alternative fuels.

Cement plants do not need just any rubbish, but fuel from waste of precisely defined properties. Every shipment must meet quality and composition criteria, including calorific value and content of moisture, chlorine, sulphur and heavy metals, and facilities that incinerate waste are subject to special rules on combustion temperature, process monitoring and emission limit values.

In addition, low-quality or hazardous waste could damage the kilns. The estimate is that from the total municipal waste, of which Croatia collects around 1.9 million tonnes annually, only about 20 percent could become sufficiently high-quality fuel for existing facilities. This also explains the apparent paradox: Croatia can simultaneously have too much of its own waste and import the waste that industry needs. It does not matter to a factory where the scrap iron obtained waste status. What matters is how much it costs, what quality it is, whether it suits its process and whether it can obtain it in sufficient quantity.

the difference between legal trade and illegal disposal

That’s why the entire question of waste imports doesn’t really have a straightforward answer. The import of clean metal waste into a Croatian foundry and the illegal burial of hazardous waste are two completely different things. The first can reduce the consumption of primary raw materials and energy and represents a desirable part of the circular economy. The second is the opposite of the economy and constitutes a criminal offence. The grey area begins precisely between the word “recovery” on the document and what actually happened to the waste. A shipment can neatly and legally cross the border, arrive at a registered entity and still end up completely differently from what the documentation suggests. Exactly such an appearance of legality occurred in Gospić.

Regardless of the State Inspectorate’s data that from 2020 to 2025 the environmental protection inspection examined a total of 2,610 shipments and discovered as many as 1,611 illegal waste shipments, or almost 62 percent, the system was not entirely without supervision.

The problem was that supervision, permits and existing documentation did not ensure reliable tracking of the movement of waste to final treatment and did not prevent enormous quantities of waste from ending up where they should not have. Likewise, this does not mean that 62 percent of the total waste entering Croatia is illegal. Inspection controls are targeted, cover imports, exports and transit, and are also carried out subsequently at companies. An illegal shipment can refer to various offences, including incorrect classification or documentation. Not every such case is criminally similar to the current one in Gospić.

Europe and specifically Croatia are currently trying to close the space in which legitimate waste trade can turn into a cover for illegal disposal. New European rules strengthen digital tracking of cross-border shipments, and an important change is also coming in Croatia from tomorrow.

who took it first isn’t important, but who resolved it last is…

The Ordinance on amendments and supplements to the Ordinance on waste management was published on 31 August and enters into force tomorrow – 8 September. The waste recipient will have to provide the consignor with data on final treatment: the name and PIN of the final processor, their authorisation for treatment of the shipment, the date of completion of treatment and the final treatment procedure.

This goes straight to the heart of the problem exposed by the scandal in Gospić: it should no longer be enough to prove to whom the waste was handed over at the first step, but what happened to it at the last. But even the best electronic form will not help if the data are not checked, if capacities exist only on paper or if the inspection reacts only when tens of thousands of tonnes of hazardous waste are already underground. Tracking the movement of waste is not filing papers in a binder, but the state’s ability to determine for every disputed tonne where it ended up.

World.title: All Eyes are on the Dubrovnik-Montreal Connection in 2027
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – Many are looking forward to the upcoming Dubrovnik-Montreal connection set for May 2027 as Air Canada makes its return.

The new Dubrovnik-Montreal route coming in May 2027 will enable passengers from Dubrovnik to connect more easily with other destinations across not only Canada but all of North America via the Air Canada network, according to Viktor Šober, President of the Management Board of Dubrovnik Airport. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that flights between Dubrovnik and Montreal will operate three times a week from the 11th of May to the 24th of October 2027.

The new route will further strengthen the international connectivity of Dubrovnik Airport with the North American market and open new opportunities for the development of tourist traffic between Croatia and Canada. The introduction of the Dubrovnik–Montreal route is part of Air Canada’s largest intercontinental network expansion to date. For the 2027 summer season, the company is announcing more than 125 international routes and up to 169,000 seats per week from Canada to more than 85 international destinations. The new direct link with Montreal is of particular importance for Dubrovnik because it enables passengers from Canada to arrive more easily to the extreme south of Croatia without transfers at European airports.

major expansion

For the 2027 summer season, Air Canada is announcing more than 125 international routes and up to 169,000 seats per week from Canada to more than 85 international destinations. “Montreal is one of the largest Canadian transport and economic centres, and the new route will at the same time enable passengers from Dubrovnik to connect more easily with other destinations in Canada and North America via the Air Canada network,” briefly commented Viktor Šober, President of the Management Board of Ruđer Bošković Airport. For Dubrovnik tourism, it is particularly important that the route will operate for almost six months, from mid-May to the end of October.

The new route thus opens additional opportunities for the growth of tourist traffic from Canada in the pre-season and post-season, as well as for the further positioning of Dubrovnik in the segments of individual, premium and luxury travel. On the route to Dubrovnik, Air Canada will use the Boeing 787 Dreamliner, including a premium cabin with fully flat seats.

the return of air canada

Flights will be operated with an aircraft featuring Signature, Premium Economy and Economy cabins, offering passengers a high level of comfort and different travel options. The use of the wide-body Boeing 787 Dreamliner is additional confirmation of the potential that Air Canada sees in Dubrovnik and its tourist market, especially in the premium leisure travel segment. Canada is an important and promising market for Dubrovnik, and the establishment of a direct link with Montreal further confirms Dubrovnik’s international position and its attractiveness on the North American market. The flight to Dubrovnik marks Air Canada’s return to Croatia with its own aircraft after several years of absence.

The carrier first began flying to Zagreb in 1989 and discontinued flights in 1991, according to Ex-Yu Aviation News. Its subsidiary, Air Canada Rouge, resumed seasonal flights between Toronto and Zagreb in June 2018, initially with four weekly flights on a Boeing 767-300ER, marking the return of the Air Canada brand to the Croatian market after 27 years. The service was maintained during 2019 but was suspended back in 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic.

World.title: Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb to Undergo Renovation
World.content:
September the 9th, 2026 – The beautiful buttermilk Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb is set to undergo renovation after over half a century of not being touched.

Since the Croatian National Theatre (HNK) building is individually protected as cultural heritage, all interventions will have to be designed in close accordance with the rules for the protection of cultural heritage. After almost 57 years since the last major renovation, the building of the Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb is once again undergoing a complete renovation. Poslovni reports that the last major construction renovation and reconstruction of the HNK took place from 1967 to 1969, and now the project has taken a new step — two bids have been received for the preparation of part of the conceptual design.

The renovation of the Croatian National Theatre building in Zagreb has taken a new step toward realisation after two bids arrived for the tender for the preparation of part of the conceptual design. Both are financially more favourable than the estimated procurement value of 1.2 million euros excluding VAT, as is currently understood. The most favourable bid, worth 762,400 euros excluding VAT, was submitted by a consortium of bidders led by the Faculty of Civil Engineering of the University of Zagreb, together with Studio Arhing and Toding. The second bid came from the company UPI-2M, which offered the job for 894,857 euros excluding VAT.

protected cultural heritage

The project concerns the structural, comprehensive and energy renovation of the existing building on Republic of Croatia Square, as well as two underground extensions. Under the stage, a reinforced concrete substructure is planned for the needs of new stage technology, while an underground floor would be built next to the existing building to ensure better working conditions for the three theatre ensembles. Since the Croatian National Theatre building in Zagreb is individually protected cultural heritage, all interventions will have to be designed in accordance with the rules for the protection of cultural heritage. The procurement includes projects for the structure, heating, cooling and ventilation, electrical installations, multimedia, water supply and drainage, traffic surfaces, fire extinguishing systems, and landscape architecture, including a green roof.

The architectural design is not included in this procurement because the client decided to organise it through a separate procedure. The conceptual design that will be prepared should serve as the basis for obtaining a location permit, as well as for defining individual phases of the renovation and estimating the costs of their implementation. The final decision on the selection of the contractor has not yet been made. After the opening of the bids, the public procurement procedure continues, and the deadline for filing an appeal against the bid opening procedure is ten days.

World.title: Iraq secures US, South Korean, Turkish air defenses
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNew.com) — Iraq has finalized contracts for new air defense systems from the United States, South Korea, and Turkey, with the first deliveries due shortly as Baghdad prepares to regain more control of its airspace when the US-led coalition mission expires on September 30.

Baghdad intends to deploy the technology around the nation to safeguard oil installations, important infrastructure, and Iraqi territory while it develops an integrated network of long-, medium-, and short-range defenses backed by radar and command systems.

The effort took on new significance as Iraq’s airspace became a conduit for missiles, drones, and military aircraft amid regional warfare involving Iran, the US, and Israel.

Iran has also directly attacked US sites in Iraq, highlighting Baghdad’s inadequate capacity to prevent foreign assaults and protect its airspace on its own.

Iraq had initially planned a six-year program to upgrade its air defenses, but Al-Zaidi reduced the timeline to three years.

The increase corresponds with the final evacuation of soldiers assigned to the multinational coalition’s mission in Iraq.

Baghdad claims Iraqi troops can now manage the residual ISIS threat, and Operation Inherent Resolve will officially finish inside Iraq at the end of the month.

The new systems from the United States, South Korea, and Turkey are likely to play a key role in Iraq’s efforts to bridge a long-standing air-defense gap and gain more control over its skies after the coalition departs.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis seize key city on Red Sea: military source
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis seized control of the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday, a Yemeni military source told AFP, as the Iran-backed group reported fresh strikes by Saudi forces.

The Houthis, who control large parts of northwest Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive last week against Yemeni government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.

They also launched attacks on Saudi territory that left dozens of people wounded, in a conflict that has reignited during the Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

Witnesses told AFP they saw Houthi forces entering Mokha on Thursday while chanting “death to America, death to Israel”.

The Yemeni military source said they were advancing towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait “after having taken control of Mokha”.

The waterway, which links Asia to Europe via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, has gained importance as a transit route since the start of the wider Middle East war, which saw Iran blockade the Strait of Hormuz.

The military source said the Houthis also seized Zuqar Island, in the southern Red Sea, “after rocket attacks and a ground assault carried out using boats transporting fighters”.

Also on Thursday, the Houthis reported airstrikes.

“The Saudi enemy’s air force conducted around 40 strikes in recent hours in the governorates of Taiz, Hodeida, Al-Jawf and Marib,” Houthi news agency Saba said.

– Hundreds dead –

Yemen relapsed into war in July after years of relative calm punctured by sporadic violence and deepening poverty.

Since last week, the fighting in Yemen has left more than 500 dead, mostly combatants, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources.

It has also forced nearly 20,000 people to flee their homes, the International Organization for Migration said on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthis said the anti-government fighters fired ballistic missiles and drones at several cities in southern Saudi Arabia.

The Saudi civil defence issued alerts warning of “potential danger” in two areas, Khamis Mushait and Abha, before lifting them soon after.

The Houthis triggered the return to hostilities in July when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.

The government retaliated by striking Sanaa airport, an attack the Houthis blamed on its sponsor, Saudi Arabia.

The ongoing exchanges risk returning Yemen to a conflict that left hundreds of thousands of people dead and sparked one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.

The Houthis, after seizing Yemen’s capital and forcing out the internationally recognised government, fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a United Nations-brokered ceasefire in 2022.

World.title: France will not support Infantino in FIFA election: federation chief
World.content:
Paris – France will not support the candidacy of Gianni Infantino, who is running for a new term as FIFA president in March 2027, the French Football Federation (FFF) announced on Thursday.

The FFF is aligning itself with the position of other European federations such as Belgium, Italy, Scotland, Sweden and Wales, who have also publicly withdrawn support for Infantino.

FIFA confirmed last weekend that Infantino will stand in the FIFA presidential election next March, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the men’s and women’s World Cups.

At this stage, the 56-year-old Swiss is the only candidate.

“We believe that the trust placed in the FIFA president has been betrayed, and that the way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us,” FFF president Philippe Diallo said in a statement.

“That is why, by a unanimous decision of its members, the French Football Federation has decided to withdraw its support for Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the FIFA presidency.”

World.title: Vance takes spotlight as Republicans close Trump-heavy convention
World.content:
Dallas – US Republicans return to the stage Thursday to close their midterm convention, still betting that Donald Trump’s political magnetism can overcome grim election forecasts — while giving Vice President JD Vance a prime-time showcase as a potential heir.

Trump will dominate the finale of the two-day gathering, delivering closing remarks after Vance’s keynote address at the American Airlines Center in downtown Dallas.

The unusual convention has been built around a simple message: Trump may not literally be on November’s ballot, but Republicans want the president’s supporters to behave as though he is.

That strategy comes with the party under heavy pressure.

US election tracking site Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats will win the House 230-205 and take the Senate 51-49. Trump’s approval rating has languished in the low-to-mid 30s amid stubborn inflation and an unpopular war with Iran.

Trump dramatically raised the stakes in his opening night keynote Wednesday, promising a $5,000 “Trump dividend” to every American adult if Republicans retain both chambers of Congress in November.

He also made explicit the convention’s central electoral pitch.

“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot — I’m on the ballot, I’m on the ballot — just one more time,” he said.

He strongly defended the Iran war, predicting victory would bring down oil prices, and warned that the United States would become a “communist country” if Democrats prevail in the election.

– Heir apparent? –

Vance’s appearance adds intrigue to the closing night.

The 42-year-old vice president is widely regarded as an early front-runner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, although he has said he will not make a decision until after the midterms.

His place immediately before Trump’s closing remarks gives him one of the most prominent speaking slots of the convention and an opportunity to address a party already beginning to consider its post-Trump future.

But in the more immediate contest, Republicans need Vance and other party figures to help deliver Trump’s voters in an election in which the president himself is absent from the ballot.

Republicans also hope to use the closing night to promote tax cuts, immigration enforcement and other administration policies while depicting Democrats as increasingly extreme.

The convention has resembled an extended Trump rally more than a traditional party meeting, with no nominations or formal business and more than 50 speakers or presentations each night.

The atmosphere inside the arena on Wednesday was festive despite the political headwinds. Yet not all Republicans have embraced the experiment.

Numerous lawmakers in competitive races chose to remain in their districts rather than spend valuable campaign time in Dallas, while both convention nights were facing competition from the opening games of the NFL season.

Those who have shown up will be looking for evidence that Vance can emulate Trump in energizing the voters who powered the flamboyant billionaire’s return to the White House.

And Vance, whether he acknowledges it or not, will be speaking to a party already asking who might inherit those voters when Trump is no longer the headline act.

“If the American people give Republicans another chance to govern, we’re going to create more prosperity,” Vance told Fox News after Trump’s speech.

“And we want the American people to share in that prosperity.”

World.title: Iraqi Airways doubles Baghdad-Amman flights on peak days
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Airways will double flights between Baghdad and Amman on peak travel days beginning Friday, Sept. 11, in response to increased passenger demand between Iraq and Jordan.

The airline said that it would boost flights from one to two each day on Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays, increasing capacity on three of the busiest days of the week.

Daily service will continue on the other days.

The increased schedule provides additional alternatives for travelers traveling between Baghdad International Airport and Amman’s Queen Alia International Airport, both of which are already available on Iraqi Airways’ booking network.

Iraqi Airways said that the extra flights are being added in response to a large increase in passenger traffic on the route, with the goal of providing more flexibility as demand develops.

The move improves air connectivity between Iraq and Jordan, which have strong business, tourist, and family travel relations.

The development coincides with Iraqi Airways’ efforts to expand fleet operating capacity and widen its regional and international network.

As part of its attempts to increase fleet availability, the state-owned airline has recently resumed aircraft operations and expanded repair capabilities.

The revised Baghdad-Amman timetable becomes effective on September 11.

World.title: Seahawks beat Patriots again in NFL opener
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Seattle Seahawks shrugged off Sam Darnold’s early injury to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the NFL’s opening game, piling more misery on the team they defeated in last season’s Super Bowl.

Backup quarterback Drew Lock threw for 187 yards and a touchdown to Jackson Smith-Njigba, as reigning champs Seattle rallied from 10-0 down for their 11th consecutive win.

The latest loss inflicted more pain on New England quarterback Drake Maye, who threw three costly interceptions, including a particularly wasteful one in the final seconds from field-goal range to throw away a patchy, defensive game.

Maye — who had been sacked six times in February’s Super Bowl, and suffered three more here — was picked off by Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe in the end zone.

“It was game on the line. You know, fourth quarter… we only was up three points, and we got to take the ball away, and we did,” said Jobe.

“Holy cow, we did it! Here we are, one-and-zero,” said Lock.

And it was a night to forget for the Patriot’s new acquisitions too, as AJ Brown limped off with an ankle injury and Romeo Doubs was beaten for one interception and was guilty of a terrible drop shortly before a second.

The Seattle evening began in festive fashion. A new Super Bowl LX championship banner was unfurled from Lumen Field’s colossal rafters. Pearl Jam’s Mike McCready performed the national anthem.

But the mood was punctured on the game’s first drive. Darnold was sacked on third down by Dre’Mont Jones, and limped to the locker room via the medical tent clutching his hip. He did not return.

The Patriots struck first. Maye hurled the ball 34 yards to Brown on the edge of the endzone. Defensive pass interference was called, and Maye immediately lofted a short pass over the top to newly drafted tight end Eli Raridon for the season’s first touchdown.

Seattle fought back. Veteran receiver Cooper Kupp took a stunning one-handed diving catch from Lock for a 24-yard gain on third down. The pair then celebrated a touchdown pass, before the score was ruled out for an illegal shift, and the Seahawks settled for a field goal.

– Interceptions –

After a promising Patriots drive, Maye’s ambitious downfield hurl to Romeo Doubs ricocheted off Rodney Thomas’s fingers to Nehemiah Pritchett for the game’s first interception.

The Seahawks made Maye pay. At 4th & 1, Lock passed to an open Smith-Njigba, who raced past the Patriots defense at lightning speed for a 45-yard touchdown, tying the game 10-10.

Seattle drove again, with Lock peppering passes before charging 14 yards into the red zone. A series of errors from a hugely promising position meant it was only a field goal.

An increasingly desperate Maye suffered his first sack of the night trying to break through the Seattle defense. Two more swiftly followed, though the Patriots somehow edged the ball upfield, twice successfully going for fourth downs.

But sensing a chance for a winning touchdown, despite being in field goal range, Maye hurled a deep right pass to Mack Hollins in the end zone, resulting in Jobe’s game-ending interception.

“We’ve moved on. This is a new season. We did the banner thing. It’s time to find out who 2026 Seahawks are going to be,” said Lock.

World.title: Philippine ferry fire kills 5, dozens missing
World.content:
Manila – At least five people were killed and 86 remain missing after a fire erupted aboard a ferry near a tourist hotspot in the Philippine province of Palawan, the coast guard said Thursday.

The blaze broke out on the M/V June Aster Wednesday evening about 2.2 kilometres (1.3 miles) offshore, the coast guard said, adding that five casualties had been brought ashore.

Video shared by the coast guard on Facebook showed the vessel completely engulfed in flames.

Hundreds of people, desperate for news about the incident, have left comments on the Coron town mayor’s Facebook page, searching for relatives, friends and even a dog.

“Based on the data we have right now on rescued (42) and the casualties, we still have 87 people who are unaccounted for,” coast guard Captain Noemi Cayabyab told a local radio station on Thursday.

The ship’s manifest had listed 134 passengers and crew, Cayabyab said.

Of those rescued, 38 were passengers and four were crew, she added.

Hours later, the Philippine Coast Guard told reporters that another person had been rescued, but their identity had yet to be confirmed.

“Just to make it clear, this is live data and may change as our search and rescue operations are ongoing,” Cayabyab said in the radio interview.

“However, we have not yet been able to obtain information from the rescued individuals because we have not been able to speak with them,” she said, adding attempts to put out the blaze were ongoing.

There were no immediate reports of foreigners on board.

Tracking data from MarineTraffic showed the June Aster had departed from Manila.

In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.

The M/V Trisha Kerstin 3 sank along nearly the same route where 31 people died in 2023 after a fire broke out aboard the Lady Mary Joy 3 ferry.

World.title: Asian Games begin with Qatar basketball win, nine days before opening ceremony
World.content:
Tokyo – The Asian Games began in Japan on Thursday when Qatar beat Iran in the men’s basketball opening group game, the first action in the continental multi-sport showpiece that has more participants than the Olympics.

Over 17,000 athletes and officials are expected to take part in 43 sports at the Nagoya-Aichi Games — which do not officially start until the opening ceremony on September 19 and will run until October 4.

Several events such as basketball, football, cricket, hockey and modern pentathlon will get under way before the opening ceremony.

Qatar held off a comeback from Iran to win their Group B encounter 59-35 at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya in the first match of a men’s basketball competition that will hold medal finals on September 20, the day after the opening ceremony.

Los Angeles 2028 Olympics qualifying spots are up for grabs in several sports at the Asian Games, which are returning to Japan for the first time since 1994.

Organisers hope the athletes will have a “unique experience” staying in eye-catching accommodation ranging from a cruise liner and wooden containers to standard hotel rooms.

Officials are confident that the plan will not be affected by Japan’s typhoon season, which is usually in full swing in September-October.

Weather has already caused disruptions, with record rainfall on Tuesday forcing hundreds of athletes briefly to evacuate their accommodation.

Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi, at the International Space Summit in Paris, on Thursday hailed Isro and its scientists, called for global cooperation in the sector and said his country âsupports a safe, secure and sustainable space domain anchored in international lawâ.Addressing the summit virtually from Delhi, Modi said, âIndiaâs approach is rooted in Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, that is One Earth, One Family, One Future. Its capabilities serve farmers and fishermen, weather forecasting, disaster management and navigation. More than 430 satellites from 34 countries have travelled to space aboard Indian rockets. Isroâs technologies and partnerships serve not only India, but the wider world.âPraising Isro scientists, the PM said, âBehind this global trust is the dedication and hard work of generations of Indian scientists, engineers and technicians. Working day and night, they have built Isroâs global reputation mission by mission, success by success, and given India a place of pride among spacefaring nations.âModiâs praise will act as a morale booster for Isro employees, some of whom had recently written to the Isro chief, raising concerns about the âshift towards privatisationâ. After nine employee associations had sought written clarification from the Isro chairman on privatisation push, agency head V Narayanan and INSPACe chairman Pawan Goenka had allayed fears of the staff, saying there was no move to privatise the organisation and that reforms were meant to widen the space ecosystem.On the private sector, the PM said, âAlongside Isro, Indiaâs private space sector is also surging in a big way. The energy of enterprise is joining the excellence of Isro.âOn Indiaâs achievements, Modi said, âChandrayan-3 made India the first nation to land near the lunar south pole. Aditya-L1 is unlocking the secrets of the Sun. Last year, an Indian visited the International Space Station. Looking ahead, we aim to establish an Indian space station by 2035 and send an Indian to the Moon by 2040. In all these efforts, our guiding principle has been clear: their benefits must reach all humanity. âOn France's support to Indiaâs space programme, Modi said, âFrance has been a trusted partner since the Indian space programme began at Thumba in the 1960s. Today, our cooperation spans Earth observation and advanced technologies, uniting scientific excellence with human purpose. We invite France and the world to be co-travellers in Indiaâs next space frontier.âThe PM said for centuries, space inspired people's imagination and now, it shapes life on Earth, from climate and crops to oceans and communities. âThe promise of space is infinite. Our responsibility is collective. As orbits become more crowded, technologies more powerful, and actors more numerous, our choices must be clear: cooperation over confrontation; sustainability over short-term gain; and inclusion over exclusion," he said.Sending a global message from the summit, Modi said, âWe will explore together, innovate together and protect space together, for all humanity, and for generations to come.â

World.title: Brics turns 25: How a Goldman Sachs acronym became a global power bloc
World.content:
New Delhi will play host to the 18th Brics Summit

From a Wall Street acronym to a global grouping

Why Brics matters in the changing global order

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping at a time when wars, trade tensions and a shifting global order are testing its ability to act as a united bloc.India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair, with the grouping now comprising 11 members and 10 partner countries.Under the theme âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,â New Delhi has placed greater focus on cooperation across economic and financial issues, technology, energy, development and global governance.The scale of that transformation becomes clearer when traced back to the origins of Brics, a term coined 25 years ago by a Goldman Sachs economist to describe four emerging economies that he believed would become major drivers of global growth.Twenty-five years ago, Brics did not exist as a political grouping. It was a term coined by Goldman Sachs economist Jim OâNeill in 2001 to describe Brazil, Russia, India and China as emerging economies that could become major drivers of global growth.His paper, Building Better Global Economic BRICs, argued that the weight of these economies in the world economy would rise significantly and called for their greater representation in global policymaking forums.The transition from an economic concept to a government-led grouping began in 2006, when the foreign ministers of Brazil, Russia, India and China met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The first summit of their leaders followed in 2009 in Yekaterinburg, Russia, giving the grouping a formal leaders-level platform.The following year, South Africa joined, turning BRIC into Brics and giving the grouping its first member from Africa.The next major transformation came at the 2023 Johannesburg Summit, when Brics agreed to its first large-scale expansion. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were invited to join from January 1, 2024. Indonesia subsequently became the bloc's 11th full member in January 2025.The expansion also created a partner-country category, allowing a wider group of developing economies to engage with Brics without becoming full members.Brics has evolved from a forum focused largely on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.Its members have repeatedly called for reforms in institutions such as the United Nations and international financial institutions, arguing that the architecture of global governance should better reflect the changing balance of economic power.Its growing importance is also backed by institutions created by the grouping itself. The New Development Bank, established in 2015, was designed to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in Brics and other emerging and developing economies.The bloc's significance has increased further with its expansion. The addition of countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia has widened Brics' economic and geographic reach and strengthened its claim to be a platform for the Global South.

World.title: 'Can't browbeat child': SC on CJP protester's intimidation complaint against 'influencer'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday took serious note of allegations that a 14-year-old girl associated with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests was harassed and that her residence was subjected to stone pelting, directing authorities to act on her FIR and provide protection to her and her family.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure action on the girl's FIR and sought status reports from the Delhi and Uttar Pradesh governments on the allegations, security arrangements and action taken against those allegedly involved.

The court stressed that nobody could be allowed to intimidate a victim or her family to prevent them from pursuing criminal proceedings.

"Such matters cannot be taken lightly. Nobody should be protected if violence against a child is involved... if persons accused of such acts were roaming free and attempting to browbeat the child or her family so that they do not pursue criminal proceedings, it would be a serious matter.

"There cannot be any second opinion about it. Such matters cannot be taken lightly. Nobody should be protected. If violence against a child is involved and persons are roaming free and trying to browbeat the child or the family so that they do not pursue the criminal proceedings, that may be a serious matter," the bench observed.





The counsel appearing for the minor told the court that she had been harassed and her house vandalised after she registered an FIR against a person who allegedly claimed in a video that he had attacked her father during the CJP's protest.

The lawyer alleged that instead of prosecuting people who accompanied the accused and were allegedly captured on camera, an FIR had been registered against the child. The counsel also submitted that this was contrary to an earlier Supreme Court order and that video evidence showing stone pelting at the girl's residence could be placed before the court.

"The high-powered committee will take time, but if something happens to the child in the meantime, that cannot subsequently be reversed or repaired through the committee," the counsel submitted.

Responding to the submission, CJI Surya Kant said, "If there are anti-social elements who indulged in violence against child, and they are roaming free, and are trying to browbeat the child, that may be a serious thing."

The Chief Justice further told the Solicitor General, "Child is a child. Some measures to protect the child can be taken. This incident can be taken as a standalone [case] by local police."

Justice Joymalya Bagchi also directed that immediate action be taken on the FIR and that the minor and her family be provided police protection.

"We would like immediate action on that FIR and police protection to victim and family by UP police.

Investigation be conducted by Parliament Street PS".

The counsel also alleged that videos showed four policemen accompanying the persons who attacked the protesters and claimed that no action had been taken against them.

Delhi Police action against accused

World.title: Amid opposition, Karnataka govt. to take up 120-km elevated corridor network
World.content:
Amid continuing controversy over Bengaluru’s elevated corridors and other large infrastructure projects, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Thursday reviewed plans for 13 elevated corridors spanning 120 km.

The agenda for the city highlights that the government is currently in the process of inviting tenders for 11 of the proposed corridors, covering 75.6 km, at an estimated cost of ₹13,262.7 crore, according to details presented at a review meeting.

It has also been decided that the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) will take up land acquisition for the elevated corridors. A survey of properties likely to be affected by land acquisition for the 11 corridors has already been undertaken.

The elevated corridors are proposed to reduce congestion on major roads and junctions, improve connectivity between Bengaluru’s core and outer areas, and cut travel time. Most of the projects have been planned in line with the Bengaluru Integrated Transport Plan-2020, Mr. Shivakumar pointed out in the meeting with Greater Bengaluru Authority officials.

The Chief Minister was reviewing works under all parastatals as the GBA marked one year earlier this month. Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda was also present during the meeting.

Economic Development Agency

The meeting also dealt with the proposed Economic Development Agency, which was supposed to be set up within one year of the GBA’s formation, with the Minister for Bengaluru Development as its chairperson. The agency can be tasked with attracting investments and generating employment in the GBA limits through suitable public-private partnership projects.

The agenda mentioned that the proposal for the agency was placed before the GBA Executive Committee at its second meeting on July 3. Members were asked to submit suggestions or instructions within three days. As no suggestions were received, the proposal was subsequently submitted to the GBA Authority for approval.

₹1,700 crore road works

The review also covered white-topping works covering 120.69 km across Bengaluru at a total cost of ₹1,700 crore. Of this, 55.54 km is being taken up under the State government’s ₹800-crore grant for 2023-24, while another 65.15 km is being developed using ₹900 crore from additional tax revenue of the municipal corporations. So far, 64.09 km of roads have been completed and opened to traffic, while work on the remaining stretches is under way.

World.title: Mandala workshop in Madurai to explore self-reflection through mindful drawing and journaling techniques
World.content:
A pencil moves slowly across a sheet of paper. There is no hurry to finish the design. In fact, participants are asked not to complete it within the given time. The instruction is simple — go slow and do not press the pencil too hard.

This is one of the exercises in city-based B Shangamithra’s 10-day session on mandala art and mindful journaling. For her, drawing is not just about creating something beautiful. It is also a way to get people to pause for a while and think about themselves.

She also offers 90-minute, one-day workshops for both groups and individual participants. One of the themes she explores is ‘self-check’. It asks a simple question: are we doing certain things because we want to, or because we want to please someone else?

To explore this, Shangamithra uses a self-portrait exercise. Participants are encouraged to look for a picture or a drawing of a girl they like and create their own version — how they see themselves now, how they would like to be or how they imagine themselves in the future. The drawing exercise is followed by journaling.

The exercise brings up the need for approval from others. “I mainly rule out people-pleasing. Don’t seek validation outside. All you seek is vision,” says Shangamithra.

She also encourages participants to write affirmations — simple statements that reflect what they want to believe in or work towards. Another exercise in the workshop is called ‘Slow, Soft and Strong’, or 3S. Here, participants are given 10 affirmations and asked to choose the one that connects with them. They are then given a tracing sheet and a timer. But there is a catch. They are not expected to finish the mandala before the timer goes off. Instead, they have to trace it as slowly as possible.

Shangamithra asks them not to press the pencil too hard. A sheet placed underneath the drawing makes the difference visible. Press the pencil hard and its pressure shows up on the sheet.

The exercise is about being slow, soft and strong — slow in the way one works, soft in the way one handles the pencil, but strong when it comes to one’s intention.

The workshop also includes a ‘trigger check’, where participants are encouraged to become aware of what causes certain reactions in them. For Shangamithra, these exercises are not about producing a perfect drawing. The mandala simply becomes a starting point for a conversation with oneself.

Over the course of the 10-day workshop, participants are introduced to different exercises that encourage them to become more aware of their thoughts, actions and choices. Drawing, in this setting, becomes a quiet activity that allows them to step away from the rush of everyday life and spend some time with themselves.

The online format also means participants can join from wherever they are, without having to be in the same room. Shangamithra’s approach is simple: pick up a pencil, slow down and pay attention to what comes up along the way.

A mandala may begin as a series of lines and patterns. But by the time the pencil stops moving, the exercise may have left the participant with something else to think about — whether they are living by their own choices or constantly looking outside for approval.

To join the session and workshop on mandala art and mindful journaling, call 8072069509. The fee for a 90 minute one-day workshop is ₹300 per individual and for a 10 day session it is ₹1200

World.title: NIMHANS conducts mental health programmes in over 420 govt. colleges
World.content:
To create awareness about mental health policy and the institutional role in preventing suicides among students as per the guidelines of the Supreme Court, the Department of Collegiate Education, in collaboration with the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS) and regional partner institutions, conducted a series of one-day orientation programmes across various districts in Karnataka.

According to NIMHANS, more than 420 Government First Grade Colleges and over 800 principals participated and received orientation on recognising and responding to student mental health concerns, strengthening institutional support systems, suicide prevention, mental health promotion, available tele-support services, and the use of digital mental health resources.

On August 11, the first programme, “Abhaya”, was organised at the NIMHANS Convention Centre, Bengaluru, in collaboration with Government Arts College, Hassan. Students from colleges across Bengaluru, Mysuru, Shivamogga, and Mangaluru participated in the first session. Similarly, the second session, “Beluguthirali Baduku”, was organised in Kalaburgi on September 2, where students and principals from Ballari and other districts also attended.

“Jeevanapreeti – Baalige Spoorthi” was the final session held in Dharwad on September 7 that brought together students from Hubballi, Haveri, Gadag, and other districts. Experts from NIMHANS created awareness on myths and facts related to mental health, developing institutional support systems, and the role of institutional leaders and faculty in creating supportive educational environments.

World.title: ‘New Congress’ will emerge in Andhra Pradesh after local body elections: AICC in-charge secretary
World.content:
Andhra Pradesh AICC in-charge secretary and Member of Karnataka Legislative Council P.V. Mohan on Thursday said that a ‘New Congress’ would emerge in Andhra Pradesh through the ensuing local body elections providing a great opportunity for the party to showcase its strength at the grassroot level.

Speaking to The Hindu over telephone ahead of his visit to the State from September 14, Mr. Mohan said: “I am planning to visit all districts in the State to hold review meetings with senior leaders and chalk out an action plan for the local body elections.”

Later, I will hold meetings in all 175 Assembly constituencies to strengthen the party ahead of the 2029 Assembly and Parliament elections, he added. He expressed confidence that the Congress would emerge victorious in several constituencies in 2029 and be in a position to form the government in 2034.

The Congress senior leader felt the Congress’s governments in Kerala, Karnataka and Telangana and its alliance with TVK in Tamil Nadu would influence votes in Andhra Pradesh also improving its prospects. He also said that Opposition Leader in Lok Sabha ‘Rahul Gandhi’ has become an icon of the new generation which are keen to vote for the Congress in the municipal and parishad elections.

He alleged that the Telugu Desam and the YSRCP had failed to develop Andhra Pradesh over the last 12 years. “YSRCP’s graph has fallen drastically in the 2024 elections. Its strength got reduced to 11 seats in the previous elections. TDP and its alliance parties such as Jana Sena Party (JSP) and BJP lost the people’s support with poor administration. All these factors will make people look at the Congress in the State,” said Mr. Mohan.

Mr. Mohan alleged that parties in Andhra Pradesh had failed to put pressure on the Narendra Modi-led government at the Centre to implement the promises made in the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act-2014.

He said: “Andhra Pradesh would have been economically strong had the Special Category Status been implemented as it was incorporated in the Act.. The TDP and YSRCP failed to ask the Centre for its implementation.”

He also criticised the government for the delay in completing the Polavaram project and alleged that adequate steps are not being taking to protect the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant which was established during the time of Indira Gandhi’s rule.

World.title: Infant dies in Thiruvananthapuram, mother taken into custody
World.content:
A one-and-a-half-year-old was allegedly murdered by her mother in Vilavoorkal, near Malayinkeezhu, here on Thursday. The child, identified as Ivana, alias Anna, the daughter of Abhijith and Christy, sustained a severe injury to her neck and later died despite being rushed to the Vilavoorkal family health centre and referred to the Thiruvananthapuram Government Medical College Hospital. The incident came to light around 5 p.m.

The Malayinkeezhu police have taken Christy into custody for questioning. According to preliminary information, the incident took place inside the family home in Vilavoorkal. The mother had reportedly taken the child into a room after lunch, as she routinely did. Other members of the family were elsewhere in the house, while the child’s father and some other family members were reportedly away for work.

The family became concerned when the mother and child did not come out of the room at the usual time. The relatives knocked on the door, following which the mother eventually opened the door and allegedly said that she had killed the child.

Looking for motive

Official sources said the motive for the alleged murder was yet to be established. While initial reports referred to the possibility of domestic disputes as one line of inquiry, the police are also examining whether Christy has any mental ailments.

Tension prevailed at the scene as local residents expressed strong anger and protested against Christy. It required considerable effort from the police team, led by the Malayinkeezhu Station House Officer (SHO), to remove Christy from the scene and take her to the police station.

World.title: Sri Lanka Supreme Court revokes controversial monk’s presidential pardon
World.content:
In a significant case of the judiciary reversing an executive decision, Sri Lanka’s Supreme Court on Thursday (September 10, 2026) overturned a presidential pardon granted to a reactionary Buddhist monk.

In May 2019, then President Maithripala Sirisena pardoned controversial monk Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara ‘Thero’ [as Buddhist priests in Sri Lanka are respectfully referred to], leader of the hardline Bodu Bala Sena (Buddhist Power Force or BBS), who was serving prison term at the time, following conviction for contempt of court and criminal intimidation.

Read The Hindu Profile Galagodaaththe Gnanasara | The divisive monk

Colombo-based non-governmental organisation Centre for Policy Alternatives (CPA) and Sandya Eknaligoda, wife of dissident political cartoonist Prageeth Eknaligoda, forcibly disappeared since 2010, had challenged the pardon. Seven years later, the Supreme Court has ruled that President Sirisena’s action was “arbitrary”, and declared it “null and void”. The ruling assumes significance in the Sinhala Buddhist-majority island nation, where the Buddhist clergy wields considerable religious influence and political power.

Gnanasara Thero rose to prominence in 2012, when he founded the BBS. Widely known for his provocative anti-Muslim remarks and mobilisations, the firebrand monk, now 51, and his organisation became a prominent symbol for a surging anti-Muslim rhetoric in Sri Lanka after the country’s civil war ended in 2009.

In January 2016, Gnanasara Thero stormed the courtroom and openly threatened Ms. Eknaligoda, when a magistrate court was hearing a case of her disappeared husband.

Two years after President Sirisena pardoned the monk, his successor Gotabaya Rajapaksa appointed Gnanasara Thero to a Presidential Task Force to draft proposals on legal reforms, a move widely criticised by rights defenders. In 2024, the Colombo High Court sentenced him to four years’ rigorous imprisonment for fanning hatred against Muslims in a 2016 press conference. He was later granted bail.

World.title: Nearly 90 kg ganja seized in Thiruvananthapuram
World.content:
The Thiruvananthapuram Rural Police have seized 87.59 kg of ganja allegedly transported from Andhra Pradesh to Keralam.

In an operation undertaken as part of the anti-narcotics enforcement drive Operation Toofan, the police nabbed three people under the Aryancode police station limits.

Addressing a press conference here on Thursday (September 10, 2026), Additional Superintendent of Thiruvananthapuram Rural Police J.K. Dinil said the ganja was seized from a Tamil Nadu-registered car during the raid. The police recovered 40 packets, with each packet containing nearly 2.2 kg of ganja.

Two persons, identified as Akhil and Sudheesh, were initially arrested. During detailed interrogation, the police allegedly learned that the consignment had been brought to the district for Joby Jose, a notorious drug peddler based in Thiruvananthapuram. The investigation team subsequently arrested the habitual offender.

According to Mr. Dinil, Jose has been an accused in 13 cases, including several cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.

The investigators suspect that the large consignment was intended for distribution across Thiruvananthapuram and other districts. The police also suspect that the drugs were to be supplied in smaller quantities to various locations, including schools and coastal and other sensitive areas.

World.title: ‘Mandaadi’ movie review: Soori, Suhas power an engaging, smooth-sailing sports actioner
World.content:
Who decides who belongs where? Who decides who gets to do what? These questions have sparked countless uprisings that have also defined many of the laws we now pride ourselves on. The powerful have always dictated how the powerless should live, and that tension has always given rise to heroes who empower the powerless to revolt. But even history won’t tell you the many sporting dreams crushed by the powerful, or the heroes silenced and forced to feel content with their own victories. This is why, whenever socio-politics meets an arena like sports in stories, the results can be truly exhilarating and thought-provoking. We have seen this happen in films like Bison Kaalamaadan and Sarpatta Parambarai, and we see it once again in the latest Soori-starrer, Mandaadi.

This Thursday has seen a unique clash at the Tamil box office — between Sardar 2 and Mandaadi. And a viewer like yours truly, who caught both films back-to-back, would have seen some superbly choreographed fight sequences in a plane, a train, a cable car, and...sailboats. Mandaadi, written and directed by Mathimaran Pugazhendhi, is set in the world of the titular sailboat racing that is popular along the southern coastline of Tamil Nadu. What his guru, Vetri Maaran, did with the traditional game of cockfighting in Aadukalam, Mathimaran attempts to do with Mandaadi.

It’s untapped territory in Tamil cinema, which is why Mathimaran refrains from anything too extraordinary — he takes the template of a socio-political sports drama and bets all-in on pitch-perfect execution. The result speaks for itself; Mandaadi is a clean, crisp, and straightforward film that holds your attention for its 150-minute runtime.

Interestingly, both films released today show what the current generation of filmmakers seems to understand about action-film audiences — modern-day action films need to start high. They don’t waste a second on unnecessary introductions and drop you right into the action. In the coastal town of Mugavaipatnam, Kittaan (Krish Hassan), the young son of a notorious business tycoon and former sailboat racer, Saattappuli (Suhas), is brought in a chariot and introduced to the townsmen as the new captain of the champion boat-racing team, Tsunami Riders.

However, the celebrations end when Maari (Mithun Jai Sankar), a member of a rival team, attempts to hack down Kittaan. As tensions rise, Maari’s father Singaaram (Ravindra Vijay) sends him to Chennai and urges his friend Muthukaali (Soori) to take good care of him. Now, here’s the big secret: Muthukaali isn’t just another ordinary man. Maari’s situation pulls Muthukaali back into the world he ran away from 20 years ago. Who is Muthukaali? What is the feud between him and Saattappuli all about? The sail is strung high, and the course is set. Mandaadi begins its journey with promise.

Mandaadi (Tamil) Director: Mathimaran Pugazhendhi Cast: Soori, Suhas, Sathyaraj, Mahima Nambiar Runtime: 154 minutes Storyline: A former sailboat racer returns to the sport he abandoned when a young racer becomes embroiled in an old feud, forcing him to confront his past and fight to preserve his coastal community’s racing legacy

First and foremost, let me address your biggest expectation in a sports flick like Mandaadi — the sailboat racing scenes stand out as major highlights. The action choreography atop the boats is meticulously planned and executed. The two races featured in the film don’t have a single dull moment. But believe me when I say that Mandaadi isn’t a film you should watch for the sailboat races.

Those who have seen Mathimaran’s previous film Selfie (which is yet to get its due) will know of the writer-director’s penchant for writing drama and intricate plots. Mandaadi shines best when it stays on the many personal, complicated spaces between the characters. Imagine what would go through the mind of a young Maari when he realises that his mother, Angel Rakkamma (Mahima Nambiar), was in a relationship with his mentor, Muthukaali. Or what would a friendship feel like between Muthukaali and the best friend who is now married to his ex-lover?

The most stirring moments in the film are between Muthukaali and Angel, and Muthukaali and his mentor, Machamuni (Sathyaraj). And I am happy to report that all actors in Mandaadi bring their A-game, further amplifying the impact of the writing. Mahima is, without a doubt, the most impressive performer in the cast, and watch how she reacts when the inevitable moment with Muthukaali arrives. Sathyaraj does what Sathyaraj does best. It is about time Tamil cinema saw the performer in Suhas. As Saattappuli, he holds the frames effortlessly and, at times, even comes close to stealing the spotlight from the ever-impressive Soori.

Importantly, Mathimaran’s character depth allows these actors to give their best. For example, the feud between Muthukaali and Saattappuli has layers — which you understand well from their positions. They are both traitors to each other, and hence, for both of them, winning the racing competition is a way to exact revenge. But that’s not all; the stakes in Mandaadi are far higher. Winning the race is the only way Saattappuli can secure the business he had to fight hard to establish. For Muthukaali, it is about protecting his late mentor Machamuni’s beliefs and winning back the honour of their sailboat clan, Mandaadi Vagaiyara.

Machamuni believed that the sailboat races weren’t merely a sport; they were a way of life for a community. He believed a real mandaadi hadto pass the sailboat-racing knowledge to newer generations, as it prepares them for a future when they have to fend for themselves on the ocean without fuel for their engines. Saattappuli’s decision to hire racers from other towns prevents coastal men from learning this craft. This idea lies at the heart of Mandaadi, and Mathimaran’s script fleshes out this emotion with ease.

Mandaadi is another example of how good, earnest writing and filmmaking can deliver a neat, engaging film even with a routine template. And one can now safely say that Soori is serious about the films he has chosen — the sidekick sportsman who gobbled parottas is long gone; this new beast can surf the Tsunami waves (oh, we are back to Aadukalam).

Mandaadi is currently running in theatres

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs3.05, diesel by Rs5.37
World.content:
The government on Thursday increased the price of petrol by Rs3.05 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs5.37 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs370.80 per litre while HSD will cost Rs398.04 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 11 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: IMF mission due on Sept 23 for biannual review of Pakistan’s economic performance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission is due to visit Pakistan on September 23 for a biannual review of the country’s economic performance and implementation of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) for the period ending June 30, 2026.

Pakistan is currently under a $7 billion, 37-month IMF programme , aimed at stabilising the economy through fiscal discipline, structural reforms, and measures to support long-term growth.

Official sources said that during an almost two-week visit ending in the first week of October, the IMF staff mission, led by Iva Petrova, would conduct the fourth review of the EFF and the third review of the RSF.

The mission would begin its visit with technical discussions at the State Bank of Pakistan, followed by meetings with the government’s sectoral teams, alongside a customary inaugural meeting with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.

The engagement would also examine policy implementation at the start of the fiscal year, particularly the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) ability and preparedness to meet its first-ever half-yearly revenue collection structural benchmark under an IMF programme, given the revenue machinery’s repeated large annual shortfalls.

This would also be the first review after the provincial governments surrendered more than Rs1.035 trillion of their National Finance Commission (NFC) shares to the Centre during the current fiscal year for national security and water resources, on top of the Rs1.8tr cash surplus separately committed under IMF pressure.

The programme’s performance against the fiscal targets as of end-June 2026 — the period under review — has mostly been on track, albeit with a major revenue shortfall and slippages in the policy matrix. These include the government’s intervention in commodity operations, particularly wheat and sugar, in violation of an IMF condition requiring the government to keep its hands off the commodities market.

Given the biannual reviews of the $7bn EFF and the $1.4bn RSF, the two sides will have to agree on past performance as well as forward-looking implementation plans.

Upon successful completion of the review, Pakistan will be eligible for the disbursement of about $1bn (760 million Special Drawing Rights) under the EFF and another $200m under the RSF by the end of November or early December.

Official reports suggest that while qualitative performance criteria on the fiscal and monetary sides were mostly on track, progress on economic governance reforms lagged far behind requirements. They suggested that only a couple of targets out of more than three dozen for improving economic governance during the January-June 2026 period had been met.

These targets were set by the prime minister after the IMF’s governance and corruption diagnostic assessment found serious shortcomings in efforts to combat corruption.

While the government had introduced reforms to ensure transparent procurement processes in state-owned entities (SOEs), direct contracting with SOEs without open competitive bidding continued unabated.

There were also reports of agencies issuing tenders after projects had been completed through preferred contractors, compromising competitive pricing and transparency. The rules aimed at ending such preferential treatment have yet to be passed.

Earlier in July, an IMF representative hailed Pakistan’s “strong” economic reforms carried out under the lender’s $7 billion loan programme.

IMF’s Resident Representative for Pakistan Mahir Binici noted that the country’s performance under the 2024 EFF had been “strong so far”, according to a press release issued by the SDPI on its guest lecture in Islamabad.

World.title: Parliament to debate new provinces next month, says minister
World.content:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday that parliament was expected to debate the issue of new provinces next month.

Addressing the corporate sector in late July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had called for the creation of new provinces or administrative units, saying that the current system had “collapsed”.

“There is no National Assembly session this month; however, sessions of both the National Assembly and Senate are expected in October. The discussions will be held whenever the sessions are convened,” the minister said in a video statement.

Chaudhry reiterated that parliament was the “proper forum” for debating the issue of forming new provinces, adding that the debate would definitely be initiated.

“Parliament can hold a debate on any topic — the National Assembly has representation from all four provinces, while the Senate has equal representation from each province. Every decision made here would be taken after consultations with all political parties,” Chaudhry said.

He also expressed hope that a “healthy discussion” would be held on the topic during the upcoming session.

Chaudhry elaborated that the discussion on forming new provinces or federating units was not a debate about “inheriting fortunes”, while advising political parties against taking an emotional stance on the issue.

“I am hopeful that before making a decision on forming new provinces or administrative units in the provinces, we will bring forward Islamabad’s governance model as a formal act.

“While maintaining the federal status of Islamabad, we will form Islamabad’s first legislative assembly,” he stated.

He clarified that Islamabad could not become a province and was not going to be made a separate province. “We are talking about improving its governance model by upholding its federal status.”

The minister said the draft proposing governance changes — including a legislative body with all relevant institutions under the supervision of a chief executive or mayor in Islamabad — had been prepared by a five-member committee appointed by the prime minister.

“It is a very simple model. We did not prepare this draft with any personal contrivance; it was prepared after studying existing governance models in various capitals around the world and their applicable plans,” he added.

Chaudhry maintained that he was in contact with other political parties. “I will sit with them, share the draft and hold consultations, and all the positive recommendations will be incorporated into the draft.”

Islamabad’s bar, chamber of commerce, residents and intellectuals would also be consulted, he added.

In July, Naqvi had proposed a dialogue among all political parties to bring about reforms to the current governance system, while also calling for new provinces and urgent administrative reforms.

His comments had ignited an animated debate across the country, with the PPP referring the question to its top decision-making forum, the Sindh chief minister flatly rejecting it, Lahore’s lawyers terming it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups demanding the minister’s resignation.

Additional reporting by Syed Irfan Raza

World.title: Trump administration proposes waiving grace period for H-1B holders after job loss
World.content:
The Trump administration has proposed eliminating a 60-day grace period that allows certain immigrants, including skilled workers on H-1B visas, to stay in the United States and find a new sponsor after losing their job, according to a government notice posted online on Thursday.

Under the planned rule change, published in the Federal Register by the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), those with H-1B and certain other temporary work visas would have to leave the country as soon as their employment ends — a potential blow to top American tech companies that rely heavily on foreign workers.

It is the latest step by US President Donald Trump to limit legal migration since returning to office in January 2025. His administration has also introduced higher visa fees for skilled workers and recently paused immigrant visa appointments at US missions around the world while it implements a new training programme.

Companies impacted by the change could see some disruption, DHS wrote in its proposal, but it said the jobs could go to American workers instead. In some situations, immigrant workers who leave could potentially reapply if their employer petitions for them, it added.

“DHS presumes that they will either offer the same jobs to equally qualified US workers or go through the I-129 petition process depending on their workforce requirement,” the notice said.

The 60-day grace period, in place since 2017, allows foreign workers time to find another US job or get their affairs in order, whether selling a home or pulling children out of school before leaving the country.

H-1B visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking talent from India and China, allowing them to fill roles where there is sometimes a lack of qualified US workers.

Consultancy companies such as Deloitte, PwC and Ernst and Young, as well as outsourcing giants like Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCL Tech and LTIMindtree, are top H-1B sponsors.

Lawyers for Berardi Immigration Law, which specialises in business-related immigration issues, said the move would “sharply compress the timeline HR teams have to manage layoffs and offboarding for foreign national employees”.

If implemented, the change would also apply to E-1 international trader visa holders; E-2 commercial vehicle operator visa holders; L-1 short-term work for executives or managers with international companies; O-1 visas for people “with an extraordinary ability” in science, sports or the arts; and TN professional workers.

It would also impact H-1B1 skilled worker visa holders from Singapore and Chile and E-3 speciality worker visa holders from Australia.

The rule is subject to a two-month public comment period before it can be enacted into law.

World.title: PM Shehbaz invites NA opposition leader Achakzai for consultation on new CEC
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken a practical step towards initiating dialogue between the government and the opposition by inviting National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai for mandatory consultations on the appointment of a new Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), a source close to the prime minister told Dawn on Thursday.

However, the opposition leader has so far not responded to the prime minister’s invitation.

Interestingly, the invitation was extended days before the PTI-led long march towards Islamabad on Sept 27.

“Yes, the prime minister invited him (Achakzai) for consultation,” the source said.

A few days ago, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq, during an NA session, stressed the need for political harmony and stability and expressed the desire for the prime minister to initiate dialogue with the opposition by, as a first step, inviting the opposition leader for consultations on the appointment of a new CEC.

On the other hand, PTI kept mum on the matter. When a senior party leader was contacted, he was reluctant to comment on the prime minister’s invitation.

The five-year term of incumbent CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja expired on Jan 26, 2025. Raja has remained controversial since the ouster of the PTI government in April 2022 over what the opposition called his “support” for the PML-N-led government.

One of the main allegations levelled against Raja was that he had deprived PTI of its party symbol, the bat, in the 2024 elections.

His critics alleged that the denial of the party symbol was aimed not only at disadvantaging PTI by confusing voters, but also at allowing PTI-backed “independents” to later join the ruling coalition without risking disqualification. They also claimed that the move was intended to deprive PTI of its share of reserved seats.

Section 2A of Article 213 of the Constitution says: “The Prime Minister shall in consultation with the Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly, forward three names for appointment of the Commissioner to a Parliamentary Committee for hearing and confirmation of any one person.”

Section 2B says: “The Parliamentary Committee to be constituted by the Speaker shall comprise fifty per cent members from the Treasury Benches and fifty per cent from the Opposition Parties, based on their strength in Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament), to be nominated by the respective Parliamentary Leaders: Provided that in case there is no consensus between the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, each shall forward separate lists to the Parliamentary Committee for consideration which may confirm any one name.”

“Provided further that the total strength of the Parliamentary Committee shall be twelve members out of which one-third shall be from the Senate, and provided also that when the National Assembly is dissolved and vacancy occurs in the office of the Chief Election Commissioner, the total membership of the Parliamentary Committee shall consist of the members from the Senate only and the foregoing provisions of this clause shall, mutatis mutandis, apply.”

Earlier in August, Achakzai urged the prime minister in a letter to appoint a new chief election commissioner, along with two members representing Sindh and Balochistan.
